# Bureau

Regulatory knowledge base containing codes, review guides, and workflow definitions for site plan analysis. Treats regulatory content like software code — git for version control, PRs for review, Markdown for content.

## Content Standard

All content must conform to the [content spec](./spec/README.md). Key rules:

- Headings follow `[Reference] - [Title]` format (e.g. `## 5.3.1 - Minimum Grades`)
- Cross-references use `§[jurisdiction/code/reference]` syntax
- No YAML frontmatter in content files — metadata goes in `meta/provenance.json`
- Processing artifacts (`raw-extractions/`, `structured-output/`, etc.) belong in `meta/`, not `contents/`
- File names match heading references but aren't used for data extraction

## Key Folders

- `jurisdictions/austin/codes/` — regulatory codes (DCM, LDC, BCM, etc.)
- `jurisdictions/austin/review-guides/` — department review guides (generated by training pipeline)
- `workflows/` — shared, jurisdiction-agnostic workflow definitions (review, review-anchored, train, etc.); Conductor falls back here when no jurisdiction-specific override exists
- `jurisdictions/austin/workflows/` — jurisdiction-specific workflow overrides (e.g. completeness-check, mcr-prep)

## Danger Zones

- NEVER merge PRs without human review — content quality is critical
- NEVER modify existing references — downstream systems depend on them
- NEVER commit processing artifacts to `contents/` — use `meta/` instead

## Architecture

@docs/architecture.md
@docs/training.md

# Agent Instructions

This project uses **bd** (beads) for issue tracking. Run `bd onboard` to get started.

## Quick Reference

```bash
bd ready              # Find available work
bd show <id>          # View issue details
bd update <id> --status in_progress  # Claim work
bd close <id>         # Complete work
bd sync               # Sync with git
```

## Landing the Plane (Session Completion)

**When ending a work session**, you MUST complete ALL steps below. Work is NOT complete until `git push` succeeds.

**MANDATORY WORKFLOW:**

1. **File issues for remaining work** - Create issues for anything that needs follow-up
2. **Run quality gates** (if code changed) - Tests, linters, builds
3. **Update issue status** - Close finished work, update in-progress items
4. **PUSH TO REMOTE** - This is MANDATORY:
   ```bash
   git pull --rebase
   bd sync
   git push
   git status  # MUST show "up to date with origin"
   ```
5. **Clean up** - Clear stashes, prune remote branches
6. **Verify** - All changes committed AND pushed
7. **Hand off** - Provide context for next session

**CRITICAL RULES:**
- Work is NOT complete until `git push` succeeds
- NEVER stop before pushing - that leaves work stranded locally
- NEVER say "ready to push when you are" - YOU must push
- If push fails, resolve and retry until it succeeds

1→# Zoning & Land Use Feasibility — Austin, TX
     2→
     3→## Domain
     4→
     5→Base zoning district, combining districts and overlays (CO, MU, V/VMU, ETOD, NCCD, UNO, WO, CVC, ERC, TODs, HCRC, AO, NBG, DB90), conditional and special use processes, use classification under LDC Chapter 25-2, dimensional standards (height, FAR, building coverage, impervious cover, site area per unit), Compatibility Standards (Article 10), parking, density bonus programs, and site plan procedural path. Excludes site engineering (sde), site form (sduf), environmental layers (el/eptp/fwp/sde), transportation (ta), and wastewater/water (wwp) even where coded in Chapter 25-2 or Subchapter E.
     6→
     7→## Authoritative sources
     8→
     9→- **Land Development Code (LDC), Chapter 25** — Austin Municode. Most-cited chapters: 25-1 (definitions, applications), 25-2 (zoning), 25-5 (site plan), 25-6 (parking and ROW), 25-8 (environmental), 25-13 (airport).
    10→- **Subchapter E (Design Standards & Mixed Use)** — design standards, connectivity, VMU, AEC.
    11→- **Subchapter B, Article 2** — PUD framework.
    12→- **General Site Plan Notes for COA (DSD)** — required notes, signature blocks, forms; modification prohibited.
    13→- **Zoning map (COA GIS, "zoning" layer)** — base district + suffixes. Zoning strings are compound: `GR-MU-CO-NP-DB90` = General Retail + Mixed Use + Conditional Overlay + Neighborhood Plan + DB90 density bonus.
    14→- **Adopted overlays (COA GIS layers)** — CVC, Capitol Dominance, Hill Country Roadway, AO-1/2/3 (Airport), WO subdistricts, NCCD ordinances, TODs (NBG, ERC, Plaza Saltillo, East MLK, Lamar/Justin Lane), UNO, ETOD subdistricts.
    15→- **AMANDA / DSD permit system** — case history, prior approvals, vested rights determinations.
    16→- **Imagine Austin (comp plan) / Future Land Use Map** — *policy, not regulatory.* FLUM does not establish zoning; zoning changes require LDC § 25-2-281 rezoning.
    17→
    18→## Regulatory pathway
    19→
    20→| Path | Trigger | Timeline | Decision body |
    21→|---|---|---|---|
    22→| Administrative site plan approval (Director) | Site plan complies with all title requirements; no commission action required | 6–12 months from intake through release | DSD Director (LDC § 25-5-112) |
    23→| Conditional use permit | Use is "C" in district use table (§ 25-2-491), incl. Large Retail (≥100,000 sf, § 25-2-815), late-hours cocktail lounge, etc. | 4–9 months before site plan can be finalized | Land Use Commission / Planning Commission (LDC § 25-5-142) |
    24→| Rezoning (incl. site-specific Article 10 amendment) | Proposed use prohibited in base district, or modification of Article 10 height/buffer | 6–12 months | P&Z recommendation → City Council |
    25→| BOA variance | Hardship from a dimensional standard (setback, parking, fence) | 3–6 months | Board of Adjustment (LDC §§ 25-2-472, 25-2-474) |
    26→| Density bonus (DDBP, DB90, ETOD, VMU, AU, NBG, Plaza Saltillo, ERC) | Site is eligible per program-specific maps + affordability/community-benefit compliance | Concurrent with site plan (DDBP must be **approved before site plan submittal** per § 25-2-586(H)) | DSD Director (DDBP); NHCD/HPD (others) |
    27→| Alternative Equivalent Compliance (AEC) | Subchapter E deviation; available only for §§ 2.2, 2.3, 2.5, 2.7, 2.8, and Article 3 | 1–4 months | Director (concept plan); expires 3 years from approval |
    28→| F1/F2 staged site plan | DSD administrative practice for large multifamily/mixed-use: F1 = horizontal, F2 = vertical | Two separate case numbers, sequential approvals | DSD (no Planning Commission or phasing fees) |
    29→| Formal § 25-5-21 phased site plan | Single case number with phasing plan; final-phase start >3 years post-approval → Planning Commission | Adds 2–4 months if PC required | DSD Director or Planning Commission |
    30→| Site plan correction / minor revision to released plan | LDC § 25-5-61(C)–(D): no significant effect, ROW relocation, or ADA | 1–3 months | Director (written approval) |
    31→
    32→Site plan approval is valid **3 years from date of approval** (LDC § 25-5-81(B)), extendable by issued building permits or active site work.
    33→
    34→## Constraints to evaluate
    35→
    36→### Use compatibility
    37→
    38→- **Confirm proposed use against base district use table** (§ 25-2-491). Use the **exact LDC name** from Chapters 25-2-3 through 25-2-6 (residential, commercial, industrial, civic). "Office," "Retail," "Restaurant," "School" alone are insufficient.
    39→- **Restaurant (General)** (§ 25-2-4(B)(64)) requires ≥51% gross income from prepared food (§ 25-2-808(B)(1)); below that, the use reclassifies to **Cocktail Lounge** (conditional, LUC approval required).
    40→- **Large Retail** (≥100,000 sf of any single enumerated use including its accessory uses, § 25-2-815) is a conditional use requiring Land Use Commission approval.
    41→- **LR (Neighborhood Commercial) restrictions** (§ 25-2-587): Restaurant (General) ≤4,000 sf, 7 a.m.–11 p.m. hours, no drive-through; General Retail (General) ≤5,000 sf, no local-street access; no outdoor entertainment or amplified sound.
    42→- **Multifamily in CS** requires MU overlay or rezone.
    43→- **W/LO** requires ≥20% of GFA or 1,000 sf (lesser) as office facing the primary street (§ 25-2-584).
    44→- **Civic use chapter** — schools, child care, adult care, community recreation are in § 25-2-6, NOT § 25-2-3 or 25-2-4. Common misclassification.
    45→
    46→### Dimensional envelope (zoning capacity table)
    47→
    48→Building Austin's zoning capacity table requires the **base district from § 25-2-492** *plus* every overlay/combining-district modifier. Selected base district maxima:
    49→
    50→| District | Use list (representative) | Max height | Max FAR | Max IC | Min parking (post-Nov 2023) |
    51→|---|---|---|---|---|---|
    52→| SF-3 / SF-5 / SF-6 | SF, duplex (SF-3+), 2/3-unit (SF-3+) | 35 ft | none | 40% / 45% / 50% (varies) | None citywide |
    53→| MF-1 / MF-2 / MF-3 / MF-4 / MF-5 / MF-6 | Multifamily, condo, townhouse, group residential | 40 / 40 (3 stry) / 40 / 60 / 60 / 90 ft | none / none / 0.75:1 / 0.75:1 / 1:1 / none | 45–70% | None citywide |
    54→| NO / LO / GO | Office sub-tiers | 35 / 40 (3 stry) / 60 ft | 0.35 / 0.7 / 1:1 | 50 / 70 / 80% | None citywide |
    55→| LR | Neighborhood commercial (capped uses) | 40 ft (3 stry) | 0.5:1 | 80% | None citywide |
    56→| GR | General commercial | 60 ft | 1:1 | 90% | None citywide |
    57→| CS / CS-1 | Commercial services | 60 ft | 2:1 | 95% | None citywide |
    58→| CH | Commercial highway | 60 ft (per § 25-2-582) | 3:1 | 95% | None citywide |
    59→| DMU | Downtown mixed use | 120 ft (8:1 with DDBP) | 5:1 | 100% | None citywide |
    60→| CBD | Central business district | 350 ft | 8:1 | 100% | None citywide |
    61→| IP / LI / MI / R&D | Industrial sub-tiers | 60 / 60 / 120 / 60 ft | 1:1 | 80% | None citywide |
    62→| LA | Lake Austin | 35 ft | none | per § 25-2-551 | None citywide |
    63→
    64→**Citywide parking minimums were eliminated November 13, 2023** by Ord. No. 20231102-028 (LDC § 25-6-471(A)). Exceptions: (1) PUDs with parking exhibits in their ordinance (e.g., Goodnight Ranch Exhibit J) continue to control; (2) UNO sets a 60% **maximum ceiling** (not minimum) on Appendix A; (3) accessibility (ADA) spaces still required. The repeal also abolished the "Type CT" plan designation and the mandatory shower-facility requirement under § 25-6-478(D)(1).
    65→
    66→**Where IC, FAR, height, and coverage are calculated:**
    67→
    68→- **FAR = GFA ÷ Gross Site Area** (§§ 25-1-21(43), (48)). GSA is the full unmodified site area — no deductions for floodplain, CWQZ, slopes, or environmental overlays.
    69→- **GFA** (§ 25-1-21(47)) includes loading docks, excludes atria airspace, parking, driveways, enclosed loading berths. The bulk-purpose GFA differs from parking-calculation GFA (which additionally excludes bike rooms and showers per § 25-6-472(C)) — don't conflate.
    70→- **Building coverage** (§ 25-1-21(14)) excludes ground-level paving, eaves, balconies. Building coverage and IC are distinct and cannot be equal where any paving exists outside buildings.

# Zoning & Land Use Feasibility — Austin, TX

## Domain

Base zoning district, combining districts and overlays (CO, MU, V/VMU, ETOD, NCCD, UNO, WO, CVC, ERC, TODs, HCRC, AO, NBG, DB90), conditional and special use processes, use classification under LDC Chapter 25-2, dimensional standards (height, FAR, building coverage, impervious cover, site area per unit), Compatibility Standards (Article 10), parking, density bonus programs, and site plan procedural path. Excludes site engineering (sde), site form (sduf), environmental layers (el/eptp/fwp/sde), transportation (ta), and wastewater/water (wwp) even where coded in Chapter 25-2 or Subchapter E.

## Authoritative sources

- **Land Development Code (LDC), Chapter 25** — Austin Municode. Most-cited chapters: 25-1 (definitions, applications), 25-2 (zoning), 25-5 (site plan), 25-6 (parking and ROW), 25-8 (environmental), 25-13 (airport).
- **Subchapter E (Design Standards & Mixed Use)** — design standards, connectivity, VMU, AEC.
- **Subchapter B, Article 2** — PUD framework.
- **General Site Plan Notes for COA (DSD)** — required notes, signature blocks, forms; modification prohibited.
- **Zoning map (COA GIS, "zoning" layer)** — base district + suffixes. Zoning strings are compound: `GR-MU-CO-NP-DB90` = General Retail + Mixed Use + Conditional Overlay + Neighborhood Plan + DB90 density bonus.
- **Adopted overlays (COA GIS layers)** — CVC, Capitol Dominance, Hill Country Roadway, AO-1/2/3 (Airport), WO subdistricts, NCCD ordinances, TODs (NBG, ERC, Plaza Saltillo, East MLK, Lamar/Justin Lane), UNO, ETOD subdistricts.
- **AMANDA / DSD permit system** — case history, prior approvals, vested rights determinations.
- **Imagine Austin (comp plan) / Future Land Use Map** — *policy, not regulatory.* FLUM does not establish zoning; zoning changes require LDC § 25-2-281 rezoning.

## Regulatory pathway

| Path | Trigger | Timeline | Decision body |
|---|---|---|---|
| Administrative site plan approval (Director) | Site plan complies with all title requirements; no commission action required | 6–12 months from intake through release | DSD Director (LDC § 25-5-112) |
| Conditional use permit | Use is "C" in district use table (§ 25-2-491), incl. Large Retail (≥100,000 sf, § 25-2-815), late-hours cocktail lounge, etc. | 4–9 months before site plan can be finalized | Land Use Commission / Planning Commission (LDC § 25-5-142) |
| Rezoning (incl. site-specific Article 10 amendment) | Proposed use prohibited in base district, or modification of Article 10 height/buffer | 6–12 months | P&Z recommendation → City Council |
| BOA variance | Hardship from a dimensional standard (setback, parking, fence) | 3–6 months | Board of Adjustment (LDC §§ 25-2-472, 25-2-474) |
| Density bonus (DDBP, DB90, ETOD, VMU, AU, NBG, Plaza Saltillo, ERC) | Site is eligible per program-specific maps + affordability/community-benefit compliance | Concurrent with site plan (DDBP must be **approved before site plan submittal** per § 25-2-586(H)) | DSD Director (DDBP); NHCD/HPD (others) |
| Alternative Equivalent Compliance (AEC) | Subchapter E deviation; available only for §§ 2.2, 2.3, 2.5, 2.7, 2.8, and Article 3 | 1–4 months | Director (concept plan); expires 3 years from approval |
| F1/F2 staged site plan | DSD administrative practice for large multifamily/mixed-use: F1 = horizontal, F2 = vertical | Two separate case numbers, sequential approvals | DSD (no Planning Commission or phasing fees) |
| Formal § 25-5-21 phased site plan | Single case number with phasing plan; final-phase start >3 years post-approval → Planning Commission | Adds 2–4 months if PC required | DSD Director or Planning Commission |
| Site plan correction / minor revision to released plan | LDC § 25-5-61(C)–(D): no significant effect, ROW relocation, or ADA | 1–3 months | Director (written approval) |

Site plan approval is valid **3 years from date of approval** (LDC § 25-5-81(B)), extendable by issued building permits or active site work.

## Constraints to evaluate

### Use compatibility

- **Confirm proposed use against base district use table** (§ 25-2-491). Use the **exact LDC name** from Chapters 25-2-3 through 25-2-6 (residential, commercial, industrial, civic). "Office," "Retail," "Restaurant," "School" alone are insufficient.
- **Restaurant (General)** (§ 25-2-4(B)(64)) requires ≥51% gross income from prepared food (§ 25-2-808(B)(1)); below that, the use reclassifies to **Cocktail Lounge** (conditional, LUC approval required).
- **Large Retail** (≥100,000 sf of any single enumerated use including its accessory uses, § 25-2-815) is a conditional use requiring Land Use Commission approval.
- **LR (Neighborhood Commercial) restrictions** (§ 25-2-587): Restaurant (General) ≤4,000 sf, 7 a.m.–11 p.m. hours, no drive-through; General Retail (General) ≤5,000 sf, no local-street access; no outdoor entertainment or amplified sound.
- **Multifamily in CS** requires MU overlay or rezone.
- **W/LO** requires ≥20% of GFA or 1,000 sf (lesser) as office facing the primary street (§ 25-2-584).
- **Civic use chapter** — schools, child care, adult care, community recreation are in § 25-2-6, NOT § 25-2-3 or 25-2-4. Common misclassification.

### Dimensional envelope (zoning capacity table)

Building Austin's zoning capacity table requires the **base district from § 25-2-492** *plus* every overlay/combining-district modifier. Selected base district maxima:

| District | Use list (representative) | Max height | Max FAR | Max IC | Min parking (post-Nov 2023) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SF-3 / SF-5 / SF-6 | SF, duplex (SF-3+), 2/3-unit (SF-3+) | 35 ft | none | 40% / 45% / 50% (varies) | None citywide |
| MF-1 / MF-2 / MF-3 / MF-4 / MF-5 / MF-6 | Multifamily, condo, townhouse, group residential | 40 / 40 (3 stry) / 40 / 60 / 60 / 90 ft | none / none / 0.75:1 / 0.75:1 / 1:1 / none | 45–70% | None citywide |
| NO / LO / GO | Office sub-tiers | 35 / 40 (3 stry) / 60 ft | 0.35 / 0.7 / 1:1 | 50 / 70 / 80% | None citywide |
| LR | Neighborhood commercial (capped uses) | 40 ft (3 stry) | 0.5:1 | 80% | None citywide |
| GR | General commercial | 60 ft | 1:1 | 90% | None citywide |
| CS / CS-1 | Commercial services | 60 ft | 2:1 | 95% | None citywide |
| CH | Commercial highway | 60 ft (per § 25-2-582) | 3:1 | 95% | None citywide |
| DMU | Downtown mixed use | 120 ft (8:1 with DDBP) | 5:1 | 100% | None citywide |
| CBD | Central business district | 350 ft | 8:1 | 100% | None citywide |
| IP / LI / MI / R&D | Industrial sub-tiers | 60 / 60 / 120 / 60 ft | 1:1 | 80% | None citywide |
| LA | Lake Austin | 35 ft | none | per § 25-2-551 | None citywide |

**Citywide parking minimums were eliminated November 13, 2023** by Ord. No. 20231102-028 (LDC § 25-6-471(A)). Exceptions: (1) PUDs with parking exhibits in their ordinance (e.g., Goodnight Ranch Exhibit J) continue to control; (2) UNO sets a 60% **maximum ceiling** (not minimum) on Appendix A; (3) accessibility (ADA) spaces still required. The repeal also abolished the "Type CT" plan designation and the mandatory shower-facility requirement under § 25-6-478(D)(1).

**Where IC, FAR, height, and coverage are calculated:**

- **FAR = GFA ÷ Gross Site Area** (§§ 25-1-21(43), (48)). GSA is the full unmodified site area — no deductions for floodplain, CWQZ, slopes, or environmental overlays.
- **GFA** (§ 25-1-21(47)) includes loading docks, excludes atria airspace, parking, driveways, enclosed loading berths. The bulk-purpose GFA differs from parking-calculation GFA (which additionally excludes bike rooms and showers per § 25-6-472(C)) — don't conflate.
- **Building coverage** (§ 25-1-21(14)) excludes ground-level paving, eaves, balconies. Building coverage and IC are distinct and cannot be equal where any paving exists outside buildings.
- **Building height** (§ 25-1-21(50)) is measured from the **average of highest and lowest grades adjacent to the building** (AAG) to a roof-type-specific reference point (top of coping for flat; deck line for mansard; average of highest gable for pitched/hip). Measuring from lowest grade alone is a common error that maximizes apparent allowable height.
- **§ 25-2-531 rooftop height exception** allows parapets, mechanicals, stairs/elevator overruns, ornamental structures to exceed by the greater of 15% of permitted height, federal/state compliance amount, engineering standard (stacks), or 30% (spires). **Inapplicable within Capitol View Corridors.**
- **2-foot projection exemption** (§ 25-8-63(C)(13)) does **not** apply to site plan IC — only to residential building permits (ECM § 1.8.1(C)).

### Overlays and combining districts

Each one materially modifies what's allowed and must be identified before applying any single standard.

- **Conditional Overlay (CO)** — site-specific use prohibitions, trip caps, height/coverage restrictions in the adopting ordinance; supersedes base-district table where stricter. Pull ordinance from AMANDA.
- **Mixed Use (MU)** — adds multifamily to a commercial base district; sets per-unit site area thresholds (Subch. E § 4.2.1(D)(6)) ranging from 800 sf/unit (GO-MU, GR-MU, CS-MU efficiency) to 4,400 sf (NO-MU 2BR+).
- **VMU / V** — Vertical Mixed Use. Commercial sites on a Core Transit Corridor or Future CTC. VMU buildings need at least one residential floor + ≥75% pedestrian-oriented commercial frontage (§ 4.3.3.B–C). Dimensional exemptions cover site area, FAR, coverage, setbacks — **not height**. 60% parking reduction (§ 4.3.3.E.3) requires affordability per § 4.3.3.F (5%+5% owner at ≤80%/≤100% AMI, 99-yr; or 10% rental at ≤80% AMI, 40-yr) and cannot stack with any other parking reduction.
- **ETOD (Equitable Transit-Oriented Development), § 25-2-182 + DBETOD** — combining district for sites near transit corridors. Subdistrict 1 (station-adjacent) allows greater height than Subdistrict 2 (60/90/120 ft tier depending on combined zoning). Identified by "ETOD" suffix or `etod-subdistricts` GIS layer.
- **DB90 (Density Bonus 90)** — bonus combining district on CS-1, CS, GR, LR, GO, or LO; +30 ft height to cap of 90 ft, plus FAR/coverage/setback exemptions in exchange for affordability (12% rental ≤60% MFI or 10% ≤50% MFI; 12% ownership ≤80% MFI). Amended late 2024 by Ord. 20240229-073 and 20240829-158.
- **UNO (University Neighborhood Overlay)** — west of UT campus. Affordability required (§ 25-2-765): 10% units at ≤60% AMFI **and** 10% at ≤50% AMFI (conjunctive — total 20%, 40-yr). Parking: 60% of Appendix A is the **maximum**.
- **NCCD (Neighborhood Conservation Combining District)** — identified by "NCCD" suffix; each NCCD has its own adopting ordinance with bespoke use/dimensional restrictions and may include pedestrian-oriented use requirements (LDC § 25-2-691(C) closed list). Each NCCD's adopting ordinance must be obtained — they are not in Bureau's code library.
- **CVC (Capitol View Corridor), § 25-2-642** — 26 named corridors. Max height = lesser of base district maximum and CVC plane elevation (in feet above mean sea level). Plans must use AMSL, not "feet from grade." A sealed CVC documentation package from a Registered Professional Surveyor or Engineer + City Height Determination Letter required. **§ 25-2-531 exceptions do NOT apply.**
- **Capitol Dominance (CD), § 25-2-641** — separate from CVC. Within ¼-mile of Capitol dome center (653 ft AMSL). Max elevation = 653 + (0.04366 × horizontal distance) ft AMSL.
- **Hill Country Roadway Corridor (HCRC), §§ 25-2-1102–1126** — within 1,000 ft of ROW of Loop 360 (US 290W–US 183), RM 620 (SH 71–Anderson Mill), RM 2222 (Highland Hills–RM 620), RM 2244 (Loop 360–SH 71), or Southwest Parkway. Exception: sites within 1,000 ft of US 183 or US 290W only are excluded. Requires ≥40% natural area (§ 25-2-1025), slope-based FAR caps in Moderate Intensity Zones (§ 25-2-1122), Hill Country building materials, ≤20% mirrored glass reflectance.
- **Airport Overlay (AO-1/2/3), Chapter 25-13** — concentric noise contours around ABIA. Restricts use, requires Aviation Department signature, height limits per § 25-13-22 imaginary surfaces.
- **Waterfront Overlay (WO), §§ 25-2-721–746** — 16 subdistricts along Lady Bird Lake (Town Lake) and the Colorado River. PARD Director review required. Shoreline setbacks vary by subdistrict (e.g., Rainey 150 ft from Town Lake, North Shore Central 100 ft, South Lakeshore 65 ft). North Shore Central and South Shore Central impose 70-degree angle-plane envelopes; Lamar uses straight caps. Primary setback area = no parking; secondary setback area = ≤30% IC.
- **TOD Regulating Plans** — NBG, ERC, Plaza Saltillo, East MLK, Lamar/Justin Lane. Each supersedes base LDC and Subchapter E within its boundary. ERC uses 5 subdistricts (CMU, IMU, NMU, UR, NR) with subdistrict-specific dimensional and use rules + a development bonus program (PAOS required).
- **PUDs (Subch. B Art. 2)** — Council-adopted ordinance + Land Use Plan supersede the LDC tables for that property. Tier One requirements include ≥10/15/20% open space (residential/industrial/non-residential), ≥2-star Austin Energy Green Building, and **affirmative Subchapter E compliance for commercial/retail/mixed-use PUDs (§ 2.3.2(A))**. PUD-specific parking exhibits survive the citywide parking elimination.

### Compatibility Standards (Article 10) — repealed and replaced July 15, 2024

> **Critical 2024 change.** The former Article 10 used a four-tier framework at 50/100/300/540 ft with a "compatibility waiver" mechanism (former §§ 25-2-1081/1082). The Ord. No. 20240516-004 replacement effective July 15, 2024 uses only **two distance thresholds (50 ft and 75 ft)**. Plans citing the old distance bands, the waiver mechanism, or §§ 25-2-1064/1066/1067 are relying on repealed authority. Plans submitted before July 15, 2024 may retain Chapter 245 vesting to prior standards.

**Applicability (§ 25-2-1051):** Site is (1) zoned MF-4 or less restrictive (MF-4, MF-5, MF-6, any commercial/industrial) AND (2) within 75 ft of a **triggering property** = 1–3 dwelling units zoned SF-5 or more restrictive (LA, RR, SF-1, SF-2, SF-3, SF-4A, SF-4B, SF-5 only — SF-6 does NOT qualify; vacant lots do NOT qualify).

**Exceptions (§ 25-2-1052):** CBD/DMU sites; structural alteration without size/height increase; sites used exclusively for duplex, SF attached, SF residential, small-lot SF, two-unit, three-unit, adult care, or child care.

1→# Site Development / Use / Form Feasibility — Austin, TX
     2→
     3→## Domain
     4→
     5→The bridge between zoning (`zlu`) and engineering (`sde`). Covers (1) whether the project triggers a site plan under LDC Chapter 25-5 and which procedural path (administrative vs. commission vs. Site Plan Lite); (2) site-and-building form requirements under LDC Subchapter E and any superseding regulating plan (NBG, ERC, Plaza Saltillo, East MLK, Lamar/Justin Lane TOD, Waller Creek District, Downtown Austin Plan, Airport Boulevard Corridor); (3) frontage build-to, entrance orientation, transparency/glazing, articulation, screening, and streetscape (clear/planting/supplemental zones); (4) overlay-driven design review (Waterfront Overlay, UNO, Downtown Creeks, DDBP/Design Commission).
     6→
     7→Boundary with neighbors: zoning entitlement (FAR, height, base use) lives in `zlu`; civil/engineering envelope (drainage, water/wastewater, ESC) lives in `sde`; this guide covers the urban-form contract the project signs at site plan.
     8→
     9→## Authoritative sources
    10→
    11→- LDC Chapter 25-5 — Site plan procedures, classifications, exemptions
    12→- LDC Chapter 25-2, Subchapter E — Design Standards and Mixed Use (Article 1 applicability; Article 2 site; Article 3 building; Article 4 VMU; Article 5 CTC definitions)
    13→- LDC § 25-2-721 et seq. — Waterfront Overlay general + 16 subdistricts (§ 25-2-738 North Shore Central; § 25-2-739 Rainey; § 25-2-733 Butler Shores)
    14→- LDC § 25-2-586 — Downtown Density Bonus Program (DDBP)
    15→- LDC § 25-2-167, § 25-2-643 — Downtown Creeks Combining District
    16→- LDC § 25-2-753 et seq. + BCM 12.1 — University Neighborhood Overlay (UNO)
    17→- ERC Regulating Plan (LDC § 25-2-149) — Articles 1–6
    18→- NBG, Plaza Saltillo TOD, East MLK TOD, Lamar/Justin Lane TOD Regulating Plans
    19→- Waller Creek District Design Guidelines
    20→- Great Streets Master Plan (downtown program)
    21→- City of Austin Standard Details — street furniture, sidewalk, dumpster enclosure
    22→
    23→## Regulatory pathway
    24→
    25→| Procedural path | Trigger | Decision body | Typical timeline |
    26→|---|---|---|---|
    27→| Building permit only — no site plan | Single-family / duplex on existing platted lot; interior remodel; ADA sidewalk projects; specific § 25-5 exemptions | DSD plan review | 4–8 wk |
    28→| **Site Plan Lite** (single-family, two-family, small commercial) | Eligible small projects under § 25-5; specific use list and size caps | Administrative (DSD) | 8–12 wk |
    29→| **Administrative site plan** (standard) | Default for most commercial / mixed-use / multifamily not requiring waivers | DSD staff | 6–9 mo from intake to release; 3+ rounds of comments common |
    30→| **Commission site plan** | Variances from § 25-5 standards; certain conditional uses; some overlays | Land Use Commission / Planning Commission | 9–14 mo; public hearing required |
    31→| **Design Commission / DDBP review** | Downtown DDBP bonus projects; certain Great Streets sites | Design Commission (advisory) + DDBP gatekeeper | Add 2–4 mo *before* site plan submittal |
    32→| **Waterfront Planning Advisory Board** | Any site plan in a WO subdistrict | Director requests recommendation per § 25-5-143(C) | Add 1–2 mo |
    33→| **PARD director sign-off** | Required for every site plan in WO | PARD director (§ 25-2-721(A)(2)) | Concurrent with admin site plan |
    34→| **AEC (Alternative Equivalent Compliance)** | Numeric Subchapter E deviation beyond Minor Modification scope; only for §§ 2.2, 2.3, 2.5, 2.7, 2.8, Article 3 | Director-approved concept plan | Concept plan due ≥ 10 days before pre-app; expires 3 yr (one 1-yr extension) |
    35→
    36→Site plan is the **envelope contract**; building permit follows and inherits the approved site plan's site form. Don't confuse the two — building permit alone cannot fix a site-plan-level form non-compliance.
    37→
    38→## Constraints to evaluate
    39→
    40→### Site plan trigger and path
    41→
    42→- **Verify site plan is required at all**. Pure interior remodel and certain minor projects are permit-only under § 25-5 exemptions. For everything commercial/multifamily/MU expect a site plan.
    43→- **Site Plan Lite eligibility** is restrictive and tied to a specific use list and size caps — don't assume eligibility from project narrative; confirm against the current § 25-5 Lite list before factoring the shorter timeline.
    44→- **Commission-level escalation** is triggered by waivers from § 25-5 standards (e.g., compatibility, parking, access). Identify the waivers needed at concept stage — every commission item adds 3–6 months and public-hearing risk.
    45→
    46→### Subchapter E applicability and compliance tier (LDC Subchapter E, § 1.2)
    47→
    48→- Subchapter E applies if (a) project requires a site plan under Chapter 25-5, (b) site is **not** in a categorically exempt regulating plan area, and (c) the specific standard is triggered by the project's principal street type per Table A.
    49→- **Categorically exempt regulating plans** (§ 1.2.4.A.12): NBG, ERC, Plaza Saltillo TOD, East MLK TOD, Lamar/Justin Lane TOD, Waller Creek District, Downtown Austin Plan, Airport Boulevard Corridor Plan. These plans *each impose their own* form standards — exemption from Subchapter E ≠ exemption from form rules.
    50→- **Other carve-outs:** AG, AV, TN zoning, UNO (§ 1.2.4.A.2–3); industrial uses *only when not on a CTC* (§ 1.2.4.A.6); warehouse with <25% non-industrial GFA *only when not on a CTC* (§ 1.2.4.A.9). PUD supersedes Subchapter E only to the extent of conflict (§ 1.2.5.B.2.g) — PUD silence ≠ exemption.
    51→- **Compliance tier:** Full Compliance (§ 1.2.2) for new construction on undeveloped land or full-demo redevelopment; Partial Compliance (§ 1.2.3) for additions / Level 3 remodels >50% work-area where principal-street façade is remodeled. # Site Development / Use / Form Feasibility — Austin, TX

## Domain

The bridge between zoning (`zlu`) and engineering (`sde`). Covers (1) whether the project triggers a site plan under LDC Chapter 25-5 and which procedural path (administrative vs. commission vs. Site Plan Lite); (2) site-and-building form requirements under LDC Subchapter E and any superseding regulating plan (NBG, ERC, Plaza Saltillo, East MLK, Lamar/Justin Lane TOD, Waller Creek District, Downtown Austin Plan, Airport Boulevard Corridor); (3) frontage build-to, entrance orientation, transparency/glazing, articulation, screening, and streetscape (clear/planting/supplemental zones); (4) overlay-driven design review (Waterfront Overlay, UNO, Downtown Creeks, DDBP/Design Commission).

Boundary with neighbors: zoning entitlement (FAR, height, base use) lives in `zlu`; civil/engineering envelope (drainage, water/wastewater, ESC) lives in `sde`; this guide covers the urban-form contract the project signs at site plan.

## Authoritative sources

- LDC Chapter 25-5 — Site plan procedures, classifications, exemptions
- LDC Chapter 25-2, Subchapter E — Design Standards and Mixed Use (Article 1 applicability; Article 2 site; Article 3 building; Article 4 VMU; Article 5 CTC definitions)
- LDC § 25-2-721 et seq. — Waterfront Overlay general + 16 subdistricts (§ 25-2-738 North Shore Central; § 25-2-739 Rainey; § 25-2-733 Butler Shores)
- LDC § 25-2-586 — Downtown Density Bonus Program (DDBP)
- LDC § 25-2-167, § 25-2-643 — Downtown Creeks Combining District
- LDC § 25-2-753 et seq. + BCM 12.1 — University Neighborhood Overlay (UNO)
- ERC Regulating Plan (LDC § 25-2-149) — Articles 1–6
- NBG, Plaza Saltillo TOD, East MLK TOD, Lamar/Justin Lane TOD Regulating Plans
- Waller Creek District Design Guidelines
- Great Streets Master Plan (downtown program)
- City of Austin Standard Details — street furniture, sidewalk, dumpster enclosure

## Regulatory pathway

| Procedural path | Trigger | Decision body | Typical timeline |
|---|---|---|---|
| Building permit only — no site plan | Single-family / duplex on existing platted lot; interior remodel; ADA sidewalk projects; specific § 25-5 exemptions | DSD plan review | 4–8 wk |
| **Site Plan Lite** (single-family, two-family, small commercial) | Eligible small projects under § 25-5; specific use list and size caps | Administrative (DSD) | 8–12 wk |
| **Administrative site plan** (standard) | Default for most commercial / mixed-use / multifamily not requiring waivers | DSD staff | 6–9 mo from intake to release; 3+ rounds of comments common |
| **Commission site plan** | Variances from § 25-5 standards; certain conditional uses; some overlays | Land Use Commission / Planning Commission | 9–14 mo; public hearing required |
| **Design Commission / DDBP review** | Downtown DDBP bonus projects; certain Great Streets sites | Design Commission (advisory) + DDBP gatekeeper | Add 2–4 mo *before* site plan submittal |
| **Waterfront Planning Advisory Board** | Any site plan in a WO subdistrict | Director requests recommendation per § 25-5-143(C) | Add 1–2 mo |
| **PARD director sign-off** | Required for every site plan in WO | PARD director (§ 25-2-721(A)(2)) | Concurrent with admin site plan |
| **AEC (Alternative Equivalent Compliance)** | Numeric Subchapter E deviation beyond Minor Modification scope; only for §§ 2.2, 2.3, 2.5, 2.7, 2.8, Article 3 | Director-approved concept plan | Concept plan due ≥ 10 days before pre-app; expires 3 yr (one 1-yr extension) |

Site plan is the **envelope contract**; building permit follows and inherits the approved site plan's site form. Don't confuse the two — building permit alone cannot fix a site-plan-level form non-compliance.

## Constraints to evaluate

### Site plan trigger and path

- **Verify site plan is required at all**. Pure interior remodel and certain minor projects are permit-only under § 25-5 exemptions. For everything commercial/multifamily/MU expect a site plan.
- **Site Plan Lite eligibility** is restrictive and tied to a specific use list and size caps — don't assume eligibility from project narrative; confirm against the current § 25-5 Lite list before factoring the shorter timeline.
- **Commission-level escalation** is triggered by waivers from § 25-5 standards (e.g., compatibility, parking, access). Identify the waivers needed at concept stage — every commission item adds 3–6 months and public-hearing risk.

### Subchapter E applicability and compliance tier (LDC Subchapter E, § 1.2)

- Subchapter E applies if (a) project requires a site plan under Chapter 25-5, (b) site is **not** in a categorically exempt regulating plan area, and (c) the specific standard is triggered by the project's principal street type per Table A.
- **Categorically exempt regulating plans** (§ 1.2.4.A.12): NBG, ERC, Plaza Saltillo TOD, East MLK TOD, Lamar/Justin Lane TOD, Waller Creek District, Downtown Austin Plan, Airport Boulevard Corridor Plan. These plans *each impose their own* form standards — exemption from Subchapter E ≠ exemption from form rules.
- **Other carve-outs:** AG, AV, TN zoning, UNO (§ 1.2.4.A.2–3); industrial uses *only when not on a CTC* (§ 1.2.4.A.6); warehouse with <25% non-industrial GFA *only when not on a CTC* (§ 1.2.4.A.9). PUD supersedes Subchapter E only to the extent of conflict (§ 1.2.5.B.2.g) — PUD silence ≠ exemption.
- **Compliance tier:** Full Compliance (§ 1.2.2) for new construction on undeveloped land or full-demo redevelopment; Partial Compliance (§ 1.2.3) for additions / Level 3 remodels >50% work-area where principal-street façade is remodeled. Partial Compliance allows existing-condition waivers; document on cover sheet.

### Principal street hierarchy (Subchapter E § 2.1)

Principal street priority: **CTC > Internal Circulation Route > Urban Roadway > Suburban Roadway > Highway/Hill Country Roadway**. Determines build-to %, glazing %, entrance orientation, and parking-placement restrictions. **Sidewalk and supplemental zone standards apply to all abutting frontages** independently (§ 2.2.1.B), each governed by its own roadway type.

- 20 enumerated CTC segments; CTC is defined by name **and** segment limits — confirm the parcel falls within stated geographic endpoints, not just on the named street.
- Sites with frontage on multiple equal-class streets: Director designates principal based on transit service; if equal/absent, owner designates.

### Build-to / frontage occupation

Net Frontage Length (NFL) = lot line minus ICR ROW, compatibility setbacks, easements, drive aisles, sidewalks, and stairs at building perimeter. Parking structures, canopies, accessory structures **do not count** toward build-to.

| Frontage type | Build-to (min % of NFL) | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Subchapter E CTC | 75% | Subchapter E § 2.2.2 |
| Subchapter E Urban Roadway | 40% | Subchapter E § 2.2.3 |
| NBG / ERC Active Edge | 100% | NBG 5.8 / ERC 5.6 |
| NBG / ERC CTC (basic) | 75% | NBG 4.3.3 / ERC 4.3.3 |
| NBG / ERC Pedestrian Priority Collector | 75% | NBG 4.3.3 / ERC 4.3.3 |
| NBG / ERC Urban Roadway (basic) | 50% | NBG 4.3.3 / ERC 4.3.3 |
| TOD CTC (Plaza Saltillo / East MLK) | 75% | TOD plan 4.3.3 |
| TOD Pedestrian Priority Street | 50% | TOD plan 4.3.3 |
| TOD Local Street | 40% | TOD plan 4.3.3 |

No 80% tier exists in current ERC/NBG/TOD plans — outdated references should be treated with suspicion.

### Building entrance (Subchapter E § 2.4)

- ≥1 customer entrance must face the principal street and connect directly to the clear or supplemental zone via an unobstructed exterior path.
- Each separate ground-floor commercial tenant along the principal-street elevation needs its own entrance.
- Advisory 75-ft entrance interval (§ 2.4.B.2): exceeding triggers long-wall pedestrian treatment (shade, glazing, articulation, awnings) — not a hard violation but is a real cost.
- Non-street-facing entrance exception (§ 2.4.B.1(a)–(d)) requires **all four** conditions: ≥80% NFL built to clear/supplemental zone; continuous shaded sidewalk principal-street→entrance; entrance within 100 ft of street-facing façade line; shade trees ≤30 ft o.c. between building and any parking.
- **AEC is not available for § 2.4 entry requirements** (§ 1.5.2). Plan the entrance correctly at concept; you cannot buy a deviation later.

### Sidewalk: clear / planting / supplemental zones (Subchapter E § 2.2)

- Three-zone system: planting (curb-adjacent, trees + utilities) → clear (unobstructed pedestrian travel) → optional supplemental (active uses adjacent to building face).
- Widths vary by principal street class; dimensions must be labeled on site + landscape plan, at narrowest point where variable.
- Build-to can be satisfied at edge of properly designated supplemental zone rather than clear zone.
- Great Streets program participation exempts downtown sites (bounded by MLK, Lady Bird Lake, IH-35, Lamar) from CTC/Urban Roadway sidewalk + supplemental zone standards per § 2.2.2.B and § 2.2.3.B — but Great Streets has its own (typically richer) streetscape spec.

### Ground-floor transparency / glazing (Subchapter E § 3.2)

| Condition | Min glazing | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Principal street, 2–10 ft above grade (non-residential, Sub. E) | 40% | § 3.2.2.A.1 |
| Other street-facing façades, 2–10 ft | 25% | § 3.2.2.C |
| Principal street, 10–30 ft above entry level | 25% | § 3.2.2.A.2 |
| Principal-street ground-floor glazing — share with VT ≥ 0.6 | ≥ 50% | § 3.2.2.E |

    50→## Persisting Your Work

    53→
    54→### save_finding

    56→Call `save_finding` after evaluating a tool's output and deciding the result is relevant. Each finding captures one coherent piece of research data.
    57→
    58→**When to call it:**

    60→- After a GIS property profile returns layer results — save findings for each major data category (zoning, flood, overlays, environmental, transportation, easements, drainage infrastructure, parkland). One finding per category, not one finding per layer.
    61→- After a FEMA flood zone lookup — save a finding with zone designation, FIRM panel, floodway status, and base flood elevation.
    62→- After transcribing a county clerk document and determining it contains relevant provisions — save a finding with key provisions in `key_information`, the full Gemini transcription in `full_content`, and the PDF path in `file_path`.

    70→- Ordinance numbers: "Ord. No. 20190201-034, effective March 1, 2019"

    79→- Tool errors or failed lookups. Document these in a note.
    80→- Preliminary search results you haven't evaluated yet.

Discarding the 12 assumed-name filings from county clerk search — all are DBA registrations unrelated to property encumbrances."

Re-searching with prior owners from deed history: MARTINEZ ELENA (2015-2019), DAVIS PROPERTIES LLC (2008-2015)."
    94→
    95→**Target: 10+ notes per session.** Notes are cheap — when in doubt, write one.

- County clerk searches used multiple strategies — search ALL prior owners (not just the 2 most recent)

- Priority county clerk documents were **downloaded and transcribed** — not just indexed
- Cross-references found in transcribed documents were followed (up to 3 levels deep)
- Development program eligibility was assessed based on GIS results
- All findings are saved using `save_finding` with data-dense `key_information`

You have two MCP tools for saving research as you go: `save_finding` and `append_note`. Use them throughout the session — do NOT wait until the end to record everything.

### save_finding

Call `save_finding` after evaluating a tool's output and deciding the result is relevant. Each finding captures one coherent piece of research data.

**When to call it:**
- After an appraisal district lookup returns a property record — save a finding with the owner, legal description, acreage, deed history, improvements, and taxing jurisdictions.
- After a GIS property profile returns layer results — save findings for each major data category (zoning, flood, overlays, environmental, transportation, easements, drainage infrastructure, parkland). One finding per category, not one finding per layer.
- After a FEMA flood zone lookup — save a finding with zone designation, FIRM panel, floodway status, and base flood elevation.
- After transcribing a county clerk document and determining it contains relevant provisions — save a finding with key provisions in `key_information`, the full Gemini transcription in `full_content`, and the PDF path in `file_path`.
- After an adjacent context query — save a finding with adjacent parcel zoning and abutting road classifications.
- After identifying development program eligibility — save a finding per program with the GIS evidence that triggers eligibility.

- Jurisdiction-specific field names and formats

**Follow the lookup chain exactly as specified in the jurisdiction context.** The steps below describe the general pattern, but the specific tool names, argument formats, and field mappings come from the jurisdiction context.

## Research Steps

### 1. Appraisal District Search

Use the appraisal search tool to find the property. Try these strategies in order until you get results:

1. **Parcel ID search** (most reliable) — if the site plan includes a parcel ID or geo ID, search by that identifier.
2. **Address search** — search by street address.
3. **Owner name search** — search by owner name.

### 2. Appraisal District Details

Once you have search results, use the appraisal details tool to fetch full property details (legal description, deed history, improvements, land segments, exemptions, taxing jurisdictions).

### 3. Parcel Lookup

Use the parcel ID from the appraisal district to find the property in the jurisdiction's GIS system. This returns parcel geometry and may provide a place ID or other key needed for the property profile lookup.

### 4. Property Profile

Use the property profile tool to query all available GIS layers and municipal data in a single call. Pass the parcel ID and any additional identifiers obtained from the parcel lookup.

If the profile tool supports selective re-query (filtering by category or layer), use it to retry any layers that failed on the first call.

#### Reading the output

The property profile returns structured results organized by category (zoning, flood, overlays, environmental, historical, transportation, etc.). Each layer result has:
- A layer identifier
- A status: data found, empty (parcel does not intersect this feature), or error (query failed)
- Feature attributes when data is found

**Important status semantics:**
- "Empty" means the parcel does NOT intersect this feature (e.g., NOT in a historic district, NOT in a floodplain). This is useful information — report it as a confirmed negative.
- "Error" means the query failed — document the failure and note the data is unavailable.

**Zoning interpretation:** When multiple zones are returned, use the classification or overlap percentage to determine how to report them:
- Report primary zones as the parcel's zoning designation
- Report significant overlap as true split zoning requiring dual compliance
- Report marginal overlap as a potential GIS discrepancy needing city verification — do NOT treat it as applicable zoning
- Report survey-tolerance overlap as a GIS artifact — mention it only as a note

### 5. Adjacent Context

Use the adjacent context tool to identify adjacent properties and abutting road segments. This queries a buffer around the parcel geometry for:
- **Adjacent parcels** with their zoning designations
- **Road segments** with functional classification, lane counts, ROW width, and project type

Use adjacent parcel zoning to characterize the surroundings — residential, commercial, industrial, park land, etc.

For abutting roads, cross-reference all available classification systems (functional class, transportation plan, highway system) to determine the roadway type. Service roads that parallel expressways are classified differently from the mainline highway they serve.

### 6. County Clerk Search

Search county clerk records for recorded instruments affecting this property — easements, deed restrictions, covenants, and other encumbrances that may not appear in the GIS data.

#### Step 6a: Parse Legal Description

Use the county clerk search tool with the appraisal district data to parse the legal description and get search parameters (subdivision, lot, block, search strategies).

If you also have owner name or volume/page references from GIS easement data, include them.

#### Step 6b: Delegate County Clerk Research

Use the Agent tool to spawn the `county-clerk` sub-agent. In your task description, provide ALL of the following:

1. **Parsed search parameters** from Step 6a output (lot, block, subdivision name, search strategies)
2. **Owner name(s)** from appraisal district data (current owner and prior owners from deed history)
3. **Easement document type codes** from the county clerk search output
4. **Any volume/page or instrument references** found in GIS easement data (from property profile results)
5. **Workspace path**: `{{ workspace }}`

The county-clerk agent will search, filter, download key documents, follow cross-references, and write findings to `{{ workspace }}/intermediate/county-clerk-findings.md`.

Wait for the agent to complete, then read the findings file to incorporate county clerk results into your research report.

## Persisting Your Work

You have two MCP tools for saving research as you go: `save_finding` and `append_note`. Use them throughout the session — do NOT wait until the end to record everything.

### save_finding

Call `save_finding` after evaluating a tool's output and deciding the result is relevant. Each finding captures one coherent piece of research data.

**When to call it:**
- After an appraisal district lookup returns a property record — save a finding with the owner, legal description, acreage, deed history, improvements, and taxing jurisdictions.
- After a GIS property profile returns layer results — save findings for each major data category (zoning, flood, overlays, environmental, transportation, easements). One finding per category, not one finding per layer.
- After a FEMA flood zone lookup — save a finding with zone designation, FIRM panel, floodway status, and base flood elevation.
- After transcribing a county clerk document and determining it contains relevant provisions — save a finding with key provisions in `key_information`, the full Gemini transcription in `full_content`, and the PDF path in `file_path`.
- After an adjacent context query — save a finding with adjacent parcel zoning and abutting road classifications.

**What goes in `key_information`:**

- Measurements: "20-ft wide utility easement along the northern boundary"
- Ordinance numbers: "Ord. No. 20190201-034, effective March 1, 2019"
- Zoning codes: "B-2-CU-NP, base district B-2 (General Business) with conditional-use and neighborhood-plan overlays"
- Flood data: "Zone AE, BFE 498.5 ft, FIRM Panel 48453C0570J, effective 1/19/2024"
- Quotes from documents: "Section 4.2: 'No building shall exceed 60 feet in height as measured from natural grade'"
- Appraisal values are excluded — do NOT include market value, appraised value, or tax data

**Do NOT save findings for:**
- Empty GIS layers (confirmed negatives). Mention these in a `negative_result` note instead.
- Tool errors or failed lookups. Document these in a note.
- Preliminary search results you haven't evaluated yet.

**Target: 15-25 findings per property.** Each finding should be self-contained — a reader seeing just that finding should understand the data without needing other context.

### append_note

**Note kinds and when to use them:**

- `plan` — Before starting a major research phase. Example: "Starting county clerk investigation. Will search by owner name (SMITH JOHN D), then by subdivision (OAK HILLS SEC 3 LOT 12), then follow cross-references from any restrictions found."
- `negative_result` — After a search returns irrelevant results or confirms the absence of data. Example: "Property profile returned 47 layers. 31 empty (no intersection). Notable negatives: not in historic district, not in aquifer recharge zone, no USTs on parcel. Discarding the 12 assumed-name filings from county clerk search — all are DBA registrations unrelated to property encumbrances."
- `reasoning` — When analyzing results or making a judgment call. Example: "GIS returns two zoning districts: B-2-CU-NP (92% overlap) and R-3 (3% overlap). The R-3 is a survey-tolerance artifact at the parcel boundary — reporting B-2-CU-NP as the sole applicable zoning."
- `correction` — When fixing an earlier mistake or changing strategy. Example: "Earlier county clerk search by owner name returned only 2 results. Realized I used the current owner only. Re-searching with prior owners from deed history: MARTINEZ ELENA (2015-2019), DAVIS PROPERTIES LLC (2008-2015)."

**Target: 10+ notes per session.** Notes are cheap — when in doubt, write one.

## Data Categories to Cover

Ensure your findings span these categories:

1. **Property identification** — appraisal district record: owner, legal description, acreage, deed history, improvements
2. **Zoning** — base zoning district, overlay districts, conditional overlays, zoning interpretation
3. **Flood** — FEMA zone, FIRM panel, floodway status, BFE; local flood data if available

     2→
     3→You are compiling research findings into a structured facts file for a site plan review.
     4→
     5→## Input
     6→
     7→Read these files:
     8→- `intermediate/site-plan-data.md` — extracted site plan data from Phase 1
     9→- The research findings file specified in the append-system-prompt (usually `intermediate/research-findings-injected.md`)
    10→- `intermediate/county-clerk-findings.md` — if it exists
    11→
    12→The research findings file contains structured findings from the database — each with a headline and key information — plus a research diary with notes from the research agent.
    13→
    14→## Output
    15→
    16→Write ONE file: `output/facts.md` using the Write tool.
    17→
    18→### facts.md
    19→
    20→This is the primary facts file that review agents will read. Follow the format specification in `schemas/facts.schema.md`.
    21→
    22→**Start with discrepancies.** If different sources report conflicting values for the same field, call these out prominently at the top under a `## Discrepancies` heading. For each discrepancy, state the field, the conflicting values, and their sources.
    23→
    24→If there are no discrepancies, omit this section entirely.
    25→
    26→**Easement discrepancies are especially important.** If GIS data shows easements not depicted on the site plan, or the site plan shows easements not found in GIS, call these out explicitly. Missing easements on a site plan can lead to construction in restricted areas.
    27→
    28→**Then list facts by category** in the order specified by the schema: Property, Ownership, Zoning & Land Use, Flood, Watershed & Environmental, Easements & Encumbrances, Recorded Document Provisions, Jurisdiction, Roadway Classification, Adjacent Properties, Development History.
    29→
    30→Format each line as:
    31→```
    32→- **Field**: Value
    33→```
    34→
    35→**Roadway Classification**: For each abutting road, list the street name, functional classification, project type, existing lane count, and ROW width. Note whether any roads are service roads. This data is critical for review agents — many site plan requirements (setbacks, landscaping, sidewalks, frontage, access management, screening) depend on the classification of abutting roadways. Always include this section even if only one road abuts the property.
    36→
    37→**Adjacent Properties**: Summarize the zoning and land use of properties adjacent to the subject parcel. Group by direction if determinable. Note any adjacent parcels with significantly different zoning — transitions between zones often trigger buffering, screening, or compatibility requirements. If the property abuts a park, school, or other civic use, note that explicitly.
    38→
    39→**Easements & Encumbrances**: List every easement identified from GIS data and/or county clerk records. For each, include type, width, document reference, and status. If county clerk search was performed, include any deed restrictions, covenants, or other recorded instruments.
    40→
    41→**Recorded Document Provisions**: For each document the research agent viewed and extracted provisions from, compile:
    42→- Development constraints: maximum building height, use restrictions, parking requirements, setback requirements beyond standard zoning, design review requirements, cost-sharing obligations
    43→- Access and drainage: joint access easements, drainage easements with maintenance responsibility, cross-lot access rights
    44→- Duration and enforcement: covenant duration, who can enforce, modification requirements
    45→
    46→Flag any provisions that conflict with the site plan or current zoning.
    47→
    48→**Only include facts relevant to site plan compliance review.** facts.md is read by review agents on every turn, so unnecessary data wastes tokens. Exclude:
    49→- Property valuation (market value, appraised value, land value, taxable value, estimated taxes)
    50→- Tax-related fields (homestead exemption status, tax office reference numbers)
    51→- Appraisal district administrative codes
    52→- Project team contact details (keep only firm names)
    53→- Geographic coordinate reference systems beyond lat/long
    54→
    55→**Do NOT include:**
    56→- Methodology narrative (how research was conducted)
    57→- Validation checkmarks or confirmation status
    58→- Meta-commentary about the research process
    59→
    60→## Important

# Phase 3: Compile Research Output

You are compiling research findings into a structured facts file for a site plan review.

## Input

Read these files:
- `intermediate/site-plan-data.md` — extracted site plan data from Phase 1
- The research findings file specified in the append-system-prompt (usually `intermediate/research-findings-injected.md`)
- `intermediate/county-clerk-findings.md` — if it exists

The research findings file contains structured findings from the database — each with a headline and key information — plus a research diary with notes from the research agent.

## Output

Write ONE file: `output/facts.md` using the Write tool.

### facts.md

This is the primary facts file that review agents will read. Follow the format specification in `schemas/facts.schema.md`.

**Start with discrepancies.** If different sources report conflicting values for the same field, call these out prominently at the top under a `## Discrepancies` heading. For each discrepancy, state the field, the conflicting values, and their sources.

If there are no discrepancies, omit this section entirely.

**Easement discrepancies are especially important.** If GIS data shows easements not depicted on the site plan, or the site plan shows easements not found in GIS, call these out explicitly. Missing easements on a site plan can lead to construction in restricted areas.

**Then list facts by category** in the order specified by the schema: Property, Ownership, Zoning & Land Use, Flood, Watershed & Environmental, Easements & Encumbrances, Recorded Document Provisions, Jurisdiction, Roadway Classification, Adjacent Properties, Development History.

Format each line as:
```
- **Field**: Value
```

**Roadway Classification**: For each abutting road, list the street name, functional classification, project type, existing lane count, and ROW width. Note whether any roads are service roads. This data is critical for review agents — many site plan requirements (setbacks, landscaping, sidewalks, frontage, access management, screening) depend on the classification of abutting roadways. Always include this section even if only one road abuts the property.

**Adjacent Properties**: Summarize the zoning and land use of properties adjacent to the subject parcel. Group by direction if determinable. Note any adjacent parcels with significantly different zoning — transitions between zones often trigger buffering, screening, or compatibility requirements. If the property abuts a park, school, or other civic use, note that explicitly.

**Easements & Encumbrances**: List every easement identified from GIS data and/or county clerk records. For each, include type, width, document reference, and status. If county clerk search was performed, include any deed restrictions, covenants, or other recorded instruments.

**Recorded Document Provisions**: For each document the research agent viewed and extracted provisions from, compile:
- Development constraints: maximum building height, use restrictions, parking requirements, setback requirements beyond standard zoning, design review requirements, cost-sharing obligations
- Access and drainage: joint access easements, drainage easements with maintenance responsibility, cross-lot access rights
- Duration and enforcement: covenant duration, who can enforce, modification requirements

Flag any provisions that conflict with the site plan or current zoning.

**Only include facts relevant to site plan compliance review.** facts.md is read by review agents on every turn, so unnecessary data wastes tokens. Exclude:
- Property valuation (market value, appraised value, land value, taxable value, estimated taxes)
- Tax-related fields (homestead exemption status, tax office reference numbers)
- Appraisal district administrative codes
- Project team contact details (keep only firm names)
- Geographic coordinate reference systems beyond lat/long

**Do NOT include:**
- Methodology narrative (how research was conducted)
- Validation checkmarks or confirmation status
- Meta-commentary about the research process

## Important

- Do NOT invent data. Only compile what was found in the input files.
- If a finding indicates a data source failed, do not fabricate what it might have returned.
- Do not mention AI tools, agents, or automated systems in the output.

# Surveyor: Property Research Agent

You are a property research agent. Your job is to gather comprehensive data about a property from multiple external sources, then compile your findings into structured output files for site plan review.

## Input

Extract the property address, parcel ID (if available), and owner name from this file. These are your starting search keys.

## Research Goals

4. **Cross-reference between sources** — IDs from one system feed into the next. Field names differ between systems; the jurisdiction field guide below maps them.
5. **Download and transcribe** any scanned documents using the `vision_transcribe` tool. County clerk documents are scanned images — they must be transcribed to extract provisions.
6. **Follow cross-references** in recorded documents. If a document references another instrument number, search for that too (up to 2 levels deep).

## How to Use Your Tools

You have MCP tools from multiple source modules. Read the jurisdiction field guide below for:
- What each tool does and what arguments it expects
- Which IDs from one tool feed into the next
- Field name mappings between systems
- Search strategies and their priority order
- Tips from prior runs

**You are free to call tools in whatever order makes sense.** The field guide suggests a starting point, but adapt based on what you find. If a tool fails, try alternative approaches before giving up.

**Success criteria:**
- Every available tool was called at least once
- County clerk searches used multiple strategies (not just owner name)

- Cross-references found in transcribed documents were followed
- All findings are saved using `save_finding` with data-dense `key_information`

## Persisting Your Work

You have two MCP tools for saving research as you go: `save_finding` and `append_note`. Use them throughout the session — do NOT wait until the end to record everything.

### save_finding

Call `save_finding` after evaluating a tool's output and deciding the result is relevant. Each finding captures one coherent piece of research data.

**When to call it:**

- After transcribing a county clerk document and determining it contains relevant provisions — save a finding with key provisions in `key_information`, the full Gemini transcription in `full_content`, and the PDF path in `file_path`.
- After an adjacent context query — save a finding with adjacent parcel zoning and abutting road classifications.

**What goes in `key_information`:**
This field must be **data-dense**. Include specific values, not summaries:
- Instrument numbers: "Doc 2019042301, Vol 12345 Pg 678"
- Measurements: "20-ft wide utility easement along the northern boundary"
- Ordinance numbers: "Ord. No. 20190201-034, effective March 1, 2019"
- Zoning codes: "B-2-CU-NP, base district B-2 (General Business) with conditional-use and neighborhood-plan overlays"

**Do NOT save findings for:**

Discarding the 12 assumed-name filings from county clerk search — all are DBA registrations unrelated to property encumbrances."

# Austin, TX — Research Field Guide

## Your Tools

| Tool | Source | What it does |
|------|--------|-------------|
| `appraisal_search` | tcad | Search TCAD by address, parcel ID, or owner name |
| `appraisal_details` | tcad | Fetch full property record (owner, legal desc, valuations, deed history, tax entities) |
| `parcel_lookup` | coa-gis | Find parcel in COA GIS by geoID — returns geometry, placeId/RSN |
| `property_profile` | coa-gis | Query all ~53 GIS layers in one call (zoning, flood, overlays, environmental, transportation, historic, drainage) |
| `adjacent_context` | coa-gis | Neighboring parcels with zoning + abutting ASMP/AMTP road segments |
| `fema_flood_lookup` | fema-nfhl | FEMA flood zone by lat/lon |
| `fema_flood_profile` | fema-nfhl | Detailed FEMA data: cross-sections, LOMA/LOMR, FIRM panel |
| `tceq_edwards_zone_lookup` | tceq-edwards-aquifer | TCEQ Edwards Aquifer regulatory zone for a point — returns Recharge/Transition/Contributing and required WPAP-or-CZP plan type |
| `tceq_edwards_profile` | tceq-edwards-aquifer | Edwards Aquifer zone + nearby SWQM stations + nearby regulated stream and reservoir segments |
| `tpdes_outfall_lookup` | tceq-tpdes | TCEQ TPDES outfalls within a radius of a point — permittee, permit #, NPDES #, decoded status and discharge type |
| `tpdes_outfall_search` | tceq-tpdes | Search TPDES outfalls by permittee name, permit number, or NPDES number |
| `pec_service_territory_lookup` | pec-service-territory | Electric retail service-territory point-in-polygon (HIFLD ORNL layer). For COA proper, returns Austin Energy as primary; useful for east-Travis / Lakeway-side parcels where PEC distributes |
| `txdot_roadway_lookup` | txdot | TxDOT roadway inventory by lat/lon: functional class, lanes, AADT |
| `txdot_traffic_counts` | txdot | TxDOT traffic count stations near a point |
| `census_tract_lookup` | census-qoz | US Census tract lookup by lat/lon: returns 11-digit GEOID + state/county/tract FIPS for joins to ACS, QOZ, HUD CDBG datasets |
| `qoz_lookup` | census-qoz | Federal Qualified Opportunity Zone (IRC § 1400Z-2) status by lat/lon OR tract GEOID — returns inQoz boolean + tract identifiers |
| `county_clerk_parse` | travis-county-clerk | Parse TCAD legal description into lot/block/subdivision + search strategies |
| `county_clerk_search` | travis-county-clerk | Search tccsearch.org for recorded instruments |
| `county_clerk_document` | travis-county-clerk | Download instrument PDFs from tccsearch.org |
| `vision_transcribe` | shared | Transcribe scanned PDF/image via Gemini vision AI |

## ID Mappings Between Systems

```
TCAD address search → geoID (10-digit, e.g. "0252080902") + accountId
accountId → appraisal_details (param: accountId)
geoID → COA GIS parcel_lookup → placeId/RSN (for Geocortex)
geoID → COA GIS property_profile (primary key for all layers)
geoID → COA GIS adjacent_context
parcel centroid (WGS84 lat/lon from parcel_lookup) → fema_flood_lookup, fema_flood_profile, txdot_roadway_lookup
TCAD legal description → county_clerk_parse → search strategies
```

**Important:** Use the 10-digit geoID format, not the extended 14-digit version. TCAD details param is `accountId`.

## Suggested Starting Point

Start with TCAD address search — it gives you the geoID that everything else needs. Then fan out: GIS profile, FEMA, TxDOT, and county clerk can all run once you have the geoID and coordinates.

## Jurisdiction-Specific Notes

### Geocortex and Amanda
The property profile includes Geocortex workflows that return COA address data (with State Plane coordinates) and Amanda planning case history. Check Amanda data for prior approvals, active permits, and open cases.

### Zoning
Zoning strings can be compound: `GR-MU-CO-NP` = General Retail + Mixed Use + Conditional Overlay + Neighborhood Plan. Report both `ZONING_ZTYPE` (full) and `ZONING_BASE` (base district).

When multiple zones intersect:
- **primary** — the parcel's zoning
- **significant** — split zoning requiring dual compliance
- **marginal** — potential GIS discrepancy; don't treat as applicable
- **survey-tolerance** — GIS artifact; mention as a note only

### Transportation (ASMP)
ASMP road levels (1-5): 1=Local, 2=Collector, 3=Corridor, 4=Service road/ramp, 5=Expressway. Service roads (level 4) are NOT highways. Cross-reference ASMP and AMTP for functional classification. TxDOT data supplements with AADT and lane counts.

### Environmental
Edwards Aquifer recharge zone triggers environmental review. Check environmental layers for recharge zone, watershed regulation areas, salamander habitat, underground storage tanks, wildland-urban interface, and creek buffers.

### Edwards Aquifer — decision-ready tools
The COA `property_profile` returns an `edwards-aquifer` polygon intersect from the city's downloaded layer snapshot. For the **regulatory** question (which TCEQ plan must be submitted under 30 TAC Ch. 213?), call **`tceq_edwards_zone_lookup`** with the parcel centroid (lat/lon from `parcel_lookup`). It returns `zoneCode: RECHARGE | TRANSITION | CONTRIBUTING` and `requiredPlanType: WPAP | CZP` with the citation — TCEQ's own ArcGIS service is authoritative when it disagrees with the COA snapshot. Use **`tceq_edwards_profile`** for the same answer plus nearby SWQM stations and regulated stream/reservoir segments. Validated: downtown Austin returns `TRANSITION → WPAP`; Floor & Decor seed in Cedar Park returns `CONTRIBUTING → CZP`.

### TPDES outfalls — neighbouring permitted dischargers
For diligence questions about regulated dischargers near a subject parcel — upstream stormwater outfalls, a downstream wastewater plant, a neighbouring industrial outfall — call **`tpdes_outfall_lookup`** with the parcel centroid (default 1000 m radius). The dataset surfaces TPDES individual permits, the Construction General Permit (TXR150000), Industrial Stormwater (TXR050000), and MS4 (TXR040000) outfalls. To find where a known operator discharges, use **`tpdes_outfall_search`** by permittee name. Caveat: not every Construction General Permit NOI produces a separate outfall point — STEERS-only filings are not in the public layer.

### Historic
27 historic districts administered by OHP/HDRC. Check for landmark status and local/national district intersection.

### Flood
Three overlapping flood sources — treat duplicates as confirmation:
- FEMA floodplain (federal)
- COA fully-developed floodplain (city's more conservative model)
- FloodPro (parcel-level FEMA zone, COA zone, BFE)

### Spatial Reference
COA GIS uses State Plane Texas Central (EPSG 102739). Parcel geometry returned in both native SR and WGS84.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about Austin's HOME amendment regarding duplexes and SF-2/SF-3 zoning in 2024-2025:

## HOME Amendment Overview

The HOME amendments allow up to three housing units, including tiny homes, on Single-Family (SF) zoned properties (SF-1, SF-2, SF-3), revise regulations for properties with two housing units, and remove restrictions on the number of unrelated adults living in a housing unit.

## Key Phases and Timeline

Phase 1 only applies to duplexes, two-unit residential, and three-unit residential uses. On November 16, 2024, citywide development applications were accepted under HOME Phase 2. Phase 2 included Site Plan Lite and Infill Plat adoption by City Council on March 6, 2025, with development applications for those programs accepted starting June 16, 2025.

## Minimum Lot Size Changes

HOME Phase 2 was approved by City Council on May 16, 2024, and lowered the minimum lot size for small lot single-family from 5,750 sq ft to 1,800 sq ft for properties zoned SF-1, SF-2, and SF-3.

## ADU Expansion to More Zones

I've performed the web search for your query about Austin TX duplex building permit demolition requirements for existing homes in SF-2 and SF-3 zones. Here are the key findings:

## Zoning Allowances for Duplexes

In Austin, duplexes are allowed in specific zoning districts including SF-3, SF-5, and SF-6. Additionally, Austin's HOME amendments allow up to three housing units, including tiny homes, on a Single-Family (SF) zoned property (SF-1, SF-2, SF-3).

## Building Permit and Demolition Requirements

The Residential Plan Review Division reviews new construction, additions, interior remodeling and demolition of single-family, duplex or two-family houses and/or additional buildings on one lot.

Residential construction projects are reviewed for compliance with Chapter 25-2 of the Land Development Code, the 2024 International Residential Code, and Chapter 25-12, Technical Codes (local amendments).

## Recent Updates (2025-2026)

As of December 2025, a Site Plan Exemption will no longer be required for 3-unit, 4-unit, and larger duplex projects to satisfy landscaping review.

## Lot Requirements for SF-2 and SF-3 Zones

For SF-2 (Single-Family Standard Lot), the requirements include front setback of 25 feet, side 5 feet, rear 10 feet, with lot coverage max 40%, impervious cover max 45%, and FAR max 0.40:1. SF-3 (Single-Family, attached housing) has front 25 feet, side 5 feet, rear 10 feet setbacks, with lot coverage max 40% and impervious cover max 45%.

For specific details about your project, the search results recommend contacting the Residential Plan Review Division directly through Austin's Development Services.

# Duplex Conversion Requirements in Austin, TX

## Zoning Districts
Duplexes are permitted in **SF-3, SF-5, SF-6** districts, plus **MF zones, Central Business District (CBD), and Downtown Mixed Use (DMU)**. Verification of specific zoning classification is essential before proceeding.

## Dimensional Standards

**Lot Size:** Minimum 5,750 square feet required

**Unit Size:** The smaller unit must be either 1,100 square feet or 0.15 Floor Area Ratio (FAR), whichever is smaller. Second-story units cannot exceed 550 square feet.

**Height:** Maximum 30 feet tall

**Impervious Cover:** Regulations limit how much of the lot can be covered with rooftops or pavement. Specific percentages are managed through the Accessory Dwelling Units guidelines to control water runoff and ensure sustainability.

**Building Coverage:** Cannot exceed "15% of the lot area or 1,100 square feet, whichever is less"

## Permit Requirements

A **building permit is mandatory** for conversion work. Permits are required for electrical, plumbing, and structural modifications. The process involves:

- Creating an Austin Build + Connect (AB+C) account
- Submitting detailed construction plans showing site layout, floor plans, and elevations
- Initial review taking several weeks
- Obtaining approval from the Residential Plan Review Division

## Parking Requirements

Each duplex unit requires **at least two parking spaces**. Not more than one required parking space may be positioned behind another required space. Spaces must be on paved surfaces (concrete preferred).

## Construction Standards

Projects must comply with the "2021 International Residential Code" and Chapter 25-2 of Austin's Land Development Code. Chapter 25-12 Technical Codes governs plumbing, electrical, and structural integrity.

## HOME Amendments Impact

The content does not provide specific information about HOME (Home Options for Middle Income Empowerment) amendments' impact on duplex development in Austin.

Multiple residential and commercial development projects have been approved in the Walnut Creek Watershed area near East Parmer Lane and Tech Ridge Boulevard, indicating significant urban expansion in north Austin.

One of the most significant projects in this area is EastVillage, a $1 billion, 425-acre master-planned community located across from the Samsung Austin Semiconductor on East Parmer Lane. The mixed-use development will bring residential, retail, restaurants, entertainment and green space, and at full occupancy is expected to host 12,000 people a day.

## Infrastructure and Growth Context

## Watershed and Water Quality Context

Walnut Creek flows from northern Austin to the Colorado River, drains about 43 square miles, and development in the upper section of the watershed has been faster and denser than in the lower section.
