1→# Subdivision & Development Engineering Feasibility — Austin, TX
     2→
     3→## Domain
     4→
     5→Drainage analysis, stormwater detention and water quality controls, grading, retaining walls, easements, storm drain design, subdivision platting, standard details, and construction inspection for City of Austin and Austin ETJ projects. Bridges with `wwp` (water/wastewater), `fwp` (floodplain & creek buffers), `ta` (transportation/ROW), and `el` (environmental — CEFs, EARZ, watershed classification).
     6→
     7→SDE is the largest discipline by code volume; expect to coordinate findings across most of the other disciplines.
     8→
     9→## Authoritative sources
    10→
    11→- **Drainage Criteria Manual (DCM)** — Watershed Protection Department; governs drainage design, easements, ponds, RSMP
    12→- **Environmental Criteria Manual (ECM)** — water quality controls (SCMs/GSI), grading, IWM, CEFs, EARZ liners
    13→- **Land Development Code (LDC) Title 25** — chapters 25-7 (drainage), 25-8 (environmental/water quality), 25-4/30-2 (subdivision)
    14→- **Transportation Criteria Manual (TCM) §13.2** — retaining wall structural and ROW requirements
    15→- **Utilities Criteria Manual (UCM) §2.5** — construction plan content, PE seal, sheet standards
    16→- **City of Austin Standard Specifications & Standard Drawings (SSM/Std Specs)** — 508S outlet structures, 661 series WQ details, 594S gabions, 414S waterstops, 623S dry-stack rock, 658S void mitigation
    17→- **RSMP Participation Handbook (FY24, effective July 15, 2024)** — Regional Stormwater Management Program
    18→- **General Site Plan Notes for COA** and **Environmental Review Requirements** — cover sheet and plan note templates
    19→
    20→Atlas 14 rainfall is mandatory for submittals on/after Nov 25, 2019 (DCM 2.3.0). Approved drainage modeling software: HEC-HMS, HEC-RAS, PondPack, StormCAD, CivilStorm (DCM 1.2.5).
    21→
    22→## Regulatory pathway
    23→
    24→| Action | Path | Typical timeline |
    25→|---|---|---|
    26→| Concept/feasibility review | Optional Pre-Development Consultation; RSMP Feasibility Meeting if pursuing RSMP | 4–8 weeks |
    27→| Subdivision | Preliminary Plan → Subdivision Construction Plans → Final Plat | 6–18 months |
    28→| Site Plan (commercial / multifamily) | SDP application → Completeness Check → Update Cycles → Approval | 9–18 months in current cycle times |
    29→| RSMP participation | Feasibility Meeting **before** Completeness Check → Application Package → Approval Letter → Agreement → Payment | 3–6 months to Approval Letter; payment before permit issuance |
    30→| Construction permit | Site Development Permit issued after plan approval; pre-construction conference required (LDC § 25-1-282) | 2–6 weeks post-approval |
    31→| Inspection / acceptance | DSD/WPD inspection through construction; engineer certifications before CO; SCM acceptance for SF/duplex (City takes maintenance); restrictive covenant for commercial/MF (owner maintains) | continuous |
    32→
    33→Key sequencing trap: **RSMP feasibility meeting must occur before formal Completeness Check.** If RSMP is in play, schedule that meeting at the start of design.
    34→
    35→## Constraints to evaluate
    36→
    37→### Drainage performance standard (DCM 1.2.2.D)
    38→
    39→- **No-increase rule** at every point of discharge for the 2-, 10-, 25-, and 100-year storms. Existing and proposed conditions modeled separately.
    40→- **Exception:** direct discharge into Lady Bird Lake, Lake Austin, Lake Travis, the Colorado River, or qualifying Waller Creek TIRZ properties (DCM 1.2.2.F).
    41→- **Atlas 14 rainfall** for all submittals after Nov 25, 2019. Pre-Atlas 14 phased developments may use DCM 1.2.2.H hybrid criteria.
    42→- Off-site contributing areas modeled at **existing IC** for pond performance (DCM 8.3.2.A) but **fully developed** for spillway/embankment design (DCM 8.3.3.A). Both apply to the same pond.
    43→
    44→### Water quality controls (LDC § 25-8-211; ECM 1.6)
    45→
    46→- **Trigger:** any new + redeveloped IC > 8,000 SF outside BSZ; **all** development in the Barton Springs Zone (no threshold).
    47→- **Green Stormwater Infrastructure (GSI) mandatory** since Nov 7, 2022 (LDC § 25-8-213(C)). Conventional sed/filtration ponds and wet ponds require a documented exemption: highly contaminated runoff land use, off-site treatment ≥ 10 acres of currently untreated developed area, or site IC > 90% gross area (LDC § 25-8-213(D)).
    48→- **WQV formula** (ECM 1.6.2.A): WQV = (0.5 in + 0.1 in per 10% IC over 20%) × DA (ac) × 3,630. Drawdown within 48 hours. Applies to all IC on site, not just new IC.
    49→- **EARZ controls (LDC § 25-8-213(A)(2); ECM 1.6.2.C):** impermeable liner required — geomembrane (≥ 30 mils, UV resistant) or concrete (basins < 1,000 SF). Clay liners (Std Detail 661-2) **prohibited** over EARZ regardless of permeability testing. Vegetative filter strips are the only exemption.
    50→- **Rain garden cap:** 2 acres contributing drainage area (ECM 1.6.7.H). Larger = biofiltration basin (ECM 1.6.7.C). Recommended max 50 acres per WQ control (ECM 1.6.2.A).
    51→- **Wet pond minimum permanent pool:** > 0.5 ac (21,780 SF) (ECM 1.6.6.A.1).
    52→- **IWM (Innovative Water Management):** commercial sites with required landscape area must irrigate ≥ 50% with stormwater or leave undisturbed (LDC § 25-2-1008; ECM 2.4.9). 1:2 minimum drainage-to-landscape ratio.
    53→
    54→### Stormwater detention
    55→
    56→- **2-year on-site control required regardless of RSMP** (LDC § 25-7-61(A)(5)(c); ECM 1.6.8).
    57→- **Detention drawdown:** max 24 hr for flood detention (DCM 8.3.2.C).
    58→- **Regional pond threshold:** > 64 ac contributing drainage area triggers WPD project-by-project review and geotechnical-based slope design (DCM 8.3.2.B; DCM 8.3.3.F).
    59→- **Dam classification:** SWM pond embankment ≥ 6 ft at any point along the perimeter → dam (DCM 8.3.3.B.1). Triggers PMF design, 20-ft clear zone (no trees/woody vegetation upstream and downstream of toe), and TCEQ jurisdiction concerns.
    60→- **Storm drain connection** required when within 300 ft of an existing storm drain system (DCM 1.2.3.C, as amended 9-8-2025). RSMP does **not** waive this.
    61→
    62→### Grading and slopes
    63→
    64→- General cut/fill side slopes: max 3H:1V (DCM 8.3.3.F; DCM 6.4.1.D). Rock slopes steeper than 3:1 require geotechnical stability report.

# Subdivision & Development Engineering Feasibility — Austin, TX

## Domain

Drainage analysis, stormwater detention and water quality controls, grading, retaining walls, easements, storm drain design, subdivision platting, standard details, and construction inspection for City of Austin and Austin ETJ projects. Bridges with `wwp` (water/wastewater), `fwp` (floodplain & creek buffers), `ta` (transportation/ROW), and `el` (environmental — CEFs, EARZ, watershed classification).

SDE is the largest discipline by code volume; expect to coordinate findings across most of the other disciplines.

## Authoritative sources

- **Drainage Criteria Manual (DCM)** — Watershed Protection Department; governs drainage design, easements, ponds, RSMP
- **Environmental Criteria Manual (ECM)** — water quality controls (SCMs/GSI), grading, IWM, CEFs, EARZ liners
- **Land Development Code (LDC) Title 25** — chapters 25-7 (drainage), 25-8 (environmental/water quality), 25-4/30-2 (subdivision)
- **Transportation Criteria Manual (TCM) §13.2** — retaining wall structural and ROW requirements
- **Utilities Criteria Manual (UCM) §2.5** — construction plan content, PE seal, sheet standards
- **City of Austin Standard Specifications & Standard Drawings (SSM/Std Specs)** — 508S outlet structures, 661 series WQ details, 594S gabions, 414S waterstops, 623S dry-stack rock, 658S void mitigation
- **RSMP Participation Handbook (FY24, effective July 15, 2024)** — Regional Stormwater Management Program
- **General Site Plan Notes for COA** and **Environmental Review Requirements** — cover sheet and plan note templates

Atlas 14 rainfall is mandatory for submittals on/after Nov 25, 2019 (DCM 2.3.0). Approved drainage modeling software: HEC-HMS, HEC-RAS, PondPack, StormCAD, CivilStorm (DCM 1.2.5).

## Regulatory pathway

| Action | Path | Typical timeline |
|---|---|---|
| Concept/feasibility review | Optional Pre-Development Consultation; RSMP Feasibility Meeting if pursuing RSMP | 4–8 weeks |
| Subdivision | Preliminary Plan → Subdivision Construction Plans → Final Plat | 6–18 months |
| Site Plan (commercial / multifamily) | SDP application → Completeness Check → Update Cycles → Approval | 9–18 months in current cycle times |
| RSMP participation | Feasibility Meeting **before** Completeness Check → Application Package → Approval Letter → Agreement → Payment | 3–6 months to Approval Letter; payment before permit issuance |
| Construction permit | Site Development Permit issued after plan approval; pre-construction conference required (LDC § 25-1-282) | 2–6 weeks post-approval |
| Inspection / acceptance | DSD/WPD inspection through construction; engineer certifications before CO; SCM acceptance for SF/duplex (City takes maintenance); restrictive covenant for commercial/MF (owner maintains) | continuous |

Key sequencing trap: **RSMP feasibility meeting must occur before formal Completeness Check.** If RSMP is in play, schedule that meeting at the start of design.

## Constraints to evaluate

### Drainage performance standard (DCM 1.2.2.D)

- **No-increase rule** at every point of discharge for the 2-, 10-, 25-, and 100-year storms. Existing and proposed conditions modeled separately.
- **Exception:** direct discharge into Lady Bird Lake, Lake Austin, Lake Travis, the Colorado River, or qualifying Waller Creek TIRZ properties (DCM 1.2.2.F).
- **Atlas 14 rainfall** for all submittals after Nov 25, 2019. Pre-Atlas 14 phased developments may use DCM 1.2.2.H hybrid criteria.
- Off-site contributing areas modeled at **existing IC** for pond performance (DCM 8.3.2.A) but **fully developed** for spillway/embankment design (DCM 8.3.3.A). Both apply to the same pond.

### Water quality controls (LDC § 25-8-211; ECM 1.6)

- **Trigger:** any new + redeveloped IC > 8,000 SF outside BSZ; **all** development in the Barton Springs Zone (no threshold).
- **Green Stormwater Infrastructure (GSI) mandatory** since Nov 7, 2022 (LDC § 25-8-213(C)). Conventional sed/filtration ponds and wet ponds require a documented exemption: highly contaminated runoff land use, off-site treatment ≥ 10 acres of currently untreated developed area, or site IC > 90% gross area (LDC § 25-8-213(D)).
- **WQV formula** (ECM 1.6.2.A): WQV = (0.5 in + 0.1 in per 10% IC over 20%) × DA (ac) × 3,630. Drawdown within 48 hours. Applies to all IC on site, not just new IC.
- **EARZ controls (LDC § 25-8-213(A)(2); ECM 1.6.2.C):** impermeable liner required — geomembrane (≥ 30 mils, UV resistant) or concrete (basins < 1,000 SF). Clay liners (Std Detail 661-2) **prohibited** over EARZ regardless of permeability testing. Vegetative filter strips are the only exemption.
- **Rain garden cap:** 2 acres contributing drainage area (ECM 1.6.7.H). Larger = biofiltration basin (ECM 1.6.7.C). Recommended max 50 acres per WQ control (ECM 1.6.2.A).
- **Wet pond minimum permanent pool:** > 0.5 ac (21,780 SF) (ECM 1.6.6.A.1).
- **IWM (Innovative Water Management):** commercial sites with required landscape area must irrigate ≥ 50% with stormwater or leave undisturbed (LDC § 25-2-1008; ECM 2.4.9). 1:2 minimum drainage-to-landscape ratio.

### Stormwater detention

- **2-year on-site control required regardless of RSMP** (LDC § 25-7-61(A)(5)(c); ECM 1.6.8).
- **Detention drawdown:** max 24 hr for flood detention (DCM 8.3.2.C).
- **Regional pond threshold:** > 64 ac contributing drainage area triggers WPD project-by-project review and geotechnical-based slope design (DCM 8.3.2.B; DCM 8.3.3.F).
- **Dam classification:** SWM pond embankment ≥ 6 ft at any point along the perimeter → dam (DCM 8.3.3.B.1). Triggers PMF design, 20-ft clear zone (no trees/woody vegetation upstream and downstream of toe), and TCEQ jurisdiction concerns.
- **Storm drain connection** required when within 300 ft of an existing storm drain system (DCM 1.2.3.C, as amended 9-8-2025). RSMP does **not** waive this.

### Grading and slopes

- General cut/fill side slopes: max 3H:1V (DCM 8.3.3.F; DCM 6.4.1.D). Rock slopes steeper than 3:1 require geotechnical stability report.
- Wet pond earthen slopes max 3:1 (ECM 1.6.6.C.6); vegetated bench between 3:1 and 4:1 (or 4:1–5:1 for ponds ≥ 2 ac, ECM Table 1-9B).
- WQ facility maintenance drives: ≤ 15% longitudinal, ≤ 5% transverse (DCM 1.2.4.E.1.e).
- Temporary ESC slopes 2:1 or flatter (ECM 1.4.5). Final slopes > 15% require erosion control matting at toe and top.
- Elevations must be NAVD88 (or equivalent absolute datum), not site-relative. BCM 4.4.3.1 requires a permanent benchmark on the plot plan.

### Retaining walls (TCM § 13.2)

- **< 2 ft (minor structure):** no PE, no geotech, no separate building permit. Construction waiver available unless wall supports roadway embankment.
- **≥ 2 ft:** licensed PE design + geotechnical investigation required.
- **≥ 4 ft:** structural plan submittal + calculations before site plan approval + separate **building permit** (IBC). Cover sheet note required.
- **> 10 ft and supporting roadway embankment:** 20-ft truck-accessible maintenance zone at base (TCM 13.2.9).
- **In/adjacent to ROW:** D1 ≤ H1 rule triggers full §13.2 review. 5-ft minimum face-to-back-of-curb. External components (geogrid, soldier piles) need ≥ 36 in cover. Private walls **not allowed in ROW** without encroachment agreement (City Council approval).
- **Drainage easement walls:** not categorically prohibited — Director approval + license/encroachment agreement + utility encasement.
- **Inside SCMs:** dry-stacked rock prohibited (ECM 1.6.3.B.7). Grouted rock walls inside SCMs require impermeable barrier. Waterstops required at expansion joints (ECM 1.6.3.B.6; Std Spec 414S.4.E).
- **Safety rails:** not a universal "> 4 ft" trigger. Triggered when wall supports roadway embankment adjacent to sidewalk/roadway, OR when wall is adjacent to park/playground/SF/MF residential with backslope toward wall (TCM 13.2.10).

1→# Electrical & Utility Feasibility — Austin
     2→
     3→## Domain
     4→
     5→Electrical utility service (Austin Energy), street lighting, overhead conductor clearances, underground utility routing, easement and ROW coordination, AULCC clearance, moonlight tower buffers, and addressing. This discipline determines whether the desired massing, frontage, and parking layout can be served by AE under the applicable corridor/regulating-plan framework — and what coordination timelines that triggers.

     7→## Authoritative sources
     8→
     9→- Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual (AEDC): §§ 1.3, 1.4, 1.6, 1.16
    10→- Utility Criteria Manual (UCM): §§ 1.3, 1.5, 1.10, 1.14, 2.5.1.F, 2.9, 3.2, 3.4, 3.8, 5.2

    14→- Plaza Saltillo TOD Regulating Plan §§ 3.3.2–3.3.4
    15→- North Burnet/Gateway (NBG) Regulating Plan § 3.3.2.B.4
    16→- Great Streets Master Plan, Chapter 6 (lighting)
    17→- City of Austin Addressing Standards (AMS / 911 Addressing)
    18→- External: OSHA 1910.333; Texas H&S Code § 752.004; NESC
    19→
    20→## Regulatory pathway
    21→
    22→| Trigger | Path | Decision body | Typical duration |
    23→|---|---|---|---|
    24→| Any new/modified electric service | Electric Service Planning Application (ESPA) to AE; resubmit after Electric Permit issuance | Austin Energy Design | 6–12 weeks after site plan approval |
    25→| Service >350 A single-phase / >225 A three-phase, or any service in downtown Network Area | ESPA via Design Services (full AE Design involvement) | AE Design Services | Add 4–8 weeks vs. Service-Only |
    26→| AE facilities proposed on private property | Electrical easement dedication on standard City forms before AE installs | AE Public Involvement | 4–6 weeks |
    27→| ≥300 LF ROW utility work citywide; ≥25 LF in DAPCZ; any pole relocation; main assignments | AULCC review → Completeness Letter | AULCC (multi-utility committee) | 8–16 weeks; gates ROW Review approval |
    28→| ≥48-hour pre-construction notice + safety meeting near transmission | AE Transmission engineering | AE Transmission | Per-event |
    29→| Within 100 ft of moonlight tower or guy wire | COA § 14-11-201 permit (building official for private; director for ROW) | Building Official / Director | Concurrent with permitting |
    30→| Light rail corridor proximity (Project Connect) | UROP consultation; Downtown Rail Corridor Permit for 4th St corridor | CapMetro / DSD | Site-specific |
    31→| Hill Country Roadway Corridor (1,000 ft of Loop 360, RM 620, RM 2222, RM 2244, SW Pkwy) | All on-site utilities underground unless utility provider requires otherwise | DSD | At site plan |
    32→| New streets, private drives, or new addresses | 911 Addressing / AMS reservation and addressing plan approval | Address Management Services | 2–4 weeks; gates site plan approval |
    33→
    34→Note: ESPA is normally submitted **after** DSD site plan approval, not before (AEDC 1.4.2.7.A). Build the AE design into the diligence timeline as a post-approval, pre-permit critical path item — not as a parallel-with-site-plan item.
    35→
    36→## Constraints to evaluate
    37→
    38→### Overhead clearance & undergrounding
    39→
    40→- **Building footprint vs. 15-ft radial / 7.5-ft sky-to-ground clearance** from any AE overhead distribution conductor on or adjacent to the site (UCM § 1.10.3). Both apply simultaneously; the outer conductor (not pole centerline) is the datum. Evaluate whether the desired building envelope physically clears overhead lines along the relevant frontage, and if not, whether undergrounding the offending span is feasible and at what cost.
    41→- **10-ft overhead utility zone** from energized conductor where overhead lines remain on a Core Transit Corridor or Urban Roadway frontage (LDC Subchapter E § 2.2.2.B.3.b; § 2.2.3.B.3). Same 10-ft zone applies inside Plaza Saltillo TOD (§ 3.3.2.A.3.b) and NBG (§ 3.3.2.B.4.b). Confirm whether the frontage street triggers Subchapter E or a regulating plan, then whether overhead is feasible to underground vs. relocate to rear-of-site.
    42→- **Building-to-property-line undergrounding** mandatory on all CTC, Urban Roadway, Plaza Saltillo TOD, NBG, and Hill Country Roadway Corridor frontages (LDC Subchapter E § 2.2.2.B.3.a, § 2.2.3.B.3; Plaza Saltillo TOD § 3.3.2.A.3 / .3.3.A.3 / .3.4.A.3; NBG § 3.3.2.B.4.a; LDC § 25-2-1125). Budget service-lateral undergrounding cost.
    43→- **ROW undergrounding "to the maximum extent practicable"** on the same frontages (same citations). This is judgment-driven; expect AE to negotiate which existing overhead is left in place vs. relocated to rear of site. Identify the existing overhead pattern early.
    44→- **Transmission proximity** (60 kV+: 69 / 138 / 345 kV AE circuits): clearance envelopes are site-specific and require AE engineering (UCM § 1.14.3.1); circuits cannot be de-energized for nearby work.     45→- **Service-drop vertical clearance** over driveways and access — 16 ft (no-truck) / 18 ft (truck/public street) (UCM § 1.10.6.2). Constrains canopy/porte-cochère height and loading-dock geometry.
    46→
    47→### Underground routing & easements
    48→
    49→- **AW planting-zone prohibition** (UCM § 2.9.1.C): no AW main, service, or appurtenance within the ROW street-tree planting zone. Root barriers required 7 ft from trunk; 2-ft AW offset from barrier; minimum 8-ft Street Tree Utility Gap between zones. Constrains where water service can leave the building when street trees are required.
    50→- **No parallel routing within AE / public utility easement** (UCM § 2.9.1.A.3) — only perpendicular or up to 45° crossings. Constrains site utility layout when easements bisect the parcel.
    51→- **Easement encroachment**: no permanent structures, pools, or buildings in AE easements (UCM § 1.10.10.2); landscaping/paving/walls in private AE easements require License Agreement from AE Public Involvement (UCM § 1.10.10.3); same items in public utility easements / public ROW require Chapter 14 license (§ 14-11-41). Evaluate whether the desired site plan crosses easements and whether the licensing pathway is workable.
    52→- **Transformer pad siting** (UCM §§ 1.5.2.6, 1.10.4): hot-stick (padlocked) side 10 ft from any adjacent building; non-operator sides 3 ft from fence; operator side 5 ft; pad within 6 ft of paved truck-accessible surface; pad must be on customer property (not ROW or parkland); dedicated AE easement encumbers the pad. Reserve ~150–250 sf of usable frontage for the pad early in concept design.
    53→- **AE truck access** (UCM § 1.3.16): 12-ft horizontal × 16-ft vertical clear path to AE equipment, with 20 × 35 ft set-up area at 35-ft vertical clearance. AE facilities normally at front of property or adjacent to paved surface (UCM § 1.3.15).
    54→- **AE underground separations** (UCM § 1.10.5.A): 12 in min from other utilities at perpendicular crossings; 36 in from ≥60 psi gas. Joint trench with other utilities requires written AE agreement.
    55→- **Water/wastewater main crossings** (UCM § 2.9.1.B.3, § 2.9.2.B.17): 12 in (AW above) / 18 in (AW below) for open-cut; trenchless = greater of 2× excavation diameter or 36 in.

    57→- **Light rail corridors**: UCM § 5.2.2 Downtown Rail Corridor Permit for E-W 4th Street corridor (IH-35 to Seaholm); UROP consultation for other Project Connect alignments. Materially affects feasibility for parcels along Project Connect.
    58→- **Moonlight towers** (downtown / central Austin): 25-ft ROW-installation prohibition (§ 14-11-205); 100-ft permit threshold for any construction near tower or guy wire (§ 14-11-201). Locations are not mapped in code — confirm by field survey early if site is in downtown or central Austin.

    61→
    62→- **SCM staging area + maintenance access drive vertical clearance**: 14 ft from existing/proposed vegetation at maturity (DCM § 1.2.4.E.2.e and § 1.2.4.E.1.e.ii).     64→- **Storm drain manhole vs. AE pole separation**: minimum 5 ft horizontal between storm drain manholes and AE overhead poles (reviewer convention). Constrains drainage outfall layout where existing poles are present.
    65→- **Encasement under roads/structures** (UCM § 2.9.1.D): encased crossings under roadways require material, dimensional, and longitudinal extent specifications on plans. Budget bored/encased crossings on any utility leaving the site under a public street.
    66→
    67→### Construction-phase impacts
    68→
    69→- **Transmission demolition sequence** (UCM § 1.14.9): pre-construction safety meeting ≥48 hr before work; barricades 10 ft from all transmission structures including guys/anchors; warning signs under overhead facilities; no spoils or materials in transmission easement; crane and temporary-structure setbacks so they cannot fall within 20 ft of transmission.     70→- **Work-zone vertical clearance below overhead** (UCM § 1.10.6.2; § 1.3.16): 18 ft where truck traffic is anticipated; 16 ft for affirmatively non-truck driveways; 35 ft set-up area in front of AE equipment. Affects crane staging and tilt-up sequencing.
    71→
    72→### Connectivity & frontage
    73→
    74→- **Table B utility-in-drive-aisle option** (LDC Subchapter E § 2.3.1.B.2): on subject sites (≥3 ac nonresidential, or surface parking between building and principal street), site must select ≥2 Table B options (3 if parking >125% of formerly required).     77→
    78→- **AE Service Availability Letter** (AEDC § 1.4.1) — only where it is unclear which utility serves the site. Confirm AE service area on edge-of-territory parcels before design.

Root barriers required 7 ft from trunk; 2-ft AW offset from barrier; minimum 8-ft Street Tree Utility Gap between zones. Constrains where water service can leave the building when street trees are required.
- **No parallel routing within AE / public utility easement** (UCM § 2.9.1.A.3) — only perpendicular or up to 45° crossings. Constrains site utility layout when easements bisect the parcel.
- **Easement encroachment**: no permanent structures, pools, or buildings in AE easements (UCM § 1.10.10.2); landscaping/paving/walls in private AE easements require License Agreement from AE Public Involvement (UCM § 1.10.10.3); same items in public utility easements / public ROW require Chapter 14 license (§ 14-11-41). Evaluate whether the desired site plan crosses easements and whether the licensing pathway is workable.
- **Transformer pad siting** (UCM §§ 1.5.2.6, 1.10.4): hot-stick (padlocked) side 10 ft from any adjacent building; non-operator sides 3 ft from fence; operator side 5 ft; pad within 6 ft of paved truck-accessible surface; pad must be on customer property (not ROW or parkland); dedicated AE easement encumbers the pad. Reserve ~150–250 sf of usable frontage for the pad early in concept design.
- **AE truck access** (UCM § 1.3.16): 12-ft horizontal × 16-ft vertical clear path to AE equipment, with 20 × 35 ft set-up area at 35-ft vertical clearance. AE facilities normally at front of property or adjacent to paved surface (UCM § 1.3.15).
- **AE underground separations** (UCM § 1.10.5.A): 12 in min from other utilities at perpendicular crossings; 36 in from ≥60 psi gas. Joint trench with other utilities requires written AE agreement.
- **Water/wastewater main crossings** (UCM § 2.9.1.B.3, § 2.9.2.B.17): 12 in (AW above) / 18 in (AW below) for open-cut; trenchless = greater of 2× excavation diameter or 36 in.
- **ROW assignment / 24-in proximity** (§ 14-11-180(C)): facilities within 24 in of an existing ROW facility require AULCC ROW assignment change approval — a process, not a prohibition, but it consumes time.
- **Light rail corridors**: UCM § 5.2.2 Downtown Rail Corridor Permit for E-W 4th Street corridor (IH-35 to Seaholm); UROP consultation for other Project Connect alignments. Materially affects feasibility for parcels along Project Connect.
- **Moonlight towers** (downtown / central Austin): 25-ft ROW-installation prohibition (§ 14-11-205); 100-ft permit threshold for any construction near tower or guy wire (§ 14-11-201). Locations are not mapped in code — confirm by field survey early if site is in downtown or central Austin.

### Drainage-utility interactions

- **SCM staging area + maintenance access drive vertical clearance**: 14 ft from existing/proposed vegetation at maturity (DCM § 1.2.4.E.2.e and § 1.2.4.E.1.e.ii). Applies to COA-maintained and residential-development SCMs above 5,000 cf / 3-ft depth thresholds. Constrains canopy planting along maintenance routes.
- **No utility routing under detention/retention ponds** (reviewer convention; common-violation pattern). Affects site utility layout when ponds dominate the site.
- **Storm drain manhole vs. AE pole separation**: minimum 5 ft horizontal between storm drain manholes and AE overhead poles (reviewer convention). Constrains drainage outfall layout where existing poles are present.
- **Encasement under roads/structures** (UCM § 2.9.1.D): encased crossings under roadways require material, dimensional, and longitudinal extent specifications on plans. Budget bored/encased crossings on any utility leaving the site under a public street.

### Construction-phase impacts

- **Transmission demolition sequence** (UCM § 1.14.9): pre-construction safety meeting ≥48 hr before work; barricades 10 ft from all transmission structures including guys/anchors; warning signs under overhead facilities; no spoils or materials in transmission easement; crane and temporary-structure setbacks so they cannot fall within 20 ft of transmission. Forces an alternate spoils/laydown area when transmission abuts the site.
- **Work-zone vertical clearance below overhead** (UCM § 1.10.6.2; § 1.3.16): 18 ft where truck traffic is anticipated; 16 ft for affirmatively non-truck driveways; 35 ft set-up area in front of AE equipment. Affects crane staging and tilt-up sequencing.

### Connectivity & frontage

- **Table B utility-in-drive-aisle option** (LDC Subchapter E § 2.3.1.B.2): on subject sites (≥3 ac nonresidential, or surface parking between building and principal street), site must select ≥2 Table B options (3 if parking >125% of formerly required). Routing utilities under parking stalls is only a deficiency if utility-in-drive-aisle is the selected option but not implemented, or if Table B count is otherwise short. Evaluate whether the site can hit its Table B count without forcing utilities under parking.

### Administrative & service-capacity

- **AE Service Availability Letter** (AEDC § 1.4.1) — only where it is unclear which utility serves the site. Confirm AE service area on edge-of-territory parcels before design.
- **Service capacity**: AE Design has sole authority over available voltage / service characteristics (AEDC § 1.3.2). For large loads (>320 A continuous → instrument-rated CT service per AEDC § 1.4.0; or any Network Area service downtown), engage AE Design early; available capacity at the nearest feeder may itself be a constraint.
- **Street lighting**: AE develops the lighting installation plan. Developer responsibilities differ by location (AEDC §§ 1.6.4–1.6.7). Inside the Great Streets boundary (MLK / Lady Bird Lake / IH-35 / Lamar), Chapter 6 dictates fixture type (Gardco Circa/Form 10; Kim ERA), spacing (8 poles/block), and mounting heights (24-ft street / 12-ft pedestrian) — non-standard poles permitted at developer cost differential.

# Floodplain & Waterway Protection Feasibility — Austin, TX

## Domain

Austin's FWP discipline encompasses three overlapping regulatory regimes that any waterway-adjacent or low-lying parcel must navigate: (1) federal FEMA SFHA / FIRM compliance, (2) the City of Austin's **stricter** fully-developed-conditions floodplain (with Atlas 14 rainfall data in updated watersheds), and (3) the environmental buffer system — Critical Water Quality Zone (CWQZ), Water Quality Transition Zone (WQTZ), Erosion Hazard Zone (EHZ), and Critical Environmental Feature (CEF) buffers — that surrounds classified waterways. Also in scope: floodplain modification analysis, no-rise certification for the COA floodway, finished floor elevation / freeboard, ASCE 24 structural compliance, watershed impervious cover limits, and the variance pathways (administrative, LUC, Council) that unlock relief.

Bridges to other disciplines: CWQZ overlaps with `el` (Environmental Landscape); impervious cover and water quality treatment overlap with `sde` (Site Drainage & Environmental); building elevations and FFE overlap with `sduf` (Site Development & Utilities Framework).

## Authoritative sources

- **FEMA FIRM panels** — current effective panels via msc.fema.gov; preliminary FIRMs if a watershed restudy is in progress
- **COA fully-developed 100-year floodplain** — derived from approved City regulatory hydraulic models intersected with site-specific topo (DCM 1.2.6.B); shown on COA GIS layer alongside FEMA
- **COA 25-year floodplain (= COA floodway)** — Atlas 14 areas: 25-yr fully developed; non-Atlas 14 areas: 100-yr fully developed pre-Atlas 14 (LDC § 25-12-52(11))
- **Land Development Code (LDC) Chapter 25-7** — Drainage / floodplain regulation (definitions § 25-7-2; calculation methods § 25-7-6; encroachment variances § 25-7-92; exceptions §§ 25-7-93, 25-7-95, 25-7-96; easement requirements § 25-7-152)
- **Land Development Code (LDC) Chapter 25-8** — Water Quality (CWQZ § 25-8-261; floodplain modification § 25-8-263; CWQZ uses § 25-8-281; cut/fill §§ 25-8-341 / 25-8-342; interbasin diversion § 25-8-365; admin variances § 25-8-42; LUC variances § 25-8-41)
- **LDC Chapter 25-12** — Floodplain administration (design flood elevation § 25-12-52; FFE / freeboard / floodproofing § 25-12-53; floodway no-rise / encroachment variances § 25-12-54)
- **Drainage Criteria Manual (DCM)** — Floodplain delineation methodology (§ 1.2.6); hydraulic study requirements (§§ 1.2.4–1.2.5); EHZ analysis procedure (Appendix E); Atlas 14 / TP40-TP49 (§ 2.3.1); dam safety (§ 8.3.3.B); culvert headwater limits (§ 1.2.4.C/D)
- **Environmental Criteria Manual (ECM)** — Floodplain modification criteria (§ 1.7); FAFH (§ 1.7.4 + App. X); restoration ratios (§ 1.7.5); CWQZ buffer averaging (§ 1.5.2.D); EARZ basin liners (§ 1.6.2.C); CEF setbacks (§ 1.10); admin variance form (§ 1.3.3)
- **Rule R161-20.01** — Atlas 14 compliance (effective 2019-11-25)
- **ASCE 24-14** — Flood Resistant Design and Construction (referenced by LDC § 25-12-53)
- **Property records** — recorded drainage easements, plat notes, prior CLOMR/LOMR documentation, prior variance approvals

## Regulatory pathway

| Pathway | Decision body | Typical timeline | When triggered |
|---|---|---|---|
| Floodplain Development Permit | WPD / DSD floodplain administrator | concurrent with site plan | Any development in or affecting the 100-yr or 25-yr floodplain |
| CLOMC / CLOMR (FEMA) | FEMA + COA acknowledgment | 6–12 months for review; CLOMC acknowledgment required **before preliminary plan or site plan permit** | Pre-construction map revision (e.g. fill, channel work that alters FEMA SFHA) |
| LOMR (FEMA) | FEMA | 6–12 months; final acceptance required **before CO** | Post-construction map revision |
| Administrative environmental variance (LDC § 25-8-42) | WPD Director, no hearing | weeks; ECM 1.3.3 form required | Enumerated items only: cut/fill 4–8 ft in DDZ, CEF buffer reduction, interbasin diversion below threshold, etc. |
| LUC environmental variance (LDC § 25-8-41) | Land Use Commission after Environmental Commission recommendation | 3–6 months | Cut/fill >8 ft, cut/fill in DWPZ, CWQZ encroachment, floodplain modification with adverse impact, slopes >15%, within 100 ft of classified waterway |
| Floodplain encroachment variance (LDC § 25-7-92) | Council (or LUC under some scenarios) | 6+ months | Buildings or parking in 25-yr or 100-yr floodplain not covered by §§ 25-7-93 / 25-7-96 exceptions |
| Floodway encroachment variance (LDC § 25-12-54) | Council | 6+ months; **cannot be granted if any flood-level rise results** (§ 25-12-54(F)(5)) | Any work in COA 25-yr floodplain (floodway) with rise |
| Save Our Springs (Article 13) | **No variance available** | — | Any project in the Barton Springs Zone — SOS is inviolable |

Project file must show CLOMC acknowledgment letter from FEMA **before** preliminary plan / site plan permit issues; LOMC acknowledgment **before** final acceptance / BP; LOMR final acceptance **before** CO.

## Constraints to evaluate

### Mapping & delineation

- **Two floodplains, not one.** Always map both the FEMA SFHA (copy directly from current FIRM shapefile per DCM 1.2.6.B — do not re-delineate to onsite topo) and the COA fully-developed 100-yr floodplain (derived from approved City hydraulic models intersected with site topo). For pre-feasibility, assume the COA boundary is larger than FEMA wherever Atlas 14 has been applied.
- **Hydraulic study trigger:** any creek, channel, or area of concentrated flow with ≥64 acres contributing drainage area requires a COA floodplain delineation (DCM 1.2.6.A.1). Below 64 acres, no COA floodplain is defined unless City or FEMA already mapped it.
- **Preliminary FIRM in process?** Check whether the watershed has a pending FEMA restudy. Using an effective FIRM when a preliminary is published is a common deficiency.

### Floodway (COA 25-yr) — the hardest constraint

- **0.00-ft rise standard.** Any encroachment in the COA 25-yr floodplain requires PE-certified zero rise, delivered as a **separate** sealed letter (LDC § 25-12-54(D)(11)) — not just the WSE comparison table.
- **Council cannot grant variance for floodway encroachment if any rise would result** (LDC § 25-12-54(F)(5)). Buildings, parking, or fill in the floodway with rise are categorically infeasible — design must avoid the floodway.

### 100-yr floodplain — buildings & parking

- Buildings and parking are prohibited in both 25-yr and 100-yr floodplains absent an enumerated exception (§ 25-7-93 for 100-yr; § 25-7-96 for 25-yr) or a Council encroachment variance (§ 25-7-92(C)) finding all seven criteria.
- **§ 25-7-93 exception conditions:** ≥2 ft above 100-yr WSE, volume compensation (compensatory storage), no additional adverse impact. Five enumerated categories (e.g. parking <5,000 sq ft with director "no adverse effect" determination).
- **Finished floor elevation:** minimum 2-ft freeboard above design flood elevation (LDC § 25-12-53(C)(1)). Design flood elevation = higher of Atlas 14 100-yr or FEMA 500-yr WSEL.
- **Safe access:** building access at or above 1 ft above DFE, equivalent to the Regulatory Flood Datum (LDC § 25-12-53(C)(4)(a)).
- **ASCE 24-14 certification** required for structures in the floodplain — separate engineer-sealed letter per structure type (retaining walls, fill, culverts, bridges, piers, fencing, buildings).
- **Below-grade structures, MEP equipment elevation, flood openings for enclosed areas, safe refuge space** — all separately addressed by LDC § 25-12-53.
- **Post-construction elevation certificate** (FEMA Form 086-0-33) by licensed surveyor — required prior to CO.

### Floodplain modification

- Any fill, grading, or channel work in the regulatory floodplain triggers LDC § 25-8-263 modification analysis: no-rise WSE, no increase in downstream peak flows, no loss of floodplain storage. WSE comparison table for 2/10/25/100-yr storms required.
- **Functional Assessment of Floodplain Health (FAFH)** per ECM 1.7.4 + Appendix X required for modifications. Zone-specific.
- **Restoration ratios (ECM 1.7.5):** Outside CWQZ (Zone 1): 2:1 / 3:1 / 4:1 for Poor / Fair / Good-or-Excellent condition (Good+ requires LUC variance). Inside CWQZ (Zone 2): 4:1 / 6:1 / 8:1 — all require LUC variance.
- **Note re ECM cross-reference:** ECM § 1.7.1 still references the repealed § 25-8-364; current governing provision is LDC § 25-8-263.

### Critical Water Quality Zone (CWQZ) — the buffer system

- **Suburban watersheds — fixed buffer widths from centerline:** 100 ft (minor, 64–320 ac); 200 ft (intermediate, 320–640 ac); 300 ft (major, >640 ac). Buffer averaging permitted per ECM 1.5.2.D.
- **CWQZ is largely undevelopable.** Most encroachments require an LUC variance under the enhanced § 25-8-41(B) standard (must prevent reasonable, economic use of the **entire** property).
- Ponds, fill, retaining walls, parking, buildings, and spray irrigation are prohibited in CWQZ outright in most cases. Trails permitted at ≥50 ft from CEF edge under § 25-8-281(C)(3) without variance.
- WQTZ is less restrictive but still constrains pond siting and stormwater controls.

### Erosion Hazard Zone (EHZ)

- EHZ analysis triggered when development is within 100 ft of a classified waterway centerline (≥64 acres drainage) or 200 ft of the Colorado River OHWM downstream of Longhorn Dam (LDC § 25-7-32(C)).
- Seven-step DCM Appendix E procedure: meander belt delineation (if sinuosity ≥1.2), bankfull geometry, incision depth, side slope projections to 100 ft max (steep terrain) or 20 ft min setback from tops of bank.
- WPD/ERM concurrence on protective works required.

1→# Transportation Access Feasibility — Austin, TX
     2→
     3→## Domain
     4→
     5→Right-of-way (existing + future per ASMP), traffic impact analysis (TIA / Transportation Assessment / NTA), driveway and access management, sidewalk + bike + transit obligations, street impact fees, and overlay-specific transportation rules (scenic roadways, Hill Country Roadway, TOD/NBG/ERC, Project Connect corridors).
     6→
     7→Excludes: parking ratio analysis (post-2023 Austin has no general parking minimums; accessible parking and bike parking still apply — covered briefly under Constraints), zoning entitlement (see `zlu.md`), and on-site civil grading (see `sde.md`).
     8→
     9→## Authoritative sources
    10→
    11→- **Austin Strategic Mobility Plan (ASMP)** — Street Network Table and Bicycle Priority Network (`atd.knack.com/asmp`). Assigns every street a Street Level (0–5) and a target ROW width from centerline. ASMP supersedes the legacy AMATP.
    12→- **Land Development Code (LDC) Chapter 25-6** — Transportation requirements: §§ 25-6-23 (proportionality), 25-6-51/54/55 (ROW reservation, alignment, dedication), 25-6-81 (waiver), 25-6-101 (mitigation), 25-6-111–117 (TIA), 25-6-114 (NTA), 25-6-354 (sidewalk fee-in-lieu), 25-6-471 (accessible parking), 25-6-477 (bicycle parking), 25-6-662/663/669 (Street Impact Fee).
    13→- **Transportation Criteria Manual (TCM)** — Section 2 (street design), 3 (intersections), 4 (sidewalks), 5 (bicycle facilities), 7 (driveways), 8 (TCP), 9 (parking / bus stops), 10 (TIA process and Table 10-6 nexus standards).
    14→- **TIA Guidelines** — Sections 2 (determination), 4 (scope), 5 (sub-threshold), 6 (compliance), 7 (NTA).
    15→- **TxDOT roadway inventory** — for ASMP Level 5 streets (freeways/interstates) and any IH/US/SH-prefixed roadway. Surveyor tool: `txdot_roadway_lookup` (functional class, lanes, AADT).
    16→- **Scenic Roadway designations** — LDC § 25-10-7 (the 23 enumerated scenic roadways) and LDC § 25-10-81(3) (Scenic Roadway Sign District). Note: the scenic roadway *sign* district is in Ch. 25-10; Hill Country Roadway *development* rules are at LDC §§ 25-2-1025 and 25-2-1127.
    17→- **Project Connect System Plan map** — Orange Line and other rail corridors. Not codified in Bureau; published by ATD/CapMetro.
    18→
    19→## Regulatory pathway
    20→
    21→| Trigger | Path | Typical timeline |
    22→|---|---|---|
    23→| Any new development on a street in the ASMP Street Network | TIA Determination Worksheet through TDS portal, signed by TDS Lead Development Review Engineer | 2–6 weeks |

# Transportation Access Feasibility — Austin, TX

## Domain

Excludes: parking ratio analysis (post-2023 Austin has no general parking minimums; accessible parking and bike parking still apply — covered briefly under Constraints), zoning entitlement (see `zlu.md`), and on-site civil grading (see `sde.md`).

## Authoritative sources

- **Austin Strategic Mobility Plan (ASMP)** — Street Network Table and Bicycle Priority Network (`atd.knack.com/asmp`). Assigns every street a Street Level (0–5) and a target ROW width from centerline. ASMP supersedes the legacy AMATP.
- **Land Development Code (LDC) Chapter 25-6** — Transportation requirements: §§ 25-6-23 (proportionality), 25-6-51/54/55 (ROW reservation, alignment, dedication), 25-6-81 (waiver), 25-6-101 (mitigation), 25-6-111–117 (TIA), 25-6-114 (NTA), 25-6-354 (sidewalk fee-in-lieu), 25-6-471 (accessible parking), 25-6-477 (bicycle parking), 25-6-662/663/669 (Street Impact Fee).
- **Transportation Criteria Manual (TCM)** — Section 2 (street design), 3 (intersections), 4 (sidewalks), 5 (bicycle facilities), 7 (driveways), 8 (TCP), 9 (parking / bus stops), 10 (TIA process and Table 10-6 nexus standards).
- **TIA Guidelines** — Sections 2 (determination), 4 (scope), 5 (sub-threshold), 6 (compliance), 7 (NTA).
- **TxDOT roadway inventory** — for ASMP Level 5 streets (freeways/interstates) and any IH/US/SH-prefixed roadway. Surveyor tool: `txdot_roadway_lookup` (functional class, lanes, AADT).
- **Scenic Roadway designations** — LDC § 25-10-7 (the 23 enumerated scenic roadways) and LDC § 25-10-81(3) (Scenic Roadway Sign District). Note: the scenic roadway *sign* district is in Ch. 25-10; Hill Country Roadway *development* rules are at LDC §§ 25-2-1025 and 25-2-1127.
- **Project Connect System Plan map** — Orange Line and other rail corridors. Not codified in Bureau; published by ATD/CapMetro.

## Regulatory pathway

| Trigger | Path | Typical timeline |
|---|---|---|
| Any new development on a street in the ASMP Street Network | TIA Determination Worksheet through TDS portal, signed by TDS Lead Development Review Engineer | 2–6 weeks |
| < 2,000 unadjusted daily trips | No TIA; sub-threshold mitigation may still apply (LDC § 25-6-101(B)) | concurrent with site plan |
| 2,000–4,999 unadjusted daily trips | Transportation Assessment + TDM Plan; TDS-approved scope first | 4–6 months end-to-end |
| ≥ 5,000 unadjusted daily trips | Full TIA + TDM Plan; TDS-approved scope first | 6–9 months end-to-end |
| Residential street access AND ≥ 300 net new daily trips (or any public K-12 school) | Neighborhood Traffic Analysis (NTA) — TDS staff write the memo; applicant submits 24-hr tube counts | 2–4 months |
| Street frontage on ASMP-designated street | ROW dedication (street deed or plat); City-issued proportionality memo required under § 25-6-23 | recordation before site plan approval |
| TxDOT-maintained frontage (IH, US, SH, Level 5) | TxDOT coordination letter / Approval Block; alignment set by TxDOT | additive 2–6 months |
| Frontage on Hill Country Roadway corridor | Hill Country Roadway development standards (LDC § 25-2 Subchapter C) overlay | concurrent with site plan |
| Site within 200 ft of any of the 23 Scenic Roadways OR 1,000 ft of a Hill Country Roadway | Scenic Roadway Sign District (LDC § 25-10-124) governs signage | concurrent with site plan |
| Site within an adopted regulating plan (NBG, ERC, MLK TOD, Plaza Saltillo, Lamar/Justin Lane) | Future street extension + frontage standards apply even before street is built | concurrent with site plan |
| Site along plausible Project Connect Orange Line alignment | Flag for ROW reservation up to 65 ft from centerline (130 ft total) — verify externally | additive coordination |

## Constraints to evaluate

### ROW dedication (existing vs. future)

- **Existing vs. future ROW is the single most important distinction.** Survey-confirmed existing ROW often differs from ASMP target width. Build-out massing and setback geometry must be measured from the *future* (ASMP) ROW line, not the curb or existing property line (LDC § 25-6-54(D)).
- Look up each frontage in the ASMP Street Network Table (`atd.knack.com/asmp`). Document Street Level (0–5) and target half-width.
  - Level 0 = alleys; Level 1 = local/residential collectors; Level 2 = collectors; Level 3 = minor/major arterials; Level 4 = principal/major arterials; Level 5 = TxDOT freeways/interstates.
- Compute the **dedication delta** (future half-width minus existing half-width). Multiply by frontage length to get area lost. Flag if delta > 10 ft on any frontage or if total area lost > 10% of gross site.
- Dedication is **roughly proportionate**; LDC § 25-6-23 requires a City-issued written proportionality determination signed by a City-retained PE before approval. Applicant-prepared SIF worksheets do not satisfy this requirement. Director may require less than full ASMP width but only via this memo.
- Dedication is by recorded **street deed** (metes + bounds + surveyor-sealed sketch, processed through City Legal) or, where ROW is held as easement only, by plat. Recordation must precede site plan approval; instrument number must appear on plan callouts.
- **TxDOT frontages (IH-35, US-290, SH-71, Parmer Lane, etc.)** carry long-term 400-ft ROW needs (200 ft from centerline). Either reserve up to 200 ft or obtain a TxDOT no-additional-dedication letter (LDC § 25-6-54(C)). TxDOT Approval Block required on the cover sheet when any work touches TxDOT ROW.
- **Orange Line corridor**: up to 65 ft from centerline (130 ft total) reservation may apply. Streets to flag include Guadalupe, Lavaca, Congress Ave. Not codified in Bureau — verify against Project Connect System Plan map.
- **Bicycle Priority Network**: streets on this network require All Ages and Abilities (AAA) facilities (Protected Bike Lanes, Shared Use Paths, or Neighborhood Bikeways per TCM 5.1.4); additional ROW beyond standard roadway width may be required.
- **Waiver**: LDC § 25-6-81 — formal written waiver required if full dedication is infeasible; available when ≥ 15% of property is subject to ROW reservation. An informal "infeasible" note on plans does **not** satisfy. ATD usually conditions waiver on a recorded alternative easement (sidewalk or public access).
- **IC math**: ROW pavement counts as IC; sidewalks in ROW or public easement are excluded (LDC § 25-8-63(C)(1)). On Hill Country Roadway sites, ROW > 60 ft from centerline counts in IC denominator (LDC § 25-2-1127), and 40% natural area is measured excluding dedicated ROW (LDC § 25-2-1025).

### TIA threshold and likely findings

- Threshold uses **unadjusted ITE daily trips** — no pass-by, internal capture, or TDM reductions for threshold determination. Only existing on-site occupied uses with documented occupancy may be subtracted.
- < 2,000 trips: no study, but sub-threshold mitigation (sidewalks, signals, traffic calming, bike lanes, RRFB/PHB, urban trails, ROW, TDM) within ¼ mile (or ¾ mile to schools/bus stops/major roads) can still be required under LDC § 25-6-101(B).
- 2,000–4,999 trips: **Transportation Assessment + TDM Plan** (LDC § 25-6-113; TCM 10.2.1).
- ≥ 5,000 trips: **Full TIA + TDM Plan**.
- All TIA work requires a **TDS-approved scope** signed by both the applicant's consultant and the TDS Lead Development Review Engineer *before* the study starts (TIA Guidelines § 4.3.2). Studies prepared without an approved scope will not be reviewed.
- Approved TIAs are valid **5 years** from final memo date or assumed build-out, whichever is earlier (TCM 10.4.3). Plan trip-budgeting accordingly.
- **TIA Compliance Letter** is a separate document from the TIA itself; if a prior TIA exists, expect a TIA Tracking Table on the cover sheet showing allowed/used/remaining VTDs and a 7-element compliance letter.
- **NTA** triggers when project accesses a non-arterial street with ≥ 50% SF-5+ frontage within 1,500 ft AND adds ≥ 300 net new daily trips (or is a public K-12). TDS writes the memo; applicant submits 24-hr tube counts.
- **Table 10-6** (TCM 10.4.4) sets nexus standards for required mitigations by category and study type — review before committing to off-site work.
- **Fiscal surety** under LDC § 25-1-112 must be posted before site plan approval for any unbuilt TIA-required improvements; below-market cost estimates without director approval will be rejected.

### Driveway and access management

- **Driveway type by use + street level** (TCM 7.3.1–7.3.2): Type I (residential) is **prohibited on ASMP Level 3 or 4 streets** regardless of use. Multi-family > 4 units requires Type II.
- **Max driveway width** (TCM 7.5.1.2, Table 7-2): Level 1 typical 20 ft (industrial 25 ft); Level 2 w/ 3-lane fire access 25 ft; high-capacity driveway serving a garage capped at 32 ft. Other Level 2/3/4 widths: verify against current TCM (Bureau data incomplete).
- **Driveway count per frontage** is capped; **opposing-driveway offset** rules can force right-in/right-out only.
- **Spacing minimums** from intersections, adjacent driveways, drainage inlets — confirm via TCM 7.6. Throat storage length per land use.
- **Joint-use driveway** requires a recorded easement with maintenance assigned (TCM 7.6.4) — built into the title package.
- **Hill Country Roadway** corridors (Loop 360 US-290W to US-183; RM 620 SH-71 to Anderson Mill; RM 2222 Highland Hills to RM 620; RM 2244 Loop 360 to SH-71; Southwest Parkway) impose extra access-spacing, grade, curve, and sight-distance restrictions (covered under guide 31).
- **Curb return radii** per TCM Table 7-1; downtown / ERC / UNO / NBG have overlay-specific values.

### Scenic Roadway constraints

- **Scenic Roadway Sign District** (LDC § 25-10-81(3); LDC § 25-10-124) — applies to land within **1,000 ft of a Hill Country Roadway corridor** OR **200 ft of any of the 23 Scenic Roadways** enumerated in LDC § 25-10-7 (e.g., Barton Springs Rd, Lake Austin Blvd, MoPac, Loop 360, RM 2222, RM 2244, William Cannon, Riverside Dr, SH 130). Governs sign size, height, lighting, setback.
- Historic and expressway sign districts override scenic per LDC § 25-10-82.
- Note: the user prompt referenced LDC § 25-2-871 (scenic roadway). The bureau guides cite § 25-10-7 / § 25-10-81 / § 25-10-124 for the **sign district**, and Hill Country Roadway development standards at LDC § 25-2-1025 / § 25-2-1127 for the *development* envelope. Confirm the controlling section against current code before drafting findings.
- For **Hill Country Roadway** sites the more material development constraints are the 40% natural-area requirement (excluding dedicated ROW; LDC § 25-2-1025), grade/cut-fill limits along the corridor, and ROW > 60 ft from centerline counting in IC denominator (LDC § 25-2-1127).

    22→|---|---|---|

    41→- **Is the parcel inside Austin Water's retail service area?** AW serves within its impact-fee boundary (UCM 2.2.1). Full-purpose annexation does not automatically mean AW is the retail provider. Common Austin-area alternatives:
    42→  - **Northtown MUD** (north Austin / Pflugerville fringe) — UCM 2.5.1.B requires its prior written approval before AW will sign anything.
    43→  - **Southwest Water / Mid-Tex** — west / southwest ETJ.
    44→  - **City of Manor** — eastern fringe.
    45→  - **WCIDs** — scattered (e.g., WCID 17 in westlake).

Triggers a Water SER under LDC § 25-9-33(A)(3). Not mappable from public data — confirm via AW correspondence.
    53→- **Pressure zone** must be designated on the AW General Info Sheet; affects pump sizing on tall buildings.

    60→- **Living Unit Equivalent (LUE)** = 1 residential dwelling = 245 gpd average flow (UCM 2.9.4.A.1). Commercial flows are calculated separately (70 gpd/capita or case-by-case). LUE counts must reconcile to the approved SER; exceeding triggers an SER revision (LDC § 25-9-39(C)(3)).

- Reclaimed / OWRS: LDC § 25-9-412 (mandatory connection); LDC § 25-9-414 + City Code § 15-13-7 (OWRS mandate, effective April 1, 2024).
- OSSF (septic) for parcels with no reachable public main: Austin City Code Chapter 15-5 (abandonment + within-corporate-limits OSSF); Travis County / Hays County / Williamson County permitting under TCEQ Chapter 285 in the ETJ.
- Industrial Waste Control Program (Chapter 15-10) — applies when AW is wastewater provider and discharge is non-domestic.
- Water Benchmarking Application (WBA/WBC): LDC § 25-9-413 (site plan submittal requirement).

## Regulatory pathway

| Action | Path / authority | Typical timing |
|---|---|---|
| Confirm service area + provider (AW vs MUD/WCID/CCN-holder) | AW GIS + PUC CCN map; LDC § 25-9-33(C)(2) | Day 0 (diligence) |
| Service availability letter (water + WW) | AW; must be dated within 6 months of review | 4-8 weeks |
| Pre-application meeting w/ AW for capacity questions | Informal; AWPE | 2-4 weeks lead |
| Service Extension Request (SER) — if triggered | LDC § 25-9-33; AW Pipeline Engineering (AWPE) | 3-9 months; approved SER is NOT a capacity reservation (UCM 2.2.3(E)) |
| WW SER multi-department review (AFD + Industrial Waste) | LDC § 25-9-33(C)(3), § 25-9-34(B) | Folded into SER timeline |
| Water Benchmarking Application (WBA/WBC) | LDC § 25-9-413(A); at site plan submittal | Concurrent with site plan |
| Large-development (GFA ≥ 250,000 SF) director consultation | LDC § 25-9-413(B) | Before site plan filing |
| AULCC (utility coordination) review for ROW work | UCM 3.2.0 | Plan set delivered 2 weeks before meeting |
| Reclaimed connection eligibility check (250 / 500 ft) | LDC § 25-9-412 | At concept; verify with AW Reclaimed Group |
| OWRS engineering report + permit (if mandated) | City Code § 15-13-7 / -10 / -11 | Adds ~6-12 mo; PE-stamped O&M manual |
| Tap permit issuance + capital recovery fee payment | LDC § 25-9-321; UCM 2.6.1 | At/before building permit |
| OSSF permit (ETJ, where no public main within 100 ft) | TCEQ Chapter 285 via county | Soil eval + 30-90 days |
| Easement recordation (if AW infrastructure outside ROW) | UCM 2.9.1.A.1-A.4; AWPE pre-recordation review | Before AW plan approval |

## Constraints to evaluate

### Service area + provider

- **Is the parcel inside Austin Water's retail service area?** AW serves within its impact-fee boundary (UCM 2.2.1). Full-purpose annexation does not automatically mean AW is the retail provider. Common Austin-area alternatives:
  - **Northtown MUD** (north Austin / Pflugerville fringe) — UCM 2.5.1.B requires its prior written approval before AW will sign anything.
  - **Southwest Water / Mid-Tex** — west / southwest ETJ.
  - **City of Manor** — eastern fringe.
  - **WCIDs** — scattered (e.g., WCID 17 in westlake).
- If a non-AW provider holds the CCN, expect a CCN release or transfer through PUC before AW can serve (LDC § 25-9-33(C)(2)). This adds 6-18 months and is not always achievable.
- If site is **inside the ETJ**, design must still meet COA standards but Industrial Waste plans go directly to the IW office, not through DSD (UCM 2.5.1.F).

### Capacity — water

- AW does **not** publish reservation; an approved SER is "acknowledgment of intent to serve" only (UCM 2.2.3(E)).
- **Pressure Concern Area** — administrative AW designation where existing infrastructure cannot maintain 20 psi residual at peak day + fire flow (UCM 2.9.2.A.3.d) or stays under 10 fps emergency velocity (UCM 2.9.2.A.3.c). Triggers a Water SER under LDC § 25-9-33(A)(3). Not mappable from public data — confirm via AW correspondence.
- **Pressure zone** must be designated on the AW General Info Sheet; affects pump sizing on tall buildings.
- Minimum public water main = 8 inches (UCM 2.9.2.A.4.a). Mains ≥24 inches are **transmission mains** (LDC § 25-9-32(15)) — no meter or fire-line tap permitted without a Director exception, even with an approved SER.
- Fire flow per FPCM Table 507-1: 1,000 gpm floor for SF < 3,600 SF; 2,500-3,500 gpm typical for multifamily / commercial. The 1,000 gpm number is a floor, not a default.

### Capacity — wastewater

- **Wastewater Capacity Concern Area** — administrative AW designation; not codified or mapped publicly. Triggers a WW SER under LDC § 25-9-33(A)(3). Confirm via AW correspondence; do not assume capacity from a 5-year-old AW master-plan study.
- **Living Unit Equivalent (LUE)** = 1 residential dwelling = 245 gpd average flow (UCM 2.9.4.A.1). Commercial flows are calculated separately (70 gpd/capita or case-by-case). LUE counts must reconcile to the approved SER; exceeding triggers an SER revision (LDC § 25-9-39(C)(3)).

# Parkland Dedication Feasibility — Austin

## Domain

Parkland dedication obligations, fee-in-lieu calculation, in-kind land dedication, public access easements, and on-site trail/recreation amenities required by City of Austin Parks and Recreation Department (PARD). Includes related instruments: Parkland Dedication Determination (formerly the PED letter), Parkland Improvement Agreements, fiscal surety, and Chapter 26 process when work touches existing City parkland.

Excludes: detailed trail design (covered by `ta` discipline for off-street network connectivity; on-site trail geometric design pulled from PARD/TCM is referenced here only as it bears on amenity cost and feasibility), and landscape/tree protection (covered by `el` discipline).

## Authoritative sources

- **Current ordinance:** Austin LDC Chapter 25-1, Article 14, §§ 25-1-601 through 25-1-612 (effective January 1, 2024 per Ord. 20231130-087, which fully repealed and renumbered the prior Article 14)
- **Operating procedures:** PDOP Rule R161-16.15 (uses pre-2024 LDC cross-references; cite by PDOP section, not embedded LDC numbers)
- **Determination:** LDC § 25-1-610 (Parkland Dedication Determination, replacing the informal "PED letter")
- **Construction on City parkland:** Texas Parks and Wildlife Code, Chapter 26, operationalized by ECM § 5.4.1
- **Fee schedule:** PARD annual fee schedule, updated October 1 each year. State formula set by Texas HB 1526 (2023); the City has no discretion over formula structure.
- **Urban trail design (if amenities include trail):** TCM § 5.3 and Standard Detail 1302S-1
- **District overlays:** ERC Regulating Plan § 4.10.3; NBG 3.5.8.D; LDC Subchapter E § 2.7 (private common open space) and § 2.3.1 (Table B connectivity)

## Regulatory pathway

Parkland dedication in Austin attaches at **site plan** (for multifamily and hotel/motel) and at **subdivision** (for single-family residential). Commercial, retail, and industrial uses are **not** subject to parkland dedication — the prior commercial requirement (Ord. 20220915-053) was repealed January 1, 2024. Civic uses (43 classifications in LDC § 25-2-6(B)) are also outside the scope of § 25-1-601(C).

Sequence:
1. **Pre-application:** Request a **Parkland Dedication Determination** from the PARD Director under LDC § 25-1-610. The Director specifies the satisfaction method (land, fee, easement, or combination), required acreage, preferred dedication location, off-site proximity limit, and any trail/connectivity conditions. Validity: lesser of 2 years (LDC § 25-1-610(D)) or 1 year (PDOP 14.3.5(B)) — assume 1 year. The Determination becomes stale if unit count changes by more than 10%.
2. **At site plan submittal:** Coversheet note must reference the Determination, current LDC Article 14, satisfaction method, unit counts, exempt units, and CO-timing for any unpaid multifamily fee.
3. **Before site plan release** (multifamily) **or final plat approval** (single-family): legal instruments executed — fee simple deed and ORS-coordinated transfer package; or recorded park easement; or recorded private parkland access easement under LDC § 25-1-605(E).
4. **Before CO** (multifamily): fee paid per LDC § 25-1-609(B).
5. **If construction touches existing City parkland:** Chapter 26 process (Parks Board hearing → City Council easement) plus PIA/PIMA — months-long timeline, not a paperwork item.

Decision body: PARD Director administers; Land Use Commission for Subchapter E waivers; City Council for Chapter 26 easements.

## Constraints to evaluate

### Applicability and exemptions

- **Use types subject:** residential dwelling units and hotel/motel rooms only. Verify all units are non-exempt before relying on a fee figure (LDC § 25-1-601(C)).
- **Exempt unit categories** (LDC § 25-1-601(D)): SMART Housing-certified units (D)(3); units income-restricted under any municipal/county/state/federal affordable housing program (D)(4) — broader than SMART, includes LIHTC, HUD Section 8, etc.; prior dedication credits (D)(1); Travis County ETJ (D)(2). The (D)(3) and (D)(4) exemptions are independent — a project may stack them across different units.
- **Site in ETJ:** parkland dedication does **not** apply at site plan stage (LDC § 25-1-601(D)(2)). Confirm jurisdictional status; sites that straddle city limits must address each portion separately.

### Calculation — multifamily

- Formula: `[(# MF units × 0.005) + (# hotel/motel rooms × 0.004)] × Avg Land Value × (1/Density Factor)` where Density Factor = 1 Suburban, 4 Urban, 40 CBD (LDC § 25-1-608).
- **Geographic Area designation is not self-selectable.** The Suburban/Urban/CBD boundary ordinance is not in Bureau. Confirm via the Determination letter or explicit PARD comment. Do **not** infer from neighborhood name or zoning.
- Land dedication cap: 10% of gross site area (LDC § 25-1-603(D)).
- Payment timing: **before CO**, not site plan release (LDC § 25-1-609(B)).
- Reference rates (per multifamily unit, FY 2025): CBD $2,427.65; Urban $4,676.52; Suburban $2,544.94. Rates update October 1 — verify current schedule before relying on these for pro forma.

### Calculation — single-family

- Density-based residents-per-unit multipliers (LDC § 25-1-602(C)): Low Density ≤6 DU/acre = 2.8; Medium 6–12 DU/acre = 2.2; High >12 DU/acre = 1.7.
- Urban Core single-family cap: **15% of gross site area** (LDC § 25-1-602(E)). This is a ceiling, not a minimum; formula amounts above 15% are converted to fee-in-lieu for the remainder.
- Two distinct single-family fees apply: fee-in-lieu (§ 25-1-606) and the parkland development fee (§ 25-1-607). Both due before plat/site plan approval.

### Land dedication — physical eligibility (PDOP § 14.3.7)

- **Minimum parcel size:** ¼ acre per dedicated parcel (§ 14.3.7(A)(7)(a)).
- **Visibility:** interior *should* be visible from public ROW — ≥200 ft frontage per 2 acres for parks ≥2 acres; ≥half the widest dimension for parks <2 acres (§ 14.3.7(A)(1); "should," not "shall").
- **Grade and active-play:** ≥50% *should* be ≤10% grade, well-drained, suitable for active play (§ 14.3.7(A)(2); "should"). Exception for trail connections or environmental/cultural resource preservation.
- **Utility connections (mandatory):** potable water on all park sites; sewer on sites ≥2 acres (§ 14.3.7(A)(4)).
- **Encumbrances (mandatory):** no recorded easement that prevents amenity construction (§ 14.3.7(A)(3)). AE electrical easements and utility easements within the parkland boundary are common disqualifiers. Transmission easement land cannot be labeled or dedicated as parkland (UCM § 1.14.7).

1→# Fire Feasibility — Austin, TX
     2→
     3→## Domain
     4→
     5→Fire department access (apparatus roads, turning, dead-ends, aerial operations), water supply for firefighting (hydrant coverage, spacing, fire flow at 20 psi residual, FDC siting), building code triggers (occupancy, construction type, high-rise classification at 75 ft, standpipe trigger at 30 ft), sprinkler-system selection (NFPA 13/13R/13D) and the fire-flow reductions they unlock, Wildland-Urban Interface (WUI) zoning, and the procedural pathway through Austin Fire Department (AFD) including AMOC pre-approvals. Bridges to: Austin Water (wwp/utilities — fire main capacity, hydrant taps), Transportation (driveway geometry, ASMP street level), and Zoning (high-rise massing implications).
     6→
     7→Scope excludes: building permit-stage sprinkler shop drawings, NFPA 13 hydraulic head calcs, fire alarm system design — those are post-site-plan deliverables. AFD WUI applies only within Full Purpose and Limited Purpose Jurisdiction; ETJ parcels are exempt from WUI but defer to the applicable county ESD for fire access.
     8→
     9→## Authoritative sources
    10→
    11→- **Fire code:** 2024 International Fire Code, adopted via LDC § 25-12-171 (Ord. 20250410-039, effective July 10, 2025). Submittals with original submission date before July 10, 2025 governed by 2021 IFC. Appendix D **not** adopted — apparatus access is governed by LDC § 25-12-173 §§ 503–507.5 with local amendments.
    12→- **Local amendments:** LDC § 25-12-173 (IFC), LDC § 25-12-183 (IWUIC), LDC § 25-12-1 (IBC). NFPA editions per LDC § 25-12-173 Chapter 80 (NFPA 13—2025, 14—2024, 20—2025, 24—2022, 72—2025, 855—2023).
    13→- **Fire Protection Criteria Manual (FPCM):** §§ 4.4.0 (general), 4.7.0 (NFPA 13), 4.8.0 (NFPA 14 / standpipes), 4.9.0 (NFPA 20 / pumps), 4.10.0 (WUI); Appendix E §§ 1.1.0, 2.1.0, 2.4.0, 3.2.x (submittal content).
    14→- **Utilities Criteria Manual (UCM):** § 2.9.2 (water/fire flow); UCM 2.9.2.D.1 (hydrant spacing); UCM 2.9.2.B.6 (fire line material, BFP, flow detection).
    15→- **Standard Specifications Manual (SSM):** Item 511.4.B (hydrant physical placement); Standards 901S-1, 901S-2, 901S-5, 901S-6 (apparatus access, turnarounds, fire-zone signs).
    16→- **Transportation Criteria Manual (TCM):** §§ 7.3, 7.5 (driveways serving fire lanes); ASMP Street Network Map for street-level lookup.
    17→- **Hydrant flow data:** AFD hydrant flow test report (Fire Marshal-witnessed; ≤1 year old). Fire Flow Map "Box" number on AW General Info & Construction Notes Sheet.
    18→- **WUI map:** 2024 WUI Code Map (dark blue/teal = Zones A & B combined; light blue = Zone C). Map does not distinguish A from B — AFD Wildfire Division field-measures.
    19→
    20→## Regulatory pathway
    21→
    22→Fire review runs **concurrently** with civil/site plan review through Development Services Department, but AFD has independent sign-off authority. Plans with fire lines additionally require both AFD and DSD approval before Austin Water Processing and Evaluation (AWPE) will approve (UCM 2.5.1.D).
    23→
    24→- **Pre-application:** AFD pre-app meeting strongly advisable for high-rise, podium, mixed-construction, WUI, alternative-surface fire lanes, or any site requiring an AMOC. AFD will not issue AMOC approval numbers during site plan cycle — AMOC must be a **separate standalone submittal**, approved before site plan submission.
    25→- **AMOC track (IFC § 104.8):** Required when standard IFC requirements cannot be met — most commonly to reduce minimum commercial fire flow below 1,500 gpm (floor: 1,000 gpm), reduce hydrant coverage, or approve pyrophoric gas storage. AMOC must be pre-approved with an AFD-issued approval number and date noted in the AFD Fire Analysis Table. "Pending"/"submitted" entries are deficient.
    26→- **WUI track (FPCM 4.10.0):** Concurrent review by AFD Wildfire Division. Required for any property within Full/Limited Purpose Jurisdiction that the 2024 WUI Code Map covers or that AFD Wildfire designates. Separate WUI approval stamp required before final site plan approval. Map status is rebuttable only by AFD Wildfire Division — self-declared "not in WUI" is a deficiency.
    27→- **High-rise track (IBC § 202 via LDC § 25-12-1):** Any occupied floor >75 ft above the lowest level of fire department vehicle access triggers IBC § 403 high-rise requirements: Fire Command Center (1-hr fire barrier; exterior access or 2-hr rated passageway; FPCM Appendix E § 3.2.13 equipment list), dual remote FDCs (NFPA 14 § 7.12.2), fire pump room, dual water mains (UCM 2.9.2.A.3.e), AEDs each occupied level, simultaneous stairway-unlock controls (LDC § 25-12-173 § 508.1.6). For buildings >420 ft, mains must be in **different streets** (IFC § 914.3.1.2). Buildings between ~65–75 ft must carry three pre-CO survey notes (ZLU-29.10/.11/.12).
    28→- **Decision body:** Fire Marshal's office; Wildfire Division (for WUI); final sign-off on cover sheet approval block.
    29→- **Timeline reality:** AMOC review adds ~6–12 weeks before site plan submission becomes viable. WUI concurrent review rarely controls the critical path. High-rise pre-app + dual-main coordination with Austin Water can add 1–2 cycles. Any post-approval change to fire lanes, hydrants, FDCs, fire service routing, riser/pump rooms, or electric disconnect requires AFD resubmission.
    30→
    31→## Constraints to evaluate
    32→
    33→**Apparatus access (LDC § 25-12-173 §§ 503.1.1, 503.2.1, 503.2.4 with City amendments; Appendix D not adopted).**
    34→- Fire apparatus access road within **150 ft** (path-of-travel, not arc) of all portions of all exterior walls of the first story. AFD routinely extends to **200 ft** for buildings fully sprinklered per NFPA 13 (not 13R/13D) under Exception 1.1, but the increase is **discretionary** — plans showing 200 ft must reflect AFD authorization; high-piled combustible storage buildings (>12,000 sf area + storage >12 ft height) are locked at 150 ft regardless of sprinklers (IFC § 3206.6). High-piled storage also requires one FD access door per 100 LF of exterior wall facing the access road, max 125 ft center-to-center (IFC § 3206.6.1, § 3206.7.5).
    35→- Measurement: actual ground-level path around obstructions ≥4 ft tall (buildings, walls, fences, grade changes); never through/under buildings; never across water-quality features; AFD will not lay supply hose across ASMP Level 3+ arterials, expressways, parkways, freeways, or toll roads. Routes that cross property lines require a recorded **JUAE or UDA** (§ 503.1.1 Exception 3).
    36→- **Minimum unobstructed width 25 ft** face-of-curb to face-of-curb (sidewalk does not count); 14 ft minimum vertical clearance for the full width; **inside turning radius 25 ft / outside 50 ft** (§ 503.2.4). Wider than 25 ft lanes may reduce to 20-in/40-out. Divided fire lanes where aerial is not anticipated: two 15-ft lanes (Exception 2.d). Security gates: 25 ft two-way / 15 ft one-way (20 ft two-way only with prior Fire Prevention Division written approval). Throat at Level 1/2 street crosswalk: 20 ft permitted (Exception 2.e). Curb-return radii at fire-access driveways from public streets follow TCM 7.5.1.1 Table 7-1 "Fire Access" column — typically 15 ft on Level 1/2 streets (vs. 10 ft typical). Turning movements onto opposing traffic lanes or where ASMP proposes a raised median are prohibited.
    37→- **Grade:** asphalt ≤ 13%; concrete ≤ 15%; maximum 10% change in any 20 ft; aerial setup areas ≤ ~12–13% running and 3.5% cross-slope; driveway grade change in a fire lane ≤ 6% (TCM 7.5.2.1.E, more restrictive). Where max grades cannot be met, a fully protected sprinkler system approved by AFD may substitute. Minimum drainage: 2% vegetated / alternative; 1% asphalt; 0.5% concrete.
    38→- **Surface:** HS-20 loading (16 kips/wheel, 80,000 lbs total) for all fire lanes and all structural elements within them (manhole covers, vault lids, trench grates). Final asphalt/concrete must be in place before combustible construction begins. Alternative surfaces (grasscrete, pavers, PICP, porous asphalt/concrete) limited to ≤25% of building-perimeter fire protection, require slip-resistant surfaces at turns and 40 LF at building corners for aerial operations, reinforced mountable curb when no Type I/II apron is present, and a post-completion PE-of-record concurrence letter (§ 503.2.3.1). Pervious or decorative paving **within 100 ft of any building** requires AFD approval + PE design for 80,000 lb live load even when not formally a fire lane.
    39→
    40→**Aerial apparatus (LDC § 25-12-173 § 503.2.6.1; AFD operational practice).**
    41→- Aerial-clearance review begins at ~73 ft per AFD practice (2 ft before the 75-ft high-rise threshold). For high-rise and near-high-rise buildings, plans must demonstrate clear staging adjacent to the building face — typically a 25-ft setback envelope plus overhead clearance for the boom. Divided 15-ft lanes are not permitted where aerial deployment is expected; full 25-ft lane required.
    42→- Elevated surfaces (podium slabs, plaza decks) that serve as fire apparatus access must be designed for the greater of IFC § 503.2.6 apparatus loads or IBC § 1607.8.1 live load (LDC § 25-12-3 § 1607.8.2). **Outrigger loads:** **43,200 lbs on one outrigger** or **28,600 lbs each on two adjacent outriggers** at 18-ft center spacing on 24"×24" contact (§ 503.2.6.1). Engineer of record must sign a post-completion concurrence letter. Access hatches, vault covers, and trench grates in the apparatus path must individually carry the 43,200-lb single-outrigger rating.
    43→- Bridges/elevated fire lane crossings: AASHTO HB-17 (or current LRFD) design; load-limit signs at both entrances (§ 503.2.6).
    44→
    45→**Dead-ends and turnarounds.**
    46→- Dead-end fire lane >150 ft requires a turnaround per Standard 901S-2: cul-de-sac with 50-ft unobstructed radius **or** hammerhead/T 25 ft × 80 ft with 10 ft additional clearance and no obstructions over 1 ft (FPCM 4.4.0).
    47→- Turnaround pavement must be marked fire lane on all sides; hose-lay extension from the turnaround counts toward apparatus-to-building distance.
    48→
    49→**Hydrant coverage and spacing (LDC § 25-12-173 § 507.5.1; UCM § 2.9.2.D).**
    50→- Primary hydrant hose-lay to all exterior walls: **400 ft** non-sprinklered (non-R-3/U); **500 ft** for buildings sprinklered throughout per NFPA 13 or 13R; **600 ft** for Group R-3 and U regardless of sprinklers.
    51→- **Second hydrant within 500 ft (600 ft for R-3/U) when required fire flow ≥1,500 gpm; additional hydrants within 1,000 ft when fire flow >2,500 gpm. One hydrant per 1,250 gpm (or fraction).** Multi-hydrant calcs must show all required hydrants flowing simultaneously, starting at the most hydraulically remote.
    52→- **Spacing:** **300 ft** maximum interval in commercial/high-density areas (CBD, DMU, W/LO, CS, CH, MF-4/5/6, or inside the Downtown Austin Project Coordination Zone); **600 ft** max interval elsewhere; hydrant at every major intersection; hydrants on **both sides** of any divided road regardless of arterial class (UCM 2.9.2.D.2).
    53→- **Placement (SSM 511.4.B):** 3–6 ft behind curb gutter face; steamer center ≥18 in above grade; steamer perpendicular to and facing the curb/fire lane; ≥20 ft from curb tangency at corners; ≥9 ft (any direction) from sanitary sewer line/lateral/service/manhole (UCM 2.9.2.D.4); ≥5 ft from storm drain; ≥3 ft clear circumference; bollards where exposed to vehicles; lead line ≤55 ft from main and cannot cross a divided road.
    54→- **Field-verified fire flow test:** AFD-conducted or AFD-witnessed only (IFC § 507.4 as locally amended); ≤1 year old at site-plan submission; on hydrants on the same main/zone serving the connection point; full FPCM Appendix E § 2.4.0 data set (static, residual, pitot, flow rate, hydrant IDs, date/time, conductor, equipment, gauge elevations).
    55→- **Required fire flow at 20 psi residual** from IFC Appendix B Table B105.1(2) using IBC construction type + fire-flow calculation area per LDC § 25-12-173 B104.1. Commercial floor: 1,500 gpm (reducible to 1,000 gpm only with pre-approved AMOC). Sprinkler reductions per Table B105.2: NFPA 13 → 75%; NFPA 13R → 50% (capped at 50% for Type III/IV/V); NFPA 13D → 25%. **No reduction** for Group H or S-1/S-2 with high-piled or rack storage.
    56→- Hydraulic calc C-factors are fixed by FPCM 4.4.0 Table 507-2: C=80 (iron/steel) or C=110 (plastic/copper) — software defaults of 140/150 are non-compliant. **Velocity ≤10 fps** upstream of the 6-in hydrant tap; the 6-in lead downstream is the only velocity exception.
    57→
    58→**FDC siting (IFC § 912; LDC § 25-12-173 § 912.5; NFPA 14 § 6.4.5.4).**
    59→- Each separate sprinkler or standpipe system requires its own FDC (NFPA 13D excluded; stand-alone local <20-head systems excluded per FPCM 4.7.0). Street side, oriented to fire apparatus access, fully visible. Prohibited: under building overhangs, inside parking garages (even sprinklered), behind walls/fences, in 100-yr floodplain, in covered courtyards.
    60→- **FDC-to-hydrant travel distance:** **100 ft** for standpipe systems (NFPA 14 § 6.4.5.4); **300 ft** for sprinklered buildings without Class I standpipe (IFC § 507.5.1.1). Working space: 36 in W × 36 in D × 78 in H; mounting 18–48 in above grade.
