# Fire Feasibility — Austin, TX

## Domain

Fire department access (apparatus roads, turning, dead-ends, aerial operations), water supply for firefighting (hydrant coverage, spacing, fire flow at 20 psi residual, FDC siting), building code triggers (occupancy, construction type, high-rise classification at 75 ft, standpipe trigger at 30 ft), sprinkler-system selection (NFPA 13/13R/13D) and the fire-flow reductions they unlock, Wildland-Urban Interface (WUI) zoning, and the procedural pathway through Austin Fire Department (AFD) including AMOC pre-approvals. Bridges to: Austin Water (wwp/utilities — fire main capacity, hydrant taps), Transportation (driveway geometry, ASMP street level), and Zoning (high-rise massing implications).

Scope excludes: building permit-stage sprinkler shop drawings, NFPA 13 hydraulic head calcs, fire alarm system design — those are post-site-plan deliverables. AFD WUI applies only within Full Purpose and Limited Purpose Jurisdiction; ETJ parcels are exempt from WUI but defer to the applicable county ESD for fire access.

## Authoritative sources

- **Fire code:** 2024 International Fire Code, adopted via LDC § 25-12-171 (Ord. 20250410-039, effective July 10, 2025). Submittals with original submission date before July 10, 2025 governed by 2021 IFC. Appendix D **not** adopted — apparatus access is governed by LDC § 25-12-173 §§ 503–507.5 with local amendments.
- **Local amendments:** LDC § 25-12-173 (IFC), LDC § 25-12-183 (IWUIC), LDC § 25-12-1 (IBC). NFPA editions per LDC § 25-12-173 Chapter 80 (NFPA 13—2025, 14—2024, 20—2025, 24—2022, 72—2025, 855—2023).
- **Fire Protection Criteria Manual (FPCM):** §§ 4.4.0 (general), 4.7.0 (NFPA 13), 4.8.0 (NFPA 14 / standpipes), 4.9.0 (NFPA 20 / pumps), 4.10.0 (WUI); Appendix E §§ 1.1.0, 2.1.0, 2.4.0, 3.2.x (submittal content).
- **Utilities Criteria Manual (UCM):** § 2.9.2 (water/fire flow); UCM 2.9.2.D.1 (hydrant spacing); UCM 2.9.2.B.6 (fire line material, BFP, flow detection).
- **Standard Specifications Manual (SSM):** Item 511.4.B (hydrant physical placement); Standards 901S-1, 901S-2, 901S-5, 901S-6 (apparatus access, turnarounds, fire-zone signs).
- **Transportation Criteria Manual (TCM):** §§ 7.3, 7.5 (driveways serving fire lanes); ASMP Street Network Map for street-level lookup.
- **Hydrant flow data:** AFD hydrant flow test report (Fire Marshal-witnessed; ≤1 year old). Fire Flow Map "Box" number on AW General Info & Construction Notes Sheet.
- **WUI map:** 2024 WUI Code Map (dark blue/teal = Zones A & B combined; light blue = Zone C). Map does not distinguish A from B — AFD Wildfire Division field-measures.

## Regulatory pathway

Fire review runs **concurrently** with civil/site plan review through Development Services Department, but AFD has independent sign-off authority. Plans with fire lines additionally require both AFD and DSD approval before Austin Water Processing and Evaluation (AWPE) will approve (UCM 2.5.1.D).

- **Pre-application:** AFD pre-app meeting strongly advisable for high-rise, podium, mixed-construction, WUI, alternative-surface fire lanes, or any site requiring an AMOC. AFD will not issue AMOC approval numbers during site plan cycle — AMOC must be a **separate standalone submittal**, approved before site plan submission.
- **AMOC track (IFC § 104.8):** Required when standard IFC requirements cannot be met — most commonly to reduce minimum commercial fire flow below 1,500 gpm (floor: 1,000 gpm), reduce hydrant coverage, or approve pyrophoric gas storage. AMOC must be pre-approved with an AFD-issued approval number and date noted in the AFD Fire Analysis Table. "Pending"/"submitted" entries are deficient.
- **WUI track (FPCM 4.10.0):** Concurrent review by AFD Wildfire Division. Required for any property within Full/Limited Purpose Jurisdiction that the 2024 WUI Code Map covers or that AFD Wildfire designates. Separate WUI approval stamp required before final site plan approval. Map status is rebuttable only by AFD Wildfire Division — self-declared "not in WUI" is a deficiency.
- **High-rise track (IBC § 202 via LDC § 25-12-1):** Any occupied floor >75 ft above the lowest level of fire department vehicle access triggers IBC § 403 high-rise requirements: Fire Command Center (1-hr fire barrier; exterior access or 2-hr rated passageway; FPCM Appendix E § 3.2.13 equipment list), dual remote FDCs (NFPA 14 § 7.12.2), fire pump room, dual water mains (UCM 2.9.2.A.3.e), AEDs each occupied level, simultaneous stairway-unlock controls (LDC § 25-12-173 § 508.1.6). For buildings >420 ft, mains must be in **different streets** (IFC § 914.3.1.2). Buildings between ~65–75 ft must carry three pre-CO survey notes (ZLU-29.10/.11/.12).
- **Decision body:** Fire Marshal's office; Wildfire Division (for WUI); final sign-off on cover sheet approval block.
- **Timeline reality:** AMOC review adds ~6–12 weeks before site plan submission becomes viable. WUI concurrent review rarely controls the critical path. High-rise pre-app + dual-main coordination with Austin Water can add 1–2 cycles. Any post-approval change to fire lanes, hydrants, FDCs, fire service routing, riser/pump rooms, or electric disconnect requires AFD resubmission.

## Constraints to evaluate

**Apparatus access (LDC § 25-12-173 §§ 503.1.1, 503.2.1, 503.2.4 with City amendments; Appendix D not adopted).**
- Fire apparatus access road within **150 ft** (path-of-travel, not arc) of all portions of all exterior walls of the first story. AFD routinely extends to **200 ft** for buildings fully sprinklered per NFPA 13 (not 13R/13D) under Exception 1.1, but the increase is **discretionary** — plans showing 200 ft must reflect AFD authorization; high-piled combustible storage buildings (>12,000 sf area + storage >12 ft height) are locked at 150 ft regardless of sprinklers (IFC § 3206.6). High-piled storage also requires one FD access door per 100 LF of exterior wall facing the access road, max 125 ft center-to-center (IFC § 3206.6.1, § 3206.7.5).
- Measurement: actual ground-level path around obstructions ≥4 ft tall (buildings, walls, fences, grade changes); never through/under buildings; never across water-quality features; AFD will not lay supply hose across ASMP Level 3+ arterials, expressways, parkways, freeways, or toll roads. Routes that cross property lines require a recorded **JUAE or UDA** (§ 503.1.1 Exception 3).
- **Minimum unobstructed width 25 ft** face-of-curb to face-of-curb (sidewalk does not count); 14 ft minimum vertical clearance for the full width; **inside turning radius 25 ft / outside 50 ft** (§ 503.2.4). Wider than 25 ft lanes may reduce to 20-in/40-out. Divided fire lanes where aerial is not anticipated: two 15-ft lanes (Exception 2.d). Security gates: 25 ft two-way / 15 ft one-way (20 ft two-way only with prior Fire Prevention Division written approval). Throat at Level 1/2 street crosswalk: 20 ft permitted (Exception 2.e). Curb-return radii at fire-access driveways from public streets follow TCM 7.5.1.1 Table 7-1 "Fire Access" column — typically 15 ft on Level 1/2 streets (vs. 10 ft typical). Turning movements onto opposing traffic lanes or where ASMP proposes a raised median are prohibited.
- **Grade:** asphalt ≤ 13%; concrete ≤ 15%; maximum 10% change in any 20 ft; aerial setup areas ≤ ~12–13% running and 3.5% cross-slope; driveway grade change in a fire lane ≤ 6% (TCM 7.5.2.1.E, more restrictive). Where max grades cannot be met, a fully protected sprinkler system approved by AFD may substitute. Minimum drainage: 2% vegetated / alternative; 1% asphalt; 0.5% concrete.
- **Surface:** HS-20 loading (16 kips/wheel, 80,000 lbs total) for all fire lanes and all structural elements within them (manhole covers, vault lids, trench grates). Final asphalt/concrete must be in place before combustible construction begins. Alternative surfaces (grasscrete, pavers, PICP, porous asphalt/concrete) limited to ≤25% of building-perimeter fire protection, require slip-resistant surfaces at turns and 40 LF at building corners for aerial operations, reinforced mountable curb when no Type I/II apron is present, and a post-completion PE-of-record concurrence letter (§ 503.2.3.1). Pervious or decorative paving **within 100 ft of any building** requires AFD approval + PE design for 80,000 lb live load even when not formally a fire lane.

**Aerial apparatus (LDC § 25-12-173 § 503.2.6.1; AFD operational practice).**
- Aerial-clearance review begins at ~73 ft per AFD practice (2 ft before the 75-ft high-rise threshold). For high-rise and near-high-rise buildings, plans must demonstrate clear staging adjacent to the building face — typically a 25-ft setback envelope plus overhead clearance for the boom. Divided 15-ft lanes are not permitted where aerial deployment is expected; full 25-ft lane required.
- Elevated surfaces (podium slabs, plaza decks) that serve as fire apparatus access must be designed for the greater of IFC § 503.2.6 apparatus loads or IBC § 1607.8.1 live load (LDC § 25-12-3 § 1607.8.2). **Outrigger loads:** **43,200 lbs on one outrigger** or **28,600 lbs each on two adjacent outriggers** at 18-ft center spacing on 24"×24" contact (§ 503.2.6.1). Engineer of record must sign a post-completion concurrence letter. Access hatches, vault covers, and trench grates in the apparatus path must individually carry the 43,200-lb single-outrigger rating.
- Bridges/elevated fire lane crossings: AASHTO HB-17 (or current LRFD) design; load-limit signs at both entrances (§ 503.2.6).

**Dead-ends and turnarounds.**
- Dead-end fire lane >150 ft requires a turnaround per Standard 901S-2: cul-de-sac with 50-ft unobstructed radius **or** hammerhead/T 25 ft × 80 ft with 10 ft additional clearance and no obstructions over 1 ft (FPCM 4.4.0).
- Turnaround pavement must be marked fire lane on all sides; hose-lay extension from the turnaround counts toward apparatus-to-building distance.

**Hydrant coverage and spacing (LDC § 25-12-173 § 507.5.1; UCM § 2.9.2.D).**
- Primary hydrant hose-lay to all exterior walls: **400 ft** non-sprinklered (non-R-3/U); **500 ft** for buildings sprinklered throughout per NFPA 13 or 13R; **600 ft** for Group R-3 and U regardless of sprinklers.
- **Second hydrant within 500 ft (600 ft for R-3/U) when required fire flow ≥1,500 gpm; additional hydrants within 1,000 ft when fire flow >2,500 gpm. One hydrant per 1,250 gpm (or fraction).** Multi-hydrant calcs must show all required hydrants flowing simultaneously, starting at the most hydraulically remote.
- **Spacing:** **300 ft** maximum interval in commercial/high-density areas (CBD, DMU, W/LO, CS, CH, MF-4/5/6, or inside the Downtown Austin Project Coordination Zone); **600 ft** max interval elsewhere; hydrant at every major intersection; hydrants on **both sides** of any divided road regardless of arterial class (UCM 2.9.2.D.2).
- **Placement (SSM 511.4.B):** 3–6 ft behind curb gutter face; steamer center ≥18 in above grade; steamer perpendicular to and facing the curb/fire lane; ≥20 ft from curb tangency at corners; ≥9 ft (any direction) from sanitary sewer line/lateral/service/manhole (UCM 2.9.2.D.4); ≥5 ft from storm drain; ≥3 ft clear circumference; bollards where exposed to vehicles; lead line ≤55 ft from main and cannot cross a divided road.
- **Field-verified fire flow test:** AFD-conducted or AFD-witnessed only (IFC § 507.4 as locally amended); ≤1 year old at site-plan submission; on hydrants on the same main/zone serving the connection point; full FPCM Appendix E § 2.4.0 data set (static, residual, pitot, flow rate, hydrant IDs, date/time, conductor, equipment, gauge elevations).
- **Required fire flow at 20 psi residual** from IFC Appendix B Table B105.1(2) using IBC construction type + fire-flow calculation area per LDC § 25-12-173 B104.1. Commercial floor: 1,500 gpm (reducible to 1,000 gpm only with pre-approved AMOC). Sprinkler reductions per Table B105.2: NFPA 13 → 75%; NFPA 13R → 50% (capped at 50% for Type III/IV/V); NFPA 13D → 25%. **No reduction** for Group H or S-1/S-2 with high-piled or rack storage.
- Hydraulic calc C-factors are fixed by FPCM 4.4.0 Table 507-2: C=80 (iron/steel) or C=110 (plastic/copper) — software defaults of 140/150 are non-compliant. **Velocity ≤10 fps** upstream of the 6-in hydrant tap; the 6-in lead downstream is the only velocity exception.

**FDC siting (IFC § 912; LDC § 25-12-173 § 912.5; NFPA 14 § 6.4.5.4).**
- Each separate sprinkler or standpipe system requires its own FDC (NFPA 13D excluded; stand-alone local <20-head systems excluded per FPCM 4.7.0). Street side, oriented to fire apparatus access, fully visible. Prohibited: under building overhangs, inside parking garages (even sprinklered), behind walls/fences, in 100-yr floodplain, in covered courtyards.
- **FDC-to-hydrant travel distance:** **100 ft** for standpipe systems (NFPA 14 § 6.4.5.4); **300 ft** for sprinklered buildings without Class I standpipe (IFC § 507.5.1.1). Working space: 36 in W × 36 in D × 78 in H; mounting 18–48 in above grade.

1→# Erosion, Trees & Plants Feasibility — Austin, TX
     2→
     3→## Domain
     4→
     5→Tree protection, erosion and sedimentation control (ESC), vegetation removal, heritage tree rules, root zone protection, landscape compliance, Critical Environmental Features (CEFs), and revegetation. Bridges with `el` (Environmental Layers: floodplain, CWQZ, BSZ pollutant loading) at the CEF/wetland boundary and with `sde` (Site Drainage/Engineering) at grading, utility, and SCM planting interfaces.
     6→
     7→## Authoritative sources
     8→
     9→- Tree ordinance: Austin LDC § 25-8 Subchapter B Article 2 (Trees), §§ 25-8-601 through 25-8-646
    10→- Tree survey & preservation standards: ECM Section 3.3 (tree survey) and ECM Section 3.5.2 (preservation criteria, restated in entirety by Rule R161-22.16, December 14, 2022)
    11→- Heritage species list: LDC § 25-8-602(1) — Texas Ash, Bald Cypress, American Elm, Cedar Elm, Texas Madrone, Bigtooth Maple, all Oaks, Pecan, Arizona Walnut, Eastern Black Walnut
    12→- Mitigation rates and methods: ECM § 3.5.4 (and Appendix F species list)
    13→- Tree protection details: ECM § 3.6.1 and SSM Item No. 610
    14→- Erosion / sediment control: LDC § 25-8-181, ECM Section 1.4 (and Appendices P-1, P-3, P-4)
    15→- Landscape and parking lot tree requirements: LDC § 25-2-1001 et seq.; ECM Section 2
    16→- Native tree replacement (Hill Country Roadway Corridor only): LDC § 25-2-1022 / 1025; corridor defined at LDC § 25-2-1103
    17→- Critical Environmental Features and ERI: LDC § 25-8-1(6), § 25-8-121, § 25-8-281(C); ECM §§ 1.3.0, 1.10.3, 1.10.4
    18→- Save Our Springs Ordinance (BSZ): LDC §§ 25-8-481, 25-8-514, 25-8-515, 25-8-516
    19→
    20→## Regulatory pathway
    21→
    22→| Trigger | Path | Decision body | Typical timeline |
    23→|---|---|---|---|
    24→| Any regulated tree (≥ 8" DBH) on site, on adjacent property with CRZ entering LOC, or in adjacent ROW | RPLS-certified tree survey + tree protection plan with site plan submittal | DSD City Arborist | Included in site plan cycle |
    25→| Protected tree (≥ 19" DBH, any species) proposed for removal | Removal permit with documentation of one of six LDC § 25-8-624(A) criteria | City Arborist | Concurrent with site plan |
    26→| Heritage tree (≥ 24" DBH + listed species), no stem ≥ 30" | Administrative Variance under LDC § 25-8-642; requires § 25-8-646 prerequisite-variance exhaustion (unless DDI) | DSD Director on City Arborist recommendation | ~2–4 months including pre-meeting + fiscal posting |
    27→| Heritage tree with at least one stem ≥ 30" | Land Use Commission variance with Environmental Commission review under LDC § 25-8-643 | LUC + EC | ~4–8 months; public hearings |
    28→| DDI (dead/diseased/imminent hazard) heritage tree | Administrative variance still required, but no fee and 0% mitigation — City Arborist letter (not private arborist alone) determines DDI | City Arborist + Director | ~1–2 months |
    29→| LOC > 25 acres OR any LOC in Barton Springs Zone | Phased ESC plan required (ECM 1.4.4.B.5.I.a; LDC § 25-8-184); BSZ adds 18-month clearing-to-revegetation cap | DSD Environmental | Within site plan cycle |
    30→| Site in EARZ, contains slope > 15%, contains CWQZ, or within 150 ft of mapped wetland | Environmental Resource Inventory (ERI) with three sub-reports (Hydrogeologic, Vegetation, Wastewater); 7-year validity | WPD | 2–4 months for field work + sealed report |
    31→| Karst feature (cave, sinkhole, fault, fracture) over EARZ | 50-ft walking transect karst survey by Texas Licensed Professional Geoscientist (ECM 1.10.3); 150–300 ft buffer to catchment | WPD | Adds 1–3 months |
    32→| Wetland CEF on or within 150 ft of site | 150-ft buffer; reducible to 50-ft avg via 1:1 in-kind on-site mitigation (ECM 1.10.4(D)(2)–(3)) | WPD | 2–4 months |
    33→| Hill Country Roadway Corridor (within 1,000 ft of Loop 360, RM 620, RM 2222, RM 2244, or Southwest Pkwy) | Native tree replacement (LDC § 25-2-1022) + 40% natural-area set-aside (LDC § 25-2-1025) | DSD | Constrains massing from concept stage |
    34→
    35→## Constraints to evaluate
    36→
    37→**Tree inventory and survey**
    38→- All trees ≥ 8" DBH must be surveyed by an RPLS within 5 years of submittal (ECM 3.3.1.A; ECM 3.3.2.A). Off-site and ROW trees count if their CRZ reaches the LOC — a 30-inch tree 28 ft beyond the boundary still triggers survey because its 30-ft CRZ enters the site (ECM 3.3.2.A.1).
    39→- Heritage trees (≥ 24" DBH + listed species) must be marked "H"; protected trees (≥ 19" DBH any species) annotated. Multi-trunk DBH formula: largest stem + ½ each additional stem ≥ 1" (ECM 3.3.2.A.2).
    40→- For initial diligence, satellite imagery is not a substitute — DBH cannot be inferred from canopy and field survey is the precondition to any reliable site plan. Budget RPLS + ISA-certified arborist field work before committing to massing.
    41→
    42→**Critical Root Zone (CRZ) geometry — the buildable envelope killer**
    43→- CRZ radius (ft) = DBH (in); Half CRZ = DBH ÷ 2 ft; Quarter CRZ = DBH ÷ 4 ft (ECM 3.5.2.A.1). For a 30" heritage oak: 30-ft CRZ, 15-ft Half CRZ, 7.5-ft Quarter CRZ.
    44→- Three nested rules apply simultaneously: ≥ 50% of total CRZ area preserved at natural grade with natural ground cover; cut/fill ≤ 4" in the Half CRZ; **zero cut/fill of any depth in the Quarter CRZ** (ECM 3.5.2.A.1). Failing any of the three means the tree is legally "removed" — mitigation and variance triggered whether or not the developer intends removal.
    45→- "Construction impacts" are measured at the line of excavation, not the visible face of improvements — over-excavation behind curbs, scaffolding, concrete form bracing, staging, and utility trenching all count (ECM 3.5.2.A.3). A curb shown right at the Half-CRZ line is non-compliant.
    46→- City Arborist may (discretionary, not automatic) require an enlarged CRZ at 1¼ to 1½ × standard radius for Post Oak (*Quercus stellata*), rare trees, or trees in sensitive conditions (ECM 3.5.2.A.1). Assume the larger radius for Post Oak when massing.
    47→
    48→**Heritage tree removal**
    49→- Removal prohibited without a permit; permit only issues with an approved variance under LDC § 25-8-642 (admin, < 30" stem) or § 25-8-643 (LUC + EC, ≥ 30" stem). Tree must meet one of the five § 25-8-624(A) criteria: prevents reasonable access, prevents reasonable use, imminent hazard, dead, or diseased and not restorable.
    50→- Prerequisite-variance rule (LDC § 25-8-646): applicant must have first sought and been denied every other applicable Code variance, waiver, exemption, or alternative compliance (setbacks, AEC, compatibility, etc.) before requesting heritage removal. This adds calendar time and forces concept-stage exploration of layout alternatives.
    51→- Mitigation: standard heritage rate is **300% of removed caliper inches** (ECM 3.5.4.A.1); reduced 150% rate is City-Arborist-discretionary for verified poor condition; DDI is 0% (City Arborist determination required). 19"+ protected tree (Appendix F species) is 100%; non-Appendix F 19"+ is 50%; 8–18.9" is 50%/25%.
    52→- Three mitigation forms (ECM 3.5.4.B): on-site replanting, preserved-undersized-tree inch-for-inch credit, or fee-in-lieu to the Urban Forest Replenishment Fund (UFRF) at $200/caliper inch (private) — but UFRF is only available when the City Arborist determines the site is unsuitable for planting. ROW/parkland trees route to the Planting for the Future Trust (PFTF), tracked separately.
    53→- Replacement trees: at least 75% of total caliper must be Significant Shade Provider species (Appendix F "SS" column — 39 species).
    54→
    55→**Erosion and sedimentation control (ESC)**
    56→- Every site requires an ESC plan (LDC § 25-8-181; ECM § 1.4). The Limit of Construction (LOC) is the operative boundary and must encompass all disturbance including off-site work and staging; ESC quantities (silt fence, mulch sock) are computed from actual LOC and disturbed area (ECM 1.4.4.B.3).
    57→- Phasing trigger: LOC > 25 acres requires a phased ESC plan (ECM 1.4.4.B.5.I.a). **Any site in the Barton Springs Zone requires phasing regardless of LOC size**, plus the 18-month clearing-to-revegetation cap (LDC § 25-8-184; ECM Appendix P-3).
    58→- Default plan scale is 1"=50' (Environmental Review Requirements § 3); 1"=100' only with express DSD authorization for large sites.
    59→- Cut/fill > 4 ft must be disclosed for Suburban, Water Supply Suburban, Water Supply Rural, and BSZ sites; Urban watersheds are exempt.
    60→- Silt fence: J-hooks at 100-ft intervals, individual sections ≤ 200 ft (ECM 1.4.5.G.4.A.1.1 / 1.4.5.G.4.A.1.4). Triangular Filter Dikes allowed only in sheet flow (≈ first 100 ft of flow path); concentrated flow areas need rock berms (ECM 1.4.5.H).

- Tree protection details: ECM § 3.6.1 and SSM Item No. 610
- Erosion / sediment control: LDC § 25-8-181, ECM Section 1.4 (and Appendices P-1, P-3, P-4)
- Landscape and parking lot tree requirements: LDC § 25-2-1001 et seq.; ECM Section 2
- Native tree replacement (Hill Country Roadway Corridor only): LDC § 25-2-1022 / 1025; corridor defined at LDC § 25-2-1103
- Critical Environmental Features and ERI: LDC § 25-8-1(6), § 25-8-121, § 25-8-281(C); ECM §§ 1.3.0, 1.10.3, 1.10.4
- Save Our Springs Ordinance (BSZ): LDC §§ 25-8-481, 25-8-514, 25-8-515, 25-8-516

## Regulatory pathway

| Trigger | Path | Decision body | Typical timeline |
|---|---|---|---|
| Any regulated tree (≥ 8" DBH) on site, on adjacent property with CRZ entering LOC, or in adjacent ROW | RPLS-certified tree survey + tree protection plan with site plan submittal | DSD City Arborist | Included in site plan cycle |
| Protected tree (≥ 19" DBH, any species) proposed for removal | Removal permit with documentation of one of six LDC § 25-8-624(A) criteria | City Arborist | Concurrent with site plan |
| Heritage tree (≥ 24" DBH + listed species), no stem ≥ 30" | Administrative Variance under LDC § 25-8-642; requires § 25-8-646 prerequisite-variance exhaustion (unless DDI) | DSD Director on City Arborist recommendation | ~2–4 months including pre-meeting + fiscal posting |
| Heritage tree with at least one stem ≥ 30" | Land Use Commission variance with Environmental Commission review under LDC § 25-8-643 | LUC + EC | ~4–8 months; public hearings |
| DDI (dead/diseased/imminent hazard) heritage tree | Administrative variance still required, but no fee and 0% mitigation — City Arborist letter (not private arborist alone) determines DDI | City Arborist + Director | ~1–2 months |
| LOC > 25 acres OR any LOC in Barton Springs Zone | Phased ESC plan required (ECM 1.4.4.B.5.I.a; LDC § 25-8-184); BSZ adds 18-month clearing-to-revegetation cap | DSD Environmental | Within site plan cycle |
| Site in EARZ, contains slope > 15%, contains CWQZ, or within 150 ft of mapped wetland | Environmental Resource Inventory (ERI) with three sub-reports (Hydrogeologic, Vegetation, Wastewater); 7-year validity | WPD | 2–4 months for field work + sealed report |
| Karst feature (cave, sinkhole, fault, fracture) over EARZ | 50-ft walking transect karst survey by Texas Licensed Professional Geoscientist (ECM 1.10.3); 150–300 ft buffer to catchment | WPD | Adds 1–3 months |
| Wetland CEF on or within 150 ft of site | 150-ft buffer; reducible to 50-ft avg via 1:1 in-kind on-site mitigation (ECM 1.10.4(D)(2)–(3)) | WPD | 2–4 months |
| Hill Country Roadway Corridor (within 1,000 ft of Loop 360, RM 620, RM 2222, RM 2244, or Southwest Pkwy) | Native tree replacement (LDC § 25-2-1022) + 40% natural-area set-aside (LDC § 25-2-1025) | DSD | Constrains massing from concept stage |

## Constraints to evaluate

**Tree inventory and survey**
- All trees ≥ 8" DBH must be surveyed by an RPLS within 5 years of submittal (ECM 3.3.1.A; ECM 3.3.2.A). Off-site and ROW trees count if their CRZ reaches the LOC — a 30-inch tree 28 ft beyond the boundary still triggers survey because its 30-ft CRZ enters the site (ECM 3.3.2.A.1).
- Heritage trees (≥ 24" DBH + listed species) must be marked "H"; protected trees (≥ 19" DBH any species) annotated. Multi-trunk DBH formula: largest stem + ½ each additional stem ≥ 1" (ECM 3.3.2.A.2).
- For initial diligence, satellite imagery is not a substitute — DBH cannot be inferred from canopy and field survey is the precondition to any reliable site plan. Budget RPLS + ISA-certified arborist field work before committing to massing.

**Critical Root Zone (CRZ) geometry — the buildable envelope killer**
- CRZ radius (ft) = DBH (in); Half CRZ = DBH ÷ 2 ft; Quarter CRZ = DBH ÷ 4 ft (ECM 3.5.2.A.1). For a 30" heritage oak: 30-ft CRZ, 15-ft Half CRZ, 7.5-ft Quarter CRZ.
- Three nested rules apply simultaneously: ≥ 50% of total CRZ area preserved at natural grade with natural ground cover; cut/fill ≤ 4" in the Half CRZ; **zero cut/fill of any depth in the Quarter CRZ** (ECM 3.5.2.A.1). Failing any of the three means the tree is legally "removed" — mitigation and variance triggered whether or not the developer intends removal.
- "Construction impacts" are measured at the line of excavation, not the visible face of improvements — over-excavation behind curbs, scaffolding, concrete form bracing, staging, and utility trenching all count (ECM 3.5.2.A.3). A curb shown right at the Half-CRZ line is non-compliant.
- City Arborist may (discretionary, not automatic) require an enlarged CRZ at 1¼ to 1½ × standard radius for Post Oak (*Quercus stellata*), rare trees, or trees in sensitive conditions (ECM 3.5.2.A.1). Assume the larger radius for Post Oak when massing.

**Heritage tree removal**
- Removal prohibited without a permit; permit only issues with an approved variance under LDC § 25-8-642 (admin, < 30" stem) or § 25-8-643 (LUC + EC, ≥ 30" stem). Tree must meet one of the five § 25-8-624(A) criteria: prevents reasonable access, prevents reasonable use, imminent hazard, dead, or diseased and not restorable.
- Prerequisite-variance rule (LDC § 25-8-646): applicant must have first sought and been denied every other applicable Code variance, waiver, exemption, or alternative compliance (setbacks, AEC, compatibility, etc.) before requesting heritage removal. This adds calendar time and forces concept-stage exploration of layout alternatives.
- Mitigation: standard heritage rate is **300% of removed caliper inches** (ECM 3.5.4.A.1); reduced 150% rate is City-Arborist-discretionary for verified poor condition; DDI is 0% (City Arborist determination required). 19"+ protected tree (Appendix F species) is 100%; non-Appendix F 19"+ is 50%; 8–18.9" is 50%/25%.
- Three mitigation forms (ECM 3.5.4.B): on-site replanting, preserved-undersized-tree inch-for-inch credit, or fee-in-lieu to the Urban Forest Replenishment Fund (UFRF) at $200/caliper inch (private) — but UFRF is only available when the City Arborist determines the site is unsuitable for planting. ROW/parkland trees route to the Planting for the Future Trust (PFTF), tracked separately.
- Replacement trees: at least 75% of total caliper must be Significant Shade Provider species (Appendix F "SS" column — 39 species).

**Erosion and sedimentation control (ESC)**
- Every site requires an ESC plan (LDC § 25-8-181; ECM § 1.4). The Limit of Construction (LOC) is the operative boundary and must encompass all disturbance including off-site work and staging; ESC quantities (silt fence, mulch sock) are computed from actual LOC and disturbed area (ECM 1.4.4.B.3).
- Phasing trigger: LOC > 25 acres requires a phased ESC plan (ECM 1.4.4.B.5.I.a). **Any site in the Barton Springs Zone requires phasing regardless of LOC size**, plus the 18-month clearing-to-revegetation cap (LDC § 25-8-184; ECM Appendix P-3).
- Default plan scale is 1"=50' (Environmental Review Requirements § 3); 1"=100' only with express DSD authorization for large sites.
- Cut/fill > 4 ft must be disclosed for Suburban, Water Supply Suburban, Water Supply Rural, and BSZ sites; Urban watersheds are exempt.
- Silt fence: J-hooks at 100-ft intervals, individual sections ≤ 200 ft (ECM 1.4.5.G.4.A.1.1 / 1.4.5.G.4.A.1.4). Triangular Filter Dikes allowed only in sheet flow (≈ first 100 ft of flow path); concentrated flow areas need rock berms (ECM 1.4.5.H).

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/wnavey/noetic/claude-plugins/plugins/noetic-tools/skills/generate-pdf

# Generate Noetic-Branded PDFs

## Package location

```
claude-plugins/plugins/noetic-tools/noetic-pdf/
```

All imports come from `./src/index` (relative) or the local package.

## Quick start

1. Write a `.tsx` file that default-exports a React element
2. Render it: `npx tsx claude-plugins/plugins/noetic-tools/noetic-pdf/src/render-cli.tsx <input.tsx> <output.pdf>`

The render CLI must be run from the `noetic-pdf/` directory (for dependency resolution), or use an absolute path to `render-cli.tsx` with the working directory set to `noetic-pdf/`.

## Page model

Every PDF follows this shape:

1. **One `<CoverPage>`** — always the first page. Large serif title, optional subtitle and date, light topographic contour pattern. There should be exactly one per document.
2. **Optional `<ContentsPage>`** — the second page when you have metadata + a table of contents to present. Skip it for short reports.
3. **One or more `<NoeticPage>`** — content pages with the logo header and page footer.

```tsx
import {
  NoeticDocument,
  CoverPage,
  ContentsPage,
  NoeticPage,
} from './src/index';

export default (
  <NoeticDocument title="Report Title">
    <CoverPage
      title="Report Title"
      subtitle="Property — Address"
      date="May 18, 2026"
    />
    <ContentsPage
      title="Report Title"
      metadata={[{ label: 'Property', value: '...' }]}
      tocItems={['Section 1', 'Section 2']}
    />
    <NoeticPage>
      {/* content */}
    </NoeticPage>
  </NoeticDocument>
);
```

### Contour background

The `<CoverPage>` always renders a light topographic contour pattern as its background. By default it generates a **fresh random seed on every render**, so each PDF you produce has its own unique pattern.

- Pin a seed for reproducible output (golden tests, regenerating an unchanged report): `contour={{ seed: 42 }}`
- Tune density / opacity: `contour={{ levels: 28, strokeOpacity: 0.15 }}`
- Disable entirely (rare): `contour={false}`

`ContentsPage` defaults to **no contour** (it's a metadata/TOC page that reads better clean), but accepts the same `contour` prop if you want one. `NoeticPage` does not support contours — content pages stay clean.

## Component catalog

| Component | Purpose | Key props |
|-----------|---------|-----------|
| `SectionHeading` | Numbered teal heading with rule | `number`, `children` (string) |
| `SubHeading` | Bold sub-section heading | `children`, `color` ('black'\|'teal'), `rule` |
| `SeverityBadge` | Constraint status callout | `level` ('none'\|'moderate'\|'significant'\|'data-gap'\|'note'), `children` (detail text) |
| `Callout` | Left-bordered insight/action box | `variant` ('insight'\|'action'\|'correction'\|'data-gap'\|'neutral'), `label`, `children` |
| `Table` | Data table with dark or light header | `columns`, `rows`, `headerStyle`, `alternateRows` |
| `KeyValue` | Label/value metadata pairs | `items` (array of {label, value}), `layout` ('stacked'\|'inline') |
| `Badge` | Small colored pill | `variant` ('green'\|'amber'\|'red'\|'gray'\|'teal'\|'blue'), `children` |
| `MarkdownBody` | Render markdown string as PDF | `markdown` (string) |
| `StackedBar` | Proportional bar chart | `segments` (array of {count, color}) |
| `Divider` | Horizontal rule | `spacing` (number) |
| `TOC` | Table of contents box | `items` (string[]), `title` |
| `ContourBackground` | Light topographic contour pattern (edge-to-edge SVG). Baked into `CoverPage` by default with a random seed; opt-in on `ContentsPage`. Use directly only on custom pages. | `seed`, `levels`, `scale`, `octaves`, `ridge`, `warp`, `strokeOpacity`, `strokeWidth`, `strokeColor` |

Read [components.md](references/components.md) for full API docs and examples.

## Theme

Import `colors`, `fonts`, `shared` from `./src/theme` for consistent styling when building custom layouts:

- `colors.teal700` — section headings, accents
- `colors.slate800` — table headers
- `colors.green600/amber600/red600` — severity dots
- `fonts.sansBold` — emphasis
- `shared.bold/italic` — inline text styles

Read [theme.md](references/theme.md) for the full palette.

## Custom components

Agents can create any layout using `View`, `Text`, `StyleSheet` from `@react-pdf/renderer` alongside the theme. The pre-built components cover ~80% of report needs — create custom components for novel visualizations or domain-specific layouts.

## Working example

See `noetic-pdf/src/examples/sir-example.tsx` for a complete Site Intelligence Report demonstrating all major components. Render it with:

```bash
cd claude-plugins/plugins/noetic-tools/noetic-pdf
npx tsx src/render-cli.tsx src/examples/sir-example.tsx /tmp/example.pdf
```

## react-pdf gotchas

- No CSS grid or flexbox `gap` — use `marginBottom`/`marginRight` on children
- `wrap={false}` on a View keeps it on one page (use for headings, callout boxes)
- Text styles only work on `<Text>` elements, not `<View>`
- Nesting `<Text>` inside `<Text>` works for inline formatting (bold words in a paragraph)
- Use `flex` ratios, not percentage `flexBasis`, for proportional widths
- `fixed` prop on a View makes it repeat on every page (used by logo header/footer)
- Images need `@react-pdf/renderer`'s `<Image>` component, not HTML img

        <SubHeading>Property Profile</SubHeading>
        <Table
          columns={[
            { header: 'Attribute', width: 160 },
            { header: 'Value', flex: 1 },
            { header: 'Source', width: 80 },
          ]}
          rows={[
            { Attribute: 'Jurisdiction', Value: 'Austin Full-Purpose', Source: '[COA GIS]' },
            { Attribute: 'Council District', Value: '9', Source: '[COA GIS]' },
            { Attribute: 'Watershed', Value: 'West Bouldin Creek (Urban)', Source: '[COA GIS]' },
            { Attribute: 'Core Transit Corridor', Value: 'S Lamar Blvd', Source: '[COA GIS]' },
            { Attribute: 'Creek Buffers', Value: 'None', Source: '[COA GIS]' },
            { Attribute: 'Downtown Coordination Zone', Value: 'South Sector', Source: '[COA GIS]' },
          ]}
        />

        <Callout variant="insight" label="Where our system adds value:">
          Automated confirmation that no conflicting overlays (ETOD, TOD, Downtown, West Campus) apply, verified across all 168 GIS layers. [COA GIS]
        </Callout>
      </NoeticPage>

      {/* ── Negotiated Agreements section ──────────────── */}
      <NoeticPage>
        <SectionHeading number={6}>Negotiated Agreements with Neighbors</SectionHeading>
        <SeverityBadge level="significant">25-year covenant restricts western boundary through 2050</SeverityBadge>

        <SubHeading>1709B Kinney Ave -- Leurig Neighbor Agreement</SubHeading>
        <KeyValue
          items={[
            { label: 'Instruments', value: '2025109628 (original) / 2025111338 (re-recorded October 6, 2025)' },
            { label: 'Effective Date', value: 'September 25, 2025' },
            { label: 'Parties', value: 'SL 1700 South Lamar, L.P. ("Stonelake") and Sharlene Leurig' },
          ]}
        />

        <Table
          columns={[
            { header: 'Provision', width: 120 },
            { header: 'Requirement', flex: 1 },
          ]}
          rows={[
            { Provision: 'Fence', Requirement: 'Min 8 ft height; cedar slat with steel posts; double-sided; must be constructed before final CO for any new building on Tract 2' },
            { Provision: '75-ft building setback', Requirement: 'Along western boundary of Tract 2 (per Exhibit E)' },
            { Provision: 'Trash/waste', Requirement: 'All trash rooms internal; no loading or exterior waste zones facing/abutting western setback' },
          ]}
        />

        <MarkdownBody markdown="**Term: 25 years from September 25, 2025 (expires September 25, 2050)**, unless modified/terminated by agreement of both parties. Runs with the land -- binding on successors and assigns. [County Clerk]" />

        <Callout variant="correction" label="Correction vs. client intake:">
          The intake references SF-5 triggering compatibility. GIS confirms SF-3, not SF-5. Both trigger identical compatibility standards under LDC 25-2-1063 et seq., so the regulatory impact is the same, but the zoning designation is more precisely SF-3. [COA GIS]
        </Callout>

        <Callout variant="data-gap" label="DATA GAP:">
          Heritage and protected trees are not tracked in the COA GIS layers queried (168 layers). Tree locations, health status, and Critical Root Zone calculations require field verification. Recommend updated arborist assessment. [COA GIS -- confirmed not available]
        </Callout>
      </NoeticPage>
    </NoeticDocument>
  );
}

   283→## KeyValue

   326→## MarkdownBody

   333→
   334→- Coverage: 99.5% of parcel

   339→
   340→| Prop | Type | Description |
   341→|------|------|-------------|

   344→---

   346→## StackedBar

   358→
   359→| Prop | Type | Description |
   360→|------|------|-------------|
   361→| `segments` | `{ count: number, color: string }[]` | Bar segments (zero-count segments are skipped) |
   362→
   363→---
   364→
   365→## Divider
   366→
   367→Simple horizontal rule for separating content sections.

   369→```tsx
   370→<Divider />

   378→---
   379→
   380→## TOC
   381→
   382→Bordered table of contents box. Usually used within CoverPage but can be placed independently.

   384→```tsx

   389→| Prop | Type | Default | Description |

   391→| `items` | string[] | required | List entries |

# Component API Reference

All components are imported from `noetic-pdf/src/index`.

---

## NoeticDocument

Top-level wrapper. Must be the outermost element.

```tsx
<NoeticDocument title="Site Intelligence Report" author="Noetic">
  {/* <CoverPage /> + optional <ContentsPage /> + one or more <NoeticPage /> */}
</NoeticDocument>
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `title` | string | required | PDF document title (metadata) |
| `author` | string | `'Noetic'` | PDF author metadata |
| `children` | ReactNode | required | Page elements |

---

## NoeticPage

Content page with logo header and page-number footer.

```tsx
<NoeticPage footerLabel="Noetic — Confidential">
  {/* section content */}
</NoeticPage>
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `children` | ReactNode | required | Page content |
| `footerLabel` | string | `'Noetic — Confidential'` | Left footer text |

---

## CoverPage

The first page of every report. Large serif title, optional subtitle and date, light topographic contour background ON by default with a random seed (each render unique). Every PDF should have exactly one of these.

```tsx
<CoverPage
  title="Concept Plan Review"
  subtitle="AutoZone Store #11094 — 9101 Cameron Rd, Austin, TX"
  date="May 18, 2026"
/>

// Pin a seed for reproducible renders:
<CoverPage title="..." contour={{ seed: 42 }} />

// Disable contour (rare):
<CoverPage title="..." contour={false} />
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `title` | string | required | Large serif report title |
| `subtitle` | string | — | Bold subtitle (shown above date in lower-left) |
| `date` | string | — | Date string (lower-left) |
| `footerLabel` | string | `'Noetic — Confidential'` | Footer text |
| `contour` | boolean \| ContourBackgroundProps | `true` | Topographic contour background. Random seed by default (unique every render). Pass `false` to disable; pass an object to tune. |

---

## ContentsPage

Optional second page: project metadata + table of contents. Use when the report needs a structured front matter; skip for short reports.

```tsx
<ContentsPage
  title="Site Intelligence Report"
  metadata={[
    { label: 'Property', value: '1700 S Lamar Blvd, Austin, TX 78704' },
    { label: 'Report Date', value: '2026-05-06' },
    { label: 'Report ID', value: 'SIR-2026-0506-ATX-001' },
    { label: 'Status', value: 'DRAFT -- Pending PE Review' },
    { label: 'Prepared by', value: 'Noetic' },
  ]}
  tocItems={['Site Information', 'TCAD', 'Zoning']}
>
  {/* Optional: first section can start on this page */}
  <SectionHeading number={1}>Site Information</SectionHeading>
</ContentsPage>
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `title` | string | required | Smaller serif heading at top of the page |
| `metadata` | KVPair[] | — | Key-value pairs shown below the title |
| `tocItems` | string[] | — | Table of contents entries |
| `footerLabel` | string | `'Noetic — Confidential'` | Footer text |
| `contour` | boolean \| ContourBackgroundProps | `false` | Contour background. Off by default — this page reads better clean. Pass `true` or an object to enable. |
| `children` | ReactNode | — | Additional content on the page |

---

## ContourBackground

Light topographic contour pattern, positioned absolutely to cover a full LETTER page edge-to-edge. `CoverPage` renders this automatically. Use this component directly only on custom pages.

```tsx
// On a custom Page (must be the first child so subsequent content draws over it):
<Page size="LETTER">
  <ContourBackground />        {/* random seed, unique every render */}
  <LogoHeader />
  {/* ...your content... */}
</Page>

// Pin a seed for reproducible renders:
<ContourBackground seed={42} />

// Tune density / opacity:
<ContourBackground levels={28} strokeOpacity={0.15} />
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `seed` | number | _random_ | Noise seed. **Defaults to a fresh random integer on every render**, so each PDF gets a unique pattern. Pass a fixed number for reproducible output (golden tests, deterministic exports). |
| `levels` | number | `22` | Number of contour bands. Higher = denser lines. |
| `scale` | number | `8` | Noise scale. Larger = broader, more sweeping features. |
| `octaves` | number | `5` | FBM octaves. More = finer detail. |
| `ridge` | number | `0.7` | 0 = soft hills, 1 = sharp ridges. |
| `warp` | number | `0.8` | Domain warp strength. 0 disables warp. |
| `strokeOpacity` | number | `0.11` | Line opacity (0–1). |
| `strokeWidth` | number | `0.5` | Line width in pt. Every 5th index line is 2× this. |
| `strokeColor` | string | `'#000000'` | Stroke color (hex). |

Note: must be the FIRST child of its `<Page>` so subsequent content draws on top. Sized to LETTER (612×792 pt) — for other page sizes, pass custom `virtualWidth`/`virtualHeight` to match the page aspect ratio.

---

## SectionHeading

Numbered teal heading with underline rule. Used for major report sections.

```tsx
<SectionHeading number={4}>Zoning</SectionHeading>
<SectionHeading>Appendix</SectionHeading>  {/* no number */}
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `number` | number | — | Section number prefix |
| `children` | string | required | Heading text |

---

## SubHeading

Bold sub-section heading. Can be black (default) or teal, with optional underline.

```tsx
<SubHeading>Ownership</SubHeading>
<SubHeading color="teal">COA FloodPro</SubHeading>

```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `children` | string | required | Heading text |
| `color` | `'black'` \| `'teal'` | `'black'` | Text color |
| `rule` | boolean | `false` | Show underline rule |

---

## SeverityBadge

Colored constraint/status callout bar with icon. The signature SIR element.

```tsx
<SeverityBadge level="none" />
<SeverityBadge level="moderate">DB90 limited to Tract 1 only</SeverityBadge>
<SeverityBadge level="significant">25-year covenant through 2050</SeverityBadge>
<SeverityBadge level="data-gap">Utility infrastructure not assessed</SeverityBadge>
<SeverityBadge level="note">Site plan filed today</SeverityBadge>
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `level` | `'none'` \| `'moderate'` \| `'significant'` \| `'data-gap'` \| `'note'` | required | Severity level |
| `children` | string | — | Detail text after " -- " separator |

Levels and their colors:
- **none**: Green — no constraint
- **moderate**: Amber — moderate constraint
- **significant**: Red — significant constraint
- **data-gap**: Gray with `?` icon — missing data
- **note**: Amber — informational note

---

## Callout

Left-bordered box for insights, actions, corrections, and data gaps.

```tsx
<Callout variant="insight" label="Where our system adds value:">
  Automated confirmation across 168 GIS layers.
</Callout>

<Callout variant="action" label="Action required:">
  Initiate early PARD coordination.
</Callout>

<Callout variant="correction" label="Correction vs. client intake:">
  GIS confirms SF-3, not SF-5.
</Callout>

<Callout variant="data-gap" label="DATA GAP:">
  Heritage trees not tracked in GIS layers.
</Callout>

<Callout variant="neutral">
  General informational note.
</Callout>
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `variant` | `'insight'` \| `'action'` \| `'correction'` \| `'data-gap'` \| `'neutral'` | required | Visual style |
| `label` | string | — | Bold prefix text |
| `children` | ReactNode | required | Body content (string or JSX) |

Variant colors:
- **insight**: Teal border, light green bg
- **action**: Red border, light red bg
- **correction**: Amber border, light yellow bg
- **data-gap**: Gray border, light gray bg
- **neutral**: Light gray border, very light gray bg

---

## Table

```tsx
<Table
  columns={[

    { header: 'Value', flex: 1 },
    { header: 'Source', width: 80 },
  ]}
  rows={[
    { Attribute: 'Jurisdiction', Value: 'Austin Full-Purpose', Source: '[COA GIS]' },
    { Attribute: 'Council District', Value: '9', Source: '[COA GIS]' },
  ]}
  headerStyle="dark"
  alternateRows
/>
```

**Column definition:**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `header` | string | required | Column header text (also used as row key) |
| `width` | number | — | Fixed width in pts |
| `flex` | number | — | Flex ratio (default 1 if no width) |
| `align` | `'left'` \| `'center'` \| `'right'` | `'left'` | Text alignment |
| `bold` | boolean | — | Bold all cells in column |
| `render` | function | — | Custom cell renderer: `(value, row, index) => ReactNode` |

**Table props:**

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `columns` | Column[] | required | Column definitions |
| `rows` | Record<string, string>[] | required | Row data keyed by column header |
| `headerStyle` | `'dark'` \| `'light'` | `'dark'` | Header background style |
| `alternateRows` | boolean | `true` | Alternate row shading |
| `fontSize` | number | — | Override cell font size |

**Row data format**: Each row is an object where keys match column `header` values.

---

## KeyValue

Label/value metadata pairs. Two layouts: stacked (one per line) or inline (flowing).

```tsx
{/* Stacked: one pair per line */}
<KeyValue items={[
  { label: 'Instruments', value: '2025109628 (original)' },
  { label: 'Effective Date', value: 'September 25, 2025' },
]} />

{/* Inline: flowing text */}
<KeyValue layout="inline" items={[
  { label: 'Property Location', value: '1700 S Lamar Blvd' },
  { label: 'Total Site Area', value: '5.2127 acres' },
]} />
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `items` | `{ label: string, value: string }[]` | required | Key-value pairs |
| `layout` | `'stacked'` \| `'inline'` | `'stacked'` | Layout mode |

---

## Badge

Small colored pill/chip for inline status indicators.

```tsx
<Badge variant="green">PASS</Badge>
<Badge variant="red">FAIL</Badge>
<Badge variant="amber">WARN</Badge>
<Badge>DEFAULT</Badge>
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `variant` | `'green'` \| `'amber'` \| `'red'` \| `'gray'` \| `'teal'` \| `'blue'` | `'gray'` | Color scheme |
| `children` | string | required | Badge text |

---

## MarkdownBody

Renders a markdown string as formatted PDF content. Supports headings (h1-h6), paragraphs, bold, italic, code, links, bullet lists, ordered lists, and horizontal rules.

```tsx
<MarkdownBody markdown={`
**Tract 1 -- CS-V-DB90** (General Commercial Services)

- Coverage: 99.5% of parcel
- DB90 entitles up to **90 ft height**
- Maximum impervious cover: 95% per CS-V base
`} />
```

| Prop | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `markdown` | string | Markdown content to render |

---

## StackedBar

Horizontal proportional bar chart with rounded ends.

```tsx
<StackedBar segments={[
  { count: 15, color: colors.green600 },
  { count: 3, color: colors.red600 },
  { count: 2, color: colors.amber600 },
  { count: 1, color: colors.gray500 },
]} />
```

| Prop | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `segments` | `{ count: number, color: string }[]` | Bar segments (zero-count segments are skipped) |

---

## Divider

Simple horizontal rule for separating content sections.

```tsx
<Divider />
<Divider spacing={24} />
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `spacing` | number | 16 | Top and bottom margin |

---

## TOC

Bordered table of contents box. Usually used within CoverPage but can be placed independently.

```tsx
<TOC items={['Site Information', 'TCAD', 'Zoning']} />
<TOC title="Sections Covered" items={['...']} />
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `items` | string[] | required | List entries |
| `title` | string | `'Table of Contents'` | Box title |
